articleTitle: Interfacial reliability analysis and structural optimization of System-in-Package modules
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The System-in-Package (SiP) module is a significant component for the next generation terminal product and system in accordance with the electronics packaging driven demands of miniaturization and multi-functionality. Nevertheless, the SiP technology also faces multiple challenges to satisfy the requirements of increased performance, smaller factor, and lower power. The interfacial reliability of SiP module is one crucial issue during the entire life-cycle of devices, especially the packaging and reflows soldering process. The interfacial delamination is driven due to the mismatch of the material properties, such as the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and Young’s modulus, even the crack propagation will be sped up due to the vapor and oxygen permeation. In this paper, the mechanical-thermal loads are applied to shed light on the interface reliability of laminated SiP structures. And the interfacial behaviors are systematically investigated using hybrid analytical method and finite element model, where the interfacial stresses between different components are calculated, the maximum von Mises stress of solder joints is obtained, and the warpage deformation of PCB-substrate is also included. Then the machine learning (ML) method is further applied to the structural optimization of SiP modules based on above interfacial reliability analysis, and the relationships between the properties of SiP modules and the thermal-mechanical behaviors are obtained. The effect of material properties and geometry of packaging components on the thermal-mechanical behavior are investigated. The interfacial stress increases with the increasing of CTE and Young’s modulus of EMC, and the maximum warpage deformation also increase with the increasing of material properties of EMC, but it decreases with the increasing of EMC thickness. The computational efficiency and accuracy of the proposed machine learning-based model are validated, and the application of ML model, in particular, is considered as a crucial useful technology to predict the thermal cycling response of laminated SiP structures and provide a helpful guidance for the geometry and material selection (structural optimization) of packaging design.

articleTitle: The structural optimization of heterogeneous integration system in display based on thermal-mechanical behaviors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The display module plays an important role in the future terminal device. The trend of "more than display" means that the multi-function units and chips (e.g., display units, storage units, sensing units, communication units, even computing units) will be integrated into the display module. The heterogeneous integration system in display (HISID) is regarded as a promising candidate and potential architecture for higher density and higher performance products, and it is proposed with the advantages of intelligence, light-weight, high bandwidth, ultra-low latency, mobility. Nevertheless, the mismatches of coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) and elastic modulus among functional components, solders, and substrate will result in the thermal reliability issues during the entire life cycle of devices. In this work, the hybrid analytical and FEM thermal shock simulation is applied to evaluate the thermal reliability of laminated HISID structures. Firstly, an effective analytical method is developed to investigate the thermal behavior of HISID models, where the inner stress along the thickness or the interfacial stress are calculated, and the warpage deformation is described with bending curvature. Then, the three-dimensional finite element HISID model is established to further investigate the thermal reliability design, where the inner stress and interfacial stress due to temperature change are obtained, and the warpage deformation from original plane are considered. Moreover, the optimal laminated HISID model is then obtained by adjusting the layer thickness and material properties. The glass-based substrate is investigated and considered as a crucial component to demonstrate the better thermal-mechanical behavior compared with traditional FR4-based substrate. The detail reduction of out-of-plane deformation (warpage) for glass-substrate is 42.18%, and the max mises stress reduction of solder bump is 32.30%. The stress distribution of solder is influenced by the thickness of silica gel layer and copper layer, the size and space of BGA-solders, and etc. The von Mises stress decreases with increasing of PCB-substrate thickness and decreasing of silica gel thickness; and the effect of BGA-solder radius on stress distribution is more obvious. Thus, the material and geometry modification of laminated HISID model is an effective way for the structural optimization based on the analytical method and finite element method.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a Wafer-level Integration for System-on-Wafer Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As one of the most important advanced packaging technologies, heterogeneous integration is desired to help advanced node to cover the integrated systems’ memory wall to further continue Moore’s law. With continuous growing demands for high performance computing, multi-chip wafer level integration is developed for artificial intelligence. By shrinking the interconnection distance and enlarging the integration scale, System-on-Wafer (SoW) is a promising architecture for improving the integration system performance. In this paper, a wafer level integration with historically large scale of over 200 dies and 1 million bumps are assembled on a 12-inch Si wafer substrate for SoW process demonstration. A 100% yield of flip chip (FC) bonding and good warpage control are demonstrated. Besides, fine FC space and high integration density are also acquired. This work proposes a novel SoW architecture and process flow solution for wafer-level integration product in the post Moore’s law era.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis between Warpage and Metal Thermal Interface Materials Thermo-mechanical Reliability of Large size FCBGA
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Taking the structural optimization process of a large size packages as an example, we summarized the results obtained by the response surface methodology(RSM). We found it is not accurate that a smaller warpage the substrate is, a higher reliability thermal interface materials(TIM) could be endowed with. Factors that are meaningful for reducing warpage may not necessarily lead to an improvement in the reliability of metal TIM. The difference in warpage between the lid side and the substrate side during temperature changes is more meaningful, the smaller this warpage is controlled, the more beneficial it was to the metal TIM reliability. On the other hand, we have also compared multiple sizes of packages, and this conclusion is still applicable for packages of different sizes and structures.

articleTitle: Optimization and Analysis of Constant Acceleration Test Fixture for Large Size Ceramic Shell
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The constant acceleration test is widely used in product assessment, screening, and reliability testing of electronic devices. Compared with mechanical shock and random vibration tests, constant acceleration tests can more effectively detect defects in product structural strength and other problems. This article analyzes the failure phenomena of three types of large-sized ceramic shells, namely DIP40, CQFP352, and PGA104 ceramic shells, such as ceramic body fracture and detachment of sealing light window cover plate, which occurred during the constant acceleration test. By using finite element software to conduct three-dimensional modeling and simulation analysis on the reasons for the failure of the above three ceramic shell constant acceleration tests, and verifying the applicability of the optimized constant acceleration test fixture, combined with constant acceleration experimental verification, the feasibility of the optimized constant acceleration test fixture has been further demonstrated, improving the product’s assessment pass rate, and providing test methods for similar products.

articleTitle: In situ nondestructive study interface aging mechanism of polymeric materials/nanocomposites based on dual-beam Raman spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Aging is a key factor affecting the service life of polymer/nanocomposites, and the research on the aging mechanism of the interface (nanoscale transition region) between polymers and nanomaterials is crucial and full of challenges. On the one hand, it is easy to change the original microscopic characteristics of the interface by cutting off the polymer/nanocomposite material to expose the interface. On the other hand, in situ spectroscopy is difficult to achieve nanoscale spatial resolution and is easily interfered with by the signal of the polymer matrix outside the interface. This project aims at these problems, by endowing polymer/nanocomposite materials with surface plasmon properties, using lasers that resonate with nanofiller plasmons to obtain surface-enhanced Raman signals of molecules at the interface (nano-region enhancement); at the same time, another wavelength laser of the dual-beam system is used to collect the intrinsic Raman signal of the polymer matrix outside the interface, so as to realize the precise characterization of the microscopic features of the interface and the effective distinction from the molecules outside the interface. In addition, multi-dimensional data analysis was performed on Raman spectra, and Raman characteristic peaks were used to analyze chemical bond changes, while background fluorescence signals were used to evaluate the excited state of polymers, further revealing the aging mechanism at the polymer/nanocomposite interface. This project can provide new methods and ideas for in situ nondestructive research on the aging mechanism of polymer/nanocomposite.

articleTitle: Research on Board Level Reliability of Mounted Ceramic Package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Board level reliability of surface mounted ceramic packages was studied based on structural design of ceramic packages. The board level reliability of ceramic packages with different external dimensions and lead support heights was simulated under same temperature cycling conditions. A board level temperature cycling test ranges from -65 ° C to 150 ° C was conducted on selected samples. After every 100 cycles, the appearance and resistance of the samples were inspected until board level failure. This article investigated the impact of different external dimensions and lead support heights on board level failure, summarized board level reliability of surface mounted ceramic package, provided guidance for the board level reliability design of similar packages in the future, and formed relevant design specifications.

articleTitle: Toward next generation interconnection technology: Ag/Cu sinter joining and their innovative application
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of high-power electronic devices, there is an increasing demand for lead-free technology with high thermal conductivity and thermal reliability. Wide band gap semiconductors have entered the market, and there is growing interest in interconnection technologies for these devices that can operate at temperatures above 200 °C. Sinter joining technology has emerged as a promising solution due to its exceptional thermal and electrical conductivity and thermal reliability. However, there are advantages and disadvantages to both Ag sinter joining and Cu sinter joining, along with their potential applications and scientific challenges that need to be addressed to realize their practical use. Ag sinter joining is a novel interconnection process that has shown unique benefits in SiC device packages. Ag particles can be sintered at low temperatures, even below 200°C, and can operate over 250°C. Sintered Ag layers exhibit high electric and thermal conductivity, high melting points, and strong bonding. Ag sintering can also be applied to various metallization such as Ag, Al, and Au, making it a promising process. However, the use of Ag as a die-attach material still faces challenges such as high cost, poor chemical migration properties, and corrosion. Cu sinter joining provides a cost-effective alternative with similar thermal and electrical conductivity as Ag, and higher resistance to chemical/gas corrosion, making it applicable in a wider range. Yet, sintering Cu demands serious conditions due to its low self-diffusion coefficient and intrinsic oxidation tendency, requiring the application of high pressure, temperature or reductive protecting gas. Cu particle sinter joining technology is highly regarded for its cost-performance ratio in interconnecting power devices. However, several issues must be resolved to make Cu sinter joining a practical alternative.This paper highlights the need for further research and development to overcome the challenges associated with each technology and realize their practical application in high-power electronic devices. Firstly, some Ag sinter joining cases were proposed to discuss the sinter behavior, and the recently emerged novel application of sinter process, such as large area bonding for substrate attachment. Secondly, the mechanism of Cu sinter joining was discussed, and efforts to realize Cu sinter joint at mild sintering conditions were released. Finally, the newest development in each technology was suggested, and the scientific challenges to fill in these gaps are presented as well.

articleTitle: Prediction of Packaging Induced-Warpage for a 3D Stacked Package with a Cure-dependent Viscoelastic Model for EMC
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electronic devices today are continuously evolving towards higher density and enhanced functionality, placing greater demands on electronic packaging technology. As a commonly used encapsulation material, EMC has a significant impact on package warpage. Due to its nature as a thermosetting resin, considering the viscoelastic behavior of EMC during simulation using ANSYS can provide more accurate results compared to using elastic materials. In this article, the research object is the three-dimensional stacked packaging structure. In its curing process, the generalized Maxwell model is used as the constitutive model to describe the thermo-mechanical properties of the encapsulating material, and the Prony series is used to represent its transient part. Due to the change in the storage modulus and Tg point of the EMC after high- temperature storage, which affects the warpage of the package, DMA equipment is used to measure the viscoelastic parameters of the epoxy molding compound before and after high- temperature storage and process the data. Simulation software is used to investigate the effect of changes in EMC viscoelastic parameters under high-temperature storage on package reliability, and the impact of stress relaxation of the epoxy molding compound on warpage is studied using ANSYS Mechanical finite element software. The boundary conditions material parameters and temperature curves, and a single-factor method are used to consider the effect of EMC thickness, curing time, and temperature on the stress distribution of the chip and the warpage of the package. The response surface method is used to process the warpage values and obtain the optimal parameter combination. The results show that the change in EMC material properties after high-temperature storage has a significant impact on the stress of the package, and appropriate process temperature curves and structural parameter combinations can reduce the warpage of the chip.

articleTitle: Research on characteristics of a high sensitivity magnetic sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a common sensor, Magnetic sensor is widely used in power generation, automotive electronics, rail transit and power field. In this paper, we describes the principle and technological process of the magnetic sensor, and compares the advantages of the hall sensor [1] [2] [3] and the magnetic sensor [4] [5] [6]. Then we tests the developed magnetic sensor sample on the basis of analyzing the demand for magnetic sensor in the power field. Finally, we conducted a preliminary test on the performance of the sensor and discuss the optimization of the sensor.

articleTitle: Silver@Expanded Microspheres/Silicone Conductive Composites with Ultra-low Compression Stress for Electromagnetic Interference Shielding in Electronic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicone conductive composites are the ideal materials for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding in electronic packages because of their excellent sealing properties, chemical inertness, and mechanical durability. Notably, chips and other miniature electronic components with limited pressure-bearing capacity often require soft conductive composites with low compressive stress and high electromagnetic shielding performance. However, conventional silicone conductive composites still face significant challenges in balancing compressibility and electromagnetic shielding performance as the conductive filler content increases. Here, a composite with ultra-low compression stress and excellent EMI shielding properties was successfully prepared by incorporating silver-plated expanded microspheres (Ag@EM) into a silicone substrate, followed by a heat curing process. In particular, the lightweight Ag@EM conductive filler possess low density (0.14 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). Compared to conventional polymer conductive composites filled with hard fillers (Ag@hollow glass microspheres), the Ag@EM/silicone composites with Ag@EM loading of 15.5 wt% show ultra-low compression stress of only 0.22 MPa at 50% of compressive strain and high EMI SE of 60 dB at thickness of 1 mm. Significantly, the Ag@EM/silicone composites has a maximum shielding effectiveness of 71 dB at the edge in near-field (NF) shielding tests due to its low compressive stress, good sealing and excellent shielding properties. This work suggests that the Ag@EM/silicone composites with ultra-low compression stress, outstanding EMI and NF shielding performance, verifying the potential of the Ag@EM/silicone composites for electronic devices.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the influence of the reliability application of a thermal insulation adhesive on the reliability of solder joints
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Based on the reliability application requirements of space borne products for thermal insulation adhesives, the impact evaluation of two-component thermal insulation adhesives on the reliability of BGA solder joints was carried out. Through the design and manufacture of the typical BGA daisy chain network structure test piece of the satellite terminal machine, and the filling of thermal insulation adhesive, carry out the identification level environmental and reliability tests of the daisy chain test piece such as temperature cycle, sinusoidal vibration, random vibration and thermal vacuum, monitor the test process, and analyze the resistance data of the daisy chain network structure circuit. The resistance of the environmental test process is not increased, interrupted, and there is no solder joint failure and fracture; The daisy chain test piece has no defects introduced in the process of filling the thermal insulation adhesive. The thermal insulation adhesive has no effect on the solder joint of the daisy chain structure. It has the ability to withstand the environmental stress of the space-borne product, meet the requirements of heat dissipation and high load resistance of the space-borne product, and achieve reliable application.

articleTitle: Study on Reliability of Hard-Lap Solder Joints of Microwave RF Coaxial Connectors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Coaxial connectors are widely used in microwave and radio frequency components due to their advantages such as low standing wave and low signal loss. However, the high stress problem of their hardwired solder joints seriously jeopardizes the reliability of connectors in service at long-term alternating temperatures. In this paper, the thermal cycling reliability of the hard-lap solder joint between the inner conductor of the microwave RF coaxial connector and the micro-strip pad has been discussed by combining finite element simulation and reliability testing. The results show that the maximum stress in the solder joint is located at the wetting angle formed between the solder and the root of the copper pillar. The overlap shape of the solder joint significantly affects the stress amplitude and distribution of the solder joint, and the optimal conductor diameter is 1.3 mm. The hard lap solder joint using an inner conductor with a diameter of 1.3 mm do not exhibit solder joint cracking under 1000 thermal cycles, while the hard-lap solder joint using an inner conductor with a diameter of 0.38 mm begin to exhibit cracking at the connecting corner of the solder joint on the copper column side after 500 thermal cycles, and completely fractured at the interface between the nickel layer and (Au<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> by 1000 thermal cycles. Through this study, the influence of the inner conductor diameter of coaxial connectors on the thermal cycle reliability of hard-lap solder joints has been clarified, which is of great significance for the development of microwave RF components.

articleTitle: Microstructural Evolution and Shear Properties Degradation of Tin-Lead/Copper Solder Joints at Cryogenic Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the Sn-37Pb/Cu and Sn-90Pb/Cu solder joints were prepared and stored at cryogenic temperatures (-50 ºC, -100 ºC, and -196 ºC) for 240 h and 960 h, to investigate the effects of extremely low temperatures on the microstructural evolution and deterioration of shear properties of tin-lead/copper solder joints with different contents of Pb. We found that the influence of cryogenic temperatures on microstructural refinement was greater than that of storage time for Sn-37Pb/Cu solder joints. With the decrease of storage temperature and the extension of storage time, the intermetallic compounds (IMCs) thickness and shear force of two kinds of solder joints fluctuated within a certain range. For the Sn-90Pb/Cu solder joints, after 960 h storage at different temperatures, the IMC thickness increased while the shear force decreased. Meanwhile, after the long-term storage at cryogenic temperatures, the fracture surface of the Sn-37Pb/Cu solder joints still was composed of parabolic dimples, indicating that the fracture mode still was kept ductile fracture. However, the fracture mode of the Sn-90Pb/Cu solder joints gradually changed from ductile fracture to ductile-brittle mixed fracture with the decrease of storage temperature.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Thermal Stability of Ni UBM through Introducing High-Density Nano-Twins
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Nickel is widely used as under bump metallization (UBM) in electronic packaging technology, due to its excellent electrical properties, processing performance, and wear resistance. However, its thermal stability and corrosion resistance are relatively poor, which limits its application in harsh environments such as high temperature and high humidity. Therefore, improving the thermal stability and corrosion resistance of Ni UBM is a critical issue. To improve the thermal stability of Ni UBM, various methods have been reported, including alloying, controlling coating thickness, and controlling microstructure. Among them, controlling microstructure is considered one of the most effective ways to enhance the thermal stability of Ni UBM. Many studies have shown that the introduction of nano-twin structures can significantly enhance the thermal stability of metals. In this study, we investigated the effect of high-density nano-twins on the thermal stability of Ni UBM. We achieved a high-density nano-twinned Ni film by electroplating, which was characterized by X-ray diffraction. The thermal stability of nano-twinned Ni film was characterized by annealing at temperatures of 350°C and 400°C for 2-12 hours, respectively. The results showed that even annealing at 400°C for 12 hours, the average grain size of nanocrystalline Ni increased from ~30 nm to 0.93 μm, while maintaining a strong <111> texture. This indicates the introduction of high-density nano-twins significantly improved the thermal stability of Ni UBM. The nano-twinned structure effectively suppressed grain growth during the annealing process. This study provided a new direction for designing and optimizing the microstructure of Ni UBM to achieve better thermal stability and performance. The results of this study could help to develop advanced Ni UBM with enhancing thermal stability and performance, thus contributing to the improvement of the reliability of microelectronic interconnection technology in electronic packaging applications.

articleTitle: The prediction of orthotropic material properties for RDL based on effective modeling and CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The Redistribution Layer (RDL) is an essential component in modern integrated circuits (ICs) which mainly conducts electrical signals from the I/O to the internal circuits on chips. The cause of RDLs’ fracture is high stress during packaging. To estimate the stresses in packaging, Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is frequently used. However, the structure of RDL, especially the complex Cu lines, is hard to model. The mostly-used effective approach is to simplify the layer to a homogeneous one by volume percentage method. This approach greatly reduces the complexity of modeling the internal geometry. However, the volume average algorithm ignores the endowed directionality by converting the layer to be isotropic, meaning that it is constrained to simple symmetric patterns. Since Cu wiring patterns cannot guarantee directional uniformity in massive production, layers have differences in orthogonal mechanical performance. Although simulation-based methods can accurately obtain the orthotropic properties, it is relatively time-costly and the cost will increase significantly with the decrease of line width and the increase of wiring quantity.This paper proposes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for calculating the orthotropic material properties of the equivalent layer based on effective modeling. Material properties, including Young’s modulus, tangent modulus, yield stress, Poisson’s ratio, shear modulus, and CTE along each principal axis can be obtained by analyzing the wiring pattern using an asymmetrically-kernelized CNN. The major steps are constructed as follows. Firstly, the properties concerned are obtained through simulation by effective modeling. Patterned models are built and the simulation of uniaxial tensile and free thermal expansion tests are carried out by FEM. The required parameters can be afterward obtained in the virtual testing. Secondly, the obtained data are divided into training sets and validation sets at a ratio of 9 to 1. Finally, CNNs are established for training. The Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) is adopted as the custom loss. CNN training results show that the network can greatly reduce the time and RAM cost required for simulation while ensuring good prediction accuracy (MAPE<10%).Based on the method, the warpage of multi-layer was investigated. A 5-layer model exhibits asymmetric warpage during the reflow process, caused by the RDL’s orthotropy. Compared to the refined model of the multi-layer structure using 3D solid elements, the present method only needs to designate the mechanical properties (output of trained CNN with patterns as input) of each layer to 2D simplified shell elements, greatly reducing computation time. The deviation between the predicted warpage by CNN and the FEM simulation of the 5-layer wafer is within 10%.

articleTitle: Surface Protecting and Particles Removing after Wafer Sawing for Die-to-wafer Hybrid Bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Hybrid bonding technology has become an essential approach to fulfill the Chiplets technology. The wafer dicing process before die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding will introduce a large number of particles on the die surface. The method of surface protection and particles removal is urgently needed for D2W hybrid bonding with the bonding pitch scaling down. In this study, the photoresist mask and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) are innovatively introduced to protect the wafer before dicing and post-clean the particles after dicing. After laser dicing, the average particle density on the surface of chips without any protection is 83.07 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. The mixture mask of AZ4620 photoresist and PDMS film before dicing reduce the average particle density to 19.71 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. Further PDMS adhesion treatment as the post-clean reduces the average particle density to only 7.60 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. It indicates the surface protecting by photoresist and PDMS mask and particles removal by PDMS is qualified to be used in the die sawing and cleaning. Organic residue on the chip surface after PDMS immersion is also detected and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma treatment is effective to remove the organic residue. The surface roughness of chips descends after PDMS immersion. The results show that the PDMS is effective for surface protection and particles removal, which is suitable for D2W hybrid bonding.

articleTitle: Study on the interfacial IMCs growth of nt-Cu/In solder joints
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the trend of miniaturization, high density, and high frequency of electronic products, system in packaging devices are increasingly widely used in electronic products. Multiple reflow soldering is required in the production process of complex electronic products, and solders with different temperature gradients are necessary to achieve assembly. Indium has good flexibility, especially in low temperature service environments, it can still guarantee good flexibility, so it has relatively excellent thermal fatigue resistance. At the same time, nanotwinned copper (nt-Cu) has attracted attention in the field of microelectronics due to its excellent properties of ultra-high conductivity and ultra-high strength. In this paper, the microstructure and reliability of nt-Cu/In/nt-Cu micro solder joints at different reflow temperatures and time were studied. It is found that the phase of the Cu-In intermetallic compound at the interface is Cu11In9. And the shear tests were performed on samples of solder joints obtained under various reflow conditions to obtain the best solder joints. Finally, the growth kinetic equation of Cu11In9 was calculated.

articleTitle: Prospective application of nanotwinned copper for Damascene via filling and hybrid bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Nanotwinned copper has excellent mechanical and electrical properties, strong thermal stability and fatigue resistance, which makes it a research hot spot in the field of electronic packaging. And recently, research started to concern its application on the Damascene via filling and hybrid bonding technology. However, there existed a layer of transition layer upon the highly (111) oriented nanotwinned copper, which was consisted of fine grains, and usually in a thickness of several microns. The transition layer may further affect the overall performance of the nanotwinned copper when the film thickness decreased to several microns level. Therefore, in this study, we investigated the evolution of oxidation performance with film thickness, then tried to reduce the thickness of transition layer, and filled the via with nanotwinned grains as more as possible. Firstly, the anti-oxidation performance of nanotwinned copper films was studied. It showed that the oxidation layer decreased when the thickness of the film increased. The result proved the influence of transition layer on degrading the anti-oxidation performance of nanotwinned copper due to their interruption of the microstructure regularity. In order to reduce the thickness of transition layer, the influencing factors were studied with a coupon electroplating system. It was found that introduction of ultrasonic power, higher temperature and adequate content of additives can significantly reduce the transition layer. Finally, the optimized electrolyte (optimized additive content) and electroplating process (optimized temperature) were replicated on a 12-inch electroplating equipment (ACM, Ultra ECP AP). The result showed the thickness uniformity of the whole wafer without patterns was 2.85 % and the transition layer was reduced to 1 μm. Also, the 12 inch wafer with patterns of Damascene via was also electroplated. The research results of this study can promote the development of nanotwinned copper as novel interconnected material for Damascene via filling and hybrid bonding.

articleTitle: Design and Manufacture of Space Transformer for Vertical Probe Card
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the mass production test of wafers, the probe card is widely used to connect the wafer pins to the tester head of the automatic test equipment (ATE) system. Generally speaking, the probe cards can be classified into cantilever probe cards, vertical probe cards, and MEMS probe cards. Vertical probe card with cost-effectiveness is generally selected for high-end SOC wafer test. A typical structure of the vertical probe card is shown in this paper. It is composed of PCB, space transformer (ST), probe head, and certain mechanical parts (stiffener, ring 1, and ring 2). The stiffener is used to fix the PCB, while ring1 and ring2 are used to fix the probe head. The role of the ST is to fan out the probe points from a small pitch to a large pitch. ST is the difficulty and key point of vertical probe card design and manufacture. This is mainly due to the fact that with the rapid development of integrated circuits, the array of wafer pins is getting larger and the pitch is getting smaller. Among them, the PIN scale of high-end SOC products reaches 4000~5000 pins, and the pitch reaches 80~150 μm. This brings great challenges to the design and manufacture of ST. In design, how to complete the interconnection design of all pins and ensure the performance of the transmission line is the main problem to be solved in design. In manufacturing, in addition to the manufacturing difficulties of this kind of product, in order to meet the requirements of structure and stress, ST also has the characteristics of high thickness, the general requirement of thickness is more than 2mm. This paper focuses on the design and processing of ST based on multi-layer organic (MLO) form. First of all, in the design, the layer stack-up design of this kind of ST product, the design method of general interconnect, and the design of key signals are introduced. At the same time, simulation technology is used to ensure that the design meets the application requirements. Secondly, in manufacture, the semi-additive process technology is used to process micro-lines and micro-vias, with a minimum line width of up to 25 μm and a minimum via diameter of up to 40 μm. At the same time, based on this processing technology, the core layer can be used to increase thickness to meet product requirements. In conclusion, this paper proposes a design and processing idea for ST in the vertical probe card, which provides an effective method for this kind of product.

articleTitle: The Thermal Transient Measurement for the Carbon Fiber-based Thermal Interface Materials in Electronic Packaging Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Although the intrinsic thermal conductivity is merit, carbon fiber based thermal interface material is not confident to be employed as candidates to help dissipating heat generated from the chip timely in electronic packaging structures since the thermal resistance of such materials in the packaging structure should be evaluated first. In this work, thermal transient measurement is applied to learn the thermal properties of the entire packaging structure successfully. Through processing the measurement data into cumulative structure functions and then extracting the valid segment data from it, the thermal resistance of CF-TIM can be learned. By the investigation, it is found that the thermal resistance of CF-TIM is constant under various conditions of driving currents but is affected significantly by the packaging pressure and roughness of contacting material surface. This work can provide a guideline for the similar TIM’s thermally analyzation used in electronic package structure.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Wafer-level Interposer for System-on-Wafer Packaging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As people’s requirements for integrated circuits increasing day by day, advanced packaging and integration technologies are constantly developing and evolving. System-on-wafer (SoW) is a method that can realize high-density integration of chiplets by attaching multiple chiplets on a whole silicon wafer. SoW can reduce communication delay and power consumption. In order to ensure the chiplets work normally on the wafer, the transmission lines communication between the chips is needed to be studied. In this paper, the finite element modelling (FEM) of the signal lines on the silicon wafer interposer was performed. Comparisons of performance of the signal lines were made based on different lengths, widths, and thicknesses. At the same time, it was obtained that the loss of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> was -2.23 dB at a communication frequency of 10 GHz, when the length, the thickness, and the width were 2000 μm, 1 μm, and 15 μm, respectively. From 0 to 15 GHz, the impedance varied from 87.49 Ω to 27.81 Ω. Based on the FEM model of the signal transmission lines, a four-inch silicon wafer substrate with 2 metal layers and 22144 Cu pillars has been designed and fabricated. As a result, four switching chiplets (SDI3210) can be bonded on the silicon substrate by Cu pillars.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling and IP Technology for High-Speed Optical Interconnection Interfaces in Optoelectronic Microsystems
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The exponential growth in data communications and processing has resulted in significant advancements in high reliability, big volume, and low-latency data transmission technology. However, due to limitations in data transmission between nodes, the collaborative and parallel computing capabilities of systems are severely restricted by the bandwidth of electrical interconnection. This has created a need for optoelectronic microsystem integration. To meet this need, a range of integrated photonics components have been developed using the silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform, which offers high-confinement and compatibility with standard CMOS processes. While complex functional blocks or intellectual property (IP) cores have been developed and used to speed up the user IC design flow, the research on IP cores in optoelectronic microsystems is currently lacking. Therefore, in this paper, we describe the design methodology for modeling and IP technology used in high-speed optical interconnection interfaces for optoelectronic microsystems. We propose an architecture for high-speed optical interconnection interfaces, as well as basic unit modeling and IP technology. To demonstrate the proposed technology, we functionally decompose and design an IP prototype of a high-speed optical interconnection interface, which shows clear eye diagrams at 56 Gbps.

articleTitle: A junction temperature prediction model for 3D stacked packaging chip based on thermal resistance matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the package size of 3D stacked chip continues to decrease and the power density continues to increase, the internal temperature of the chip rises sharply. In order to meet the heat dissipation and reliability requirements of the chip, it is important to accurately predict the junction temperature of the chip. After fully considering the thermal coupling effect, this paper proposes a junction temperature prediction model of 3D stacked chip based on thermal resistance matrix. Meanwhile, The thermal simulation software FloTHERM is used to verify the prediction model. The results show that when different power is applied to 3D stacked packaging chip, the relative error between the calculation results of the model and the simulation results of FloTHERM is less than 5%, which indicates that the model can predict the junction temperature of 3D stacked packaging chip efficiently and accurately.

articleTitle: Board Level Solder Joint Thermal Fatigue Reliability Improvement by Optimizing PCB Pad Size and Solder Paste Stencil Mask Designs
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the application of consumer electronics, thermal fatigue reliability of solder joints have been received considerable attention nowadays due to the increasing requirement of long-term usage. Ball grid array (BGA) package as one of high-density packages has many advantages including excellent electrical performance, heat dissipation and improved re-workability, and is therefore widely used. The BGA packaging solders in the field are normally under the circumstance of frequent temperature variations because of ambient temperature change and various usage scenarios. The coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch between BGA package and printed circuit board (PCB) will induce fatigue stress in solder joints when the change of temperature occurs. Consequently, the fatigue cracks inside the solder joints may generate and propagate, leading to the severe facture of solder joints. Moreover, the underfill often apply in the interval of solder joints to enhance the mechanical behavior of bonding, which accelerates the thermal fatigue failure due to the larger difference of CTE introduced by underfilll. In order to improve the thermal fatigue reliability of BGA solder joints, the geometry appearance of joint was optimized by altering the size of stencil and PCB pad in this study. The BGA components were surface mounted on the PCB using different size of stencil and PCB pad, followed by the application of underfill. Thermal shock tests were carried out to measure the thermal fatigue life of BGAs. The cracks in solder joints were observed via X-ray computed tomography (CT) and cross-section cutting. Finite element method (FEM) using ABAQUS software was applied to simulate the stress and strain of solder joints under thermal shock, indicating the tendency of crack generation. The geometry appearance of solder joint used in FEM models was obtained by the numerical simulation of Surface Evolver.

articleTitle: Anti-oxidation property of nanotwinned copper micro-cone array for low-temperature bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Solid-state insertion bonding utilizing nanotwinned copper micro-cone array (nt-Cu MCA) was regarded as a potential solution to the vertical interconnection of chips. It is widely acknowledged that oxide on the Cu substrate is a hazard to the Cu/Sn bonding. However, the anti-oxidation property of nt-Cu MCA has not been evaluated, which is exactly the focus of our investigation. We measured the thickness evolution of oxide film on nt-Cu MCA during heated in air condition, which was determined to follow logarithmic law. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation showed that the growth rate of oxide slowed down as it thickened. Surface morphology observation revealed that oxide particles segregated around the grain boundaries, while twin boundaries had little effect on the oxidation, which was verified by MD simulation. The oxygen content on nt-Cu MCA was about half that on fine-grained Cu (fg-Cu), which can be ascribed to the small amount of grain boundaries. The great anti-oxidation property of nt-Cu MCA ensures the quality of Cu/Sn bonding in the future application in low temperature solid-state bonding.

articleTitle: Study on Micro-silver Joint Doped with Silicon Carbide Nanowires for Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Sintered Ag paste is considered as a promising die-attach material for the packaging in the power electronics, because it has great electrical and thermal conductivity as well as excellent mechanical properties. In this paper, the influence of minor silicon carbide nanowires (SiC NWs) addition on the mechanical properties and the microstructures of micro-Ag paste pressureless sintered at different temperatures are investigated. The preheating parameter of the specimens is set to 130 °C for 10 min, which is contributing to the evaporation of organic solvents in order to achieve a better sintered structure. The results demonstrate that as the sintering temperature increases from 250 °C to 300 °C, the shear strength of Ag sintered joints rises from 38.93 MPa to 43.44 MPa under the same sintering time. After doping SiC nanowires, the shear strength of composite Ag-SiC joint is better than the pure Ag joints at different sintering temperatures. The shear strength of Ag joint added with SiC nanowires is up to 41.95 MPa and 45.98 MPa under 250 °C and 300 °C for 30 min, respectively. What’s more, the fracture morphology shows that the sintered Ag structure produces plastic deformation in both Ag joint and composite Ag-SiC joint. Moreover, it is obvious that the SiC NWs nail at the porous Ag structure, which is beneficial to prohibiting the dislocation motion in sintered Ag layer. Thus, SiC NWs addition to micro-Ag paste can improve the mechanical performance of sintered Ag joint. It is hoped that this research can provide theoretical support for the application of micro-Ag paste applied to high power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Study on the Control Method of Moisture Content in Microwave Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the high integration of aerospace microwave modules, the number of electronic components and conductive adhesives in the modules has also raised. Correspondingly, the water molecules adsorbed on the internal surfaces and combined inside the conductive adhesive also significantly increase. Aiming at the issues of poor effect and long duration of traditional baking method, a new moisture control method was studied in this paper. Modules of the same batch were placed in an off-line independent oven for a pre-baking at one temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>). After the pre-baking, they were transferred to an on-line integrated oven for a short secondary-baking at another temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and then hermetically sealed. We compared and analyzed the effects of baking temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and baking time (on and offline) on the moisture content. Our data show that the off-line coupling variable-temperature baking method of appropriate parameters can significantly reduce the moisture content in modules, as well as shorten the baking time.

articleTitle: Study on low temperature sintering mechanism and performance of multiscale silver paste
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the vigorous development of new-energy area, the demand for high-power device gradually increases. However, high power inevitably cause a problem of heat accumulation. Materials with high thermal dispersion performance are required. Nano pastes that can be used for low temperature connection and high temperature service. Nowadays, multi-size particles mixed nano pastes have been developed, and mixed pastes based on micron silver as the skeleton exhibit better performance, including smaller porosity and better thermal conductivity. Nano particles plays a similar role like connection bridge between micro particles and flakes. After sintering at 200 °C for 2 h, dense joint with basic performance is obtained and sintering at 300 °C for 2 h, the thermal conductivity of the solder joint will reach 284 W/(mK).

articleTitle: Research on simulation of Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding process and interface failure mechanism by Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid bonding technology is proposed as a solution for the increasing demand of 3D packaging for higher I/O density and higher bandwidth applications. In this paper, a numerical approach to investigate the stress distribution of fine-pitch die-to-die hybrid bonding (D2D-HB) is proposed. The Finite Element Analysis (FEA) tool is used to build the model of the bonding process of D2D-HB. The influence of design parameters and conditions on the evolution of the stress on the Cu-Cu bonding interface and the dielectric layer interface during the bonding process is investigated. The results show that, the peak pressure on the Cu-Cu interface and the peak tensile force on the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface can reach up to 85.26 MPa and 183.37 MPa during heating stage, respectively. During cooling stage, the pressure on the Cu-Cu interface changes into tensile force, and the tensile force on the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface changes into pressure. In addition, the simulation results of the Cu-Cu bonding area are also displayed and discussed. For all the D2D-HB design studied in this research, up to 97.5% of Cu bonding area could be obtained. The simulation results will provide not only theoretical support for hybrid bonding technology.

articleTitle: Microstructural evolution and thermal fatigue reliability of Sn-Ag-Cu/Sn-Bi-Ag hybrid BGA solder joints assembled by low-temperature soldering
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu/Sn-49Bi-1Ag hybrid BGA solder joints were assembled by low-temperature soldering at 190°C and 210°C, respectively. The microstructural evolution and thermal fatigue reliability (-55~100°C) of hybrid solder joints were investigated. In the as-soldered complete melting solder joint (210°C), the chemical composition was uniform and identified as Sn-8.3Bi-2.7Ag-0.4Cu (wt.%); while in the partial hybrid solder joint (190°C), an inhomogeneous structure of un-melted Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu solder ball was partially wrapped by Bi-rich zone, which was identified as Sn-14.0Bi-2.4Ag-0.4Cu (wt.%). The Bi phases in the partial hybrid solder joint was mostly irregular reticular. The higher Bi content and irregular reticular Bi phases in partial hybrid solder joints led to a better thermal fatigue performance. However, the thick interfacial IMC layer and the large difference in thermal expansion coefficient among the materials in complete melting solder joints caused worser thermal fatigue performance of the complete melting solder joints than that of partial hybrid solder joints.

articleTitle: Selective Laser-induced Etching of Borosilicate Glass In Hydrofluoric Acid
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous development of 2.5D/3D packaging, glass interposers that can achieve vertical interconnection have been widely used due to their excellent high-frequency electrical characteristics. However, one of the main difficulties restricting the development of glass interposers is vias formation technology. The through glass via (TGV) technology has become a research hotspot due to its advantages such as low cost, small size, fine spacing, and simple process flow. This paper introduces a method of selective etching borosilicate glass substrate by laser modification. In this method, the borosilicate glass substrate was modified with an infrared ultrashort pulse laser, and then the modified substrate was etched with hydrofluoric acid. In this paper, a hydrofluoric acid wet etching model was established, and an electromagnetic simulation of TGV was conducted using the HFSS software. Ultimately, the process was optimized based on the wet etching model and electromagnetic simulation results. Through the experiments in this paper, the validity of the established wet etching model has been confirmed, and the optimization results based on the wet etching model and HFSS simulation show that a vertical through-hole (~85 °) with a diameter of about 100 μm can be obtained on borosilicate glass. A low-cost and small-size TGV formation technology has been realized.

articleTitle: Etching scallop-less nano-TSV with F/O coupling plasma
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through-silicon via (TSV) technology is significantly important in the three-dimensional integrated circuit (3D-IC), aiming to minimize the connection distance, reduce energy consumption, and improve integration density. To increase the stacking chip layers and the mechanical reliability, it is essential to develop TSVs with the nano-scale diameters. However, the scallop pattern resulting from the Bosch etch process is fatal to nanoscale TSV. In this paper, the impact of thermal stress caused by sidewall scallop on nano-TSVs is investigated by the finite element analyses. The high stresses may lead to crack propagation and potential failures. Thus, the use of F/O coupling plasma to etch scallop-less nano-TSV is explored. The effect of etching pressure and O2/SF6 ratio on the undercut and Si etch rate is investigated in detail. The results in the study can be used to improve the reliability of nano-TSV in 3D packaging.

articleTitle: A ReaxFF molecular dynamics study on the mechanism of material removal from 4H-SiC substrate in chemical mechanical polishing
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A model of chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) is developed using the reaction force field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD). Simulations are conducted on the chemical reactions and mechanical synergies of the 4H-SiC substrate in the CMP process, and material removal mechanism is analyzed. The results show that hydroxyl radicals from H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> decomposition play a significant role in oxidation during the chemical reaction. The atoms on the substrate surface are removed as Si-OH, SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by chemical etching of the polishing solution and mechanical abrasion of the abrasive, which are carried away from the substrate surface with the abrasive movement.

articleTitle: The Study on Bulging Mechanism of Plastic Packaging Materials for Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the character of lowly cost and large-scale automated production, plastic packaging materials are widely used in the packaging of electronics. As a common failure mode of plastic packaging materials, bulging will reduce the protective effect of plastic packaging materials on electronics, which has negative impacts on the reliability of electronics. The expansion of gas inside plastic packaging materials and the evaporation of moisture contained in plastic packaging materials are the main reasons for the bulging of plastic packaging materials. Through Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC) and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS), further research on bulging mechanism of plastic packaging materials is carried out. It is found that the curing degree of plastic packaging materials and the additives contained in plastic packaging materials are closely related to the bulging. In case 1, the DSC results show that the curing degree of the failed plastic packaging materials is significantly lower than that of the good plastic packaging materials, resulting in a decline in the mechanical strength of the failed plastic packaging materials. The gas in the inner cavity of the failed sample expands during the preheating, leading to the bulging of the failed plastic packaging materials. In case 2, the GC-MS results show that the failed plastic packaging materials contain 4-tert-butylphenyl glycidyl ether which is hygroscopic. During the wave soldering, moisture in the failed plastic packaging materials evaporates at high temperature, leading to the bulging of the failed plastic packaging materials.

articleTitle: A 3D Crystal plasticity finite element model for a 3D package under drop impact
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As one of the most vulnerable positions in the microelectronic package structure, the defect of the solder joint may result in the breakdown of the entire electronic package. Researching the deformation behavior of solder joints in various kinds of loads is significant. The micron-sized solder joints may only contain one or several grains, the traditional macroscopic phenomenology constitutive model cannot reasonably reflect the grain deformation caused by crystalline sliding. A 3D crystal plastic finite element (CPFE) model of 40 Oriented Grains is set up to study the deformation behavior of Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu (SAC305) at various strain rates of 1%s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 0.1s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 0.01%s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and different temperatures of 298K, 348K, and 398K. Using the Crystal Plasticity Theory, the deformation behavior of every grain, and the mean stress and strain relation of the structure is achieved by means of homogenization. The model is used to simulate monoaxial tension testing of SAC305 solders under various strain rates of 1%s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 0.1s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and 0.01%s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and different temperatures of 298K, 348K, and 398K. Based on the stress and strain relation of experiment data, the relative parameters of the model were adjusted. The results show that the Proper Precision of the SAC305 solder joints under various loading conditions can be used to describe the stress and strain behavior. On this basis, a 3D package finite element model with two chips is established to calculate the stress and non-elastic strain under the impact of dropping, and the sub-model analysis of solder joints in the package is carried out by using the constitutive model and a study was made on the deformed state of the solder joints. By analyzing the influence of different dropping heights (1m, 10m, 20m) and dropping gestures (face-down, right-side-up, and vertical-fall) on the deformation of the electronic package structure, the most vulnerable position of the package structure can be found out, which can provide suggestions for 3D package design.

articleTitle: Wafer-level Sn-Ag-Cu/SiO2 Transient Liquid Phase Hybrid Bonding (TLP-HB) Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Direct Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> bonding is an emerging bonding technology to achieve the high density and fine pitch interconnections, compared with the standard flip chip technology and the μbump technology. In the process of bonding step, the defect on the copper surface and the mismatch of the copper dishing weight would result in the property deterioration, even a complete electric failure. In this paper, to improve the bonding performance of the Cu-Cu bonding and reduce the difficulty of dishing height control, we promote a novel transient liquid phase hybrid bonding (TLP-HB) Technology, by using a deposited tin and silver bi-layer on the copper surface by the electron beam evaporation, which could change the solid phase diffusion process of Cu-Cu bonding into a transient liquid phase bonding process. The first part of this paper is to design and to fabricate the test wafer with the micro-fabrication technology. Wafer processing is achieved through the Damascus process, which includes the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film the deposition, the lithography, the dry etching, and the metal thin film deposition. The excess metal layer was stripped by lift-off process. The second part of this paper is the method to bond the silicon wafer and the glass wafer, which were aligned with the double-side alignment lithography machine. The bonding process was operated on the thermo-compression bonding machine under a high vacuum condition. Bonding parameters had been tested, and an appropriate process profile had been suggested. The hybrid bonding interface mechanism had been studied for both the metal bonding area and the dielectronic bonding area. In addition, the specific contact resistance for these interconnection joints were also discussed, based on the experimental measurement.

articleTitle: Conjugated Small Molecule Crystals as A Coupling Layer Between Carbon-based Thermal Interface Materials and Heat Sink
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Carbon-based thermal interface materials (TIMs) play a crucial role in maintaining the performance and reliability of electronic devices by improving their thermal management capabilities. Previous researchers have done a lot of work around improving the thermal conductivity of carbon-based TIMs themselves. However, as the thickness of thermal interface materials used has gradually decreased, researchers have gradually realized that the main bottleneck of heat transfer lies in reducing the interface thermal resistance between the carbon-based TIMs and the encapsulating shell or metal heat sink. In this work, we investigate the mechanism by which organic conjugated small molecule crystals reduce the interfacial thermal contact resistance between carbon-based TIMs and copper heat sink. By modulating the orientation of the organic conjugated small molecules, which have a π-π conjugated structure and a certain electron mobility, we have constructed a heat transfer channel at the interface, significantly enhancing the interfacial heat transfer and improving the overall heat dissipation performance of the device.

articleTitle: Warpage Control Method in Fan-Out Wafer Level Packaging with Rectangular Chips
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) is an enhancement of general wafer-level packaging developed to provide a solution for devices requiring a higher integration level and a greater number of external contacts. Compared to traditional packaging, FOWLP has strong advantages in packaging thickness, manufacturing costs, power consumption, and signal integrity. Considering the technical advantages and market forecast of FOWLP, it has the potential to become a preferred packaging technology for the next generation of portable mobile device chips. However, due to the influence of geometry structure or material distribution, there may be some differences in bending stiffness in different directions of the wafer, resulting in asymmetric warpage, which is also known as warpage bifurcating behavior. In addition, in fan-out packaging, most of the silicon chips are rectangular, i.e., the length and width of which are different, which will inevitably lead to serious asymmetric warpage after the process of the reconstituted wafer. Therefore, to reduce or even avoid the influence of asymmetric warpage in FOWLP, it is necessary to analyze the evolution of asymmetric warpage, explore the reasons for asymmetric warpage, and propose reasonable warpage control methods.In this paper, the asymmetric warpage process of the reconstituted wafer caused by package structure is analyzed by finite element analysis (FEA) and experiential verification, and the reasons of asymmetric warpage are explained in detail. Keeping the fan-out ratio, two warpage control methods are proposed by optimizing the chip layout, namely "dummy replacement method" and "interval arrangement method". Compared with the traditional layout method, the "dummy replacement method" can effectively improve the warpage morphology and reduce the warpage value. At room temperature, the warpage value decreased by 34.9%, but obvious asymmetric warpage still happens after debonding. The "interval arrangement method" shows a better result on warpage morphology, and maintains a relatively uniform warpage distribution after debonding, the warpage value decreases up to 47.3%.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of cell and multiple-zone gradient modulation field limiting ring(MGM-FLR) termination for 1700V/10A 4H-SiC merged PiN/Schottky (MPS) Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Compared with traditional Si, SiC devices have become feasible candidates for the next generation of power semiconductors due to their low on-resistance characteristics and excellent high temperature, high frequency and high voltage performance. At present, a large number of silicon carbide diodes have been used in the market, mainly including junction barrier Schottky(JBS) diodes and Merged PiN Schottky(MPS) diodes. They have achieved a good balance between forward conduction, reverse blocking performance and surge and avalanche reliability. In this paper, a 1700V blocking-voltage 4H-SiC MPS is designed and simulated, which uses multiple-zone gradient modulation field limiting ring (MGM-FLR) junction termination structure. The device structure and termination protection parameters are optimized in the paper, under the optimal parameters, Technology Computer Aided Design(TCAD) simulation results show that the designed 4H-SiC MPS cell can withstand 2170V blocking-voltage and the forward-voltage drop is 1.5V without considering the termination protection. When considering the MGM-FLR termination structure, the blocking-voltage is up to 1988V, where the efficiency of termination protection can reach to 92%.

articleTitle: A Novel No-Clean Type 5 SAC305 Solder Paste Reflowed under Air Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The advancement of miniaturization in package and board level assembly has been substantially accelerated by the growth of the Internet of Things and 5G. As the industry moves to smaller devices and finer pitches, the particle size of powder in solder paste must decrease to achieve ideal solder paste deposition according to the seven balls theory. Problematically, the oxidation rate of solder powder is inversely related to its particle size, as reflected by the higher oxide thickness observed for very fine powders such as Type 5 powder of size 15 to 25um. High-quality print performance and solderability of Type 5 solder pastes are critical features for fine pitch applications. Leveraging an improved understanding of print mechanisms and the material factors contributing to powder stability and solderability, a new halogen-free, lead-free, and no-clean solder paste 106-66-2 with Type 5 SAC305 was developed. The test results demonstrate this paste significantly improves print performance and solderability in an air reflow atmosphere. It also exhibited nearly none-grape and outstanding performance on low voids, non-slump, wetting on OSP and Nickle under air.

articleTitle: The Influence of Welding Interfacial Voids on the Thermal Conductivity of Space-borne High-power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Excellent thermal conductivity of space-borne high-power electronics is an important guarantee for the functional realization and reliability of space-borne high-power products. The welding interfacial voids of high-power electronics have a great influence on the thermal conductivity of high-power electronics. According to the typical space-borne high-power electronics structure and the actual situation of development process, the defect test samples with different void ratios were prepared, the X-ray detector was used to accurately detect the void shape, the Solidworks software was used to establish the high-power electronics structure and welding interface simulation model, and the ICEPAK software was used for thermal simulation analysis. The heat transfer test platform was built to test and verify the surface temperature distribution of test samples. The experimental results show that the overall heat dissipation capacity of high-power electronics decreases with the increase of the void ratios at the welding interface. The void ratio of solder layer of the power component should not exceed 30%, and the void ratio is better below 20%-25%. For high-power components with higher heat dissipation requirements, the void ratio of solder layer should not be higher than 10%. When the large area of the hole at the welding interface is located at the bottom of the power device, the overall heat dissipation capacity of the high-power component will be further deteriorated. At a lower void ratio, the void distribution has little effect on the overall heat dissipation capacity. When the void ratio is high, the void distribution has a great influence on the overall heat dissipation capacity, and the influence is mainly reflected in the position of the power device, but has little influence on the position.

articleTitle: Research for the development of advanced packaging material testing technology and standardization
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the analysis of testing and analysis technology for the main and auxiliary advanced integrated circuit packaging materials, and the main standards developed by SEMI, ASTM, IEC and domestic standard committees. The concrete research contents involve the test and analysis standard index system of major materials, main materials test methods and development of test and analysis equipment, including interface thermal conductivity materials, packaging substrate, plastic sealing material, electroplating solution, micro-connection materials, through silicon hole related materials, etc., As the same time, this paper summarizes the shortcomings of the current advanced packaging material testing technology and standardization, and put forward suggestions for the development of the industry.

articleTitle: Development of Low-Loss and Low-Cost Air-Filled Transmission Lines based on Advanced Glass Wafer-Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: To solve the problem of high dielectric loss of glass in mm-W/THz bands, we proposed two novel low-cost and low-loss air-filled transmission lines based on advanced glass packaging. They are the air-filled double-sided gap waveguide (DS-GWG) and post-wall waveguide (PWWG). It is verified that those two solutions have excellent transmission performance in the mm-W band. The low-loss and low-cost characteristics can also be realized in the THz band because of the high-precision glass wafer-level packaging.

articleTitle: Three-point Bending Test Method Experimental Study for Package Strength and Crack Prediction through Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years with the thinner, smaller, higher-density stack trend for package (PKG) design, the package crack risk becomes higher and higher in the assembly process and reliability tests. Therefore, it is crucial to establish an effective method to measure and predict package strength. The three-point bending (3PB) test is widely used to evaluate package strength. However, detailed parameters of the 3PB test vary among different manufacturers, making it difficult to compare data. Here, the main impact factors and mechanisms were evaluated to demonstrate the impact of 3PB test parameters on data. Additionally, a package strength prediction method was established using ANSYS software and Python based on epoxy mold compound (EMC) fracture. Results showed that the placement direction determined how the package crack and internal chips cracked before EMC instead of simultaneous fracture when the indenter was parallel to the package`s long side. Both crack force and strain were changed by more than 20% when one of the indenter sizes, span, or pre-treatment was altered greatly. The effect of speed and strain gage type on the test results was less than 10%. Furthermore, 3PB finite element models were set up, in which boundary setting was solder ball side towards up, short side parallel to indenter, φ0.6mm indenter size, and 12mm span without pre-treatment. The crack force of a typical same-die structure package was predicted through iterations, starting with an initial load value of 100Nton and increments of 5Nton. It was observed that EMC and chips broke simultaneously under the setting test conditions, with the EMC fracture threshold of 130MPa adopted as the criterion for terminating iterations. The highest prediction accuracy of package 3PB strength was 92%, which assists in package crack risk management and provides guidance for future structured design.

articleTitle: Glycine-Modified Boron Nitride/Epoxy Composites with High Thermal Conductivity and Low Coefficient of Thermal Expansion
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As electronic devices are being developed towards higher integration density and higher frequency, significant amount of heat will be generated during operation. The accumulated heat will impact the performance and the lifespan of electronic devices, which must be dissipated effectively and timely. Boosting the thermal conductivity of their constituents is one of the most efficient approaches to dissipate the accumulated heat. Boron nitride (BN) represents an attractive filler for enhancing the thermal conductivity of composite materials because of its excellent properties in terms of insulation capability, thermal conductivity, and coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). However, its chemical inertness and poor dispersion capability in polymer matrix limit its practical application. This paper presents a simple method to modify hexagonal BN (hBN) with glycine via ball milling to prepare g-hBN, which is then filled into epoxy matrix to form composites. Compared to unmodified hBN, g-hBN fillers endow the composite films with higher thermal conductivity (up to by 19%) and lower CTE due to better dispersion. Besides, the composites film can also maintain excellent dielectric and mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Copper Raw Material with Elongation Factor to Improve Delamination Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
