abstract: Delamination is one critical challenge for small outline semiconductor packages, a lot of studies have been done on Bill of Material and process setting influence on delamination. For small packages like DFN1006 that use normal pre-plated lead frame (PPF LF) compared with rough PPF, delamination is worse and cannot been eliminated with current process. Semiconductor practitioners are deep driving to find solutions to improve delamination. This study is about delamination performance with different widely used Cu material "Type C", other BOM and process conditions keep same. It was observed that different delamination performance was achieved with different Type C raw material. CSAM ( Sonoscan GEN5 machine ) is used for delamination investigation, Chemical composition is taken by X-ray fluorescence spectrometer (XRF, JEOL JSX-3201Z), mechanical properties were collected through a Universal Tensile Machine(Model: MTS Alliance RT5). Detail material properties been compared between different Type C, there was a variance of elongation found from different raw material supplier, which may be the reason that caused different delamination. A dedicated group of Type C was made with different elongation values for further validation. The results show that high elongation with low delamination between mold compound to LF surface. That helps explained the dependency between raw material and delamination, this data base would serve as guideline of cooper raw material selection to prevent severe delamination. The mechanism between Type C elongation vs package delamination is discussed and proposed. Two theories are assumption, one is during the saw blade work on the interface of mold compound and LF, the deformation of high elongation lead frame is closer to the compounds. The other is that the CTE mismatch between the copper LF and the plastic (EMC) is partly compensated by that higher elongation or "stretch" in case of a wide temperature swing.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of a simple fractional model for viscoelastic behavior of high filled polymer-based composites
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The design for the reliability of high filled polymer-based composites requires accurate knowledge of their viscoelastic properties. With the increasing complexity in classic constitutive models to achieve an excellent description, however, the inadequacy of requiring too many parameters and the difficulty of describing complex dynamic viscoelastic behaviors has been noted. In this work, a version of the fractional derivative model (M-S model) is developed, which is composed of a fractional Maxwell element and a Maxwell element in parallel, in order to simultaneously describe complex dynamic and static viscoelastic behavior of soft high-filled polymer-based composites using fewer parameters. The performance of the fractional derivative model and four parallel Maxwell model is further compared. The two models can be used to describe the relaxation behaviors and storage modulus, but it is relevant to underline that our M-S model requires fewer parameters (five) than the latter model (eight). Meanwhile, our M-S model also can provide accurate descriptions of loss factor of soft high-filled polymer-based composites, which cannot be described by the latter model.

articleTitle: Thermal fatigue behavior of Cu/Co-P/Sn/Co-P/Cu solder joint interface with crystalline/amorphous Co-P coating
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Brittle Cu-Sn intermetallic compounds (IMCs) are detrimental to the serviceability of solder joints. Cobalt-phosphorus (Co-P) is a coating choice with good diffusion barrier properties. In this work, Co-P coatings with 4 at.% and 15 at.% P content representing crystalline and amorphous were electroplated onto the Cu pad surface, and formed Cu/Co-P/Sn-Ag/Co-P/Cu joints by soldering. Thermal shock test was carried out for 250 cycles in the range of -50°C to 150°C, each cycle was 30 minutes. Under mechanical and thermal fatigue loading, fatigue cracks appeared at the interface of Cu/Co-4 at.% P/Sn-Ag/Co-4 at.% P/Cu, while the interface of Cu/Co-15 at.% P/Sn-Ag/Co-15 at.% P/Cu joint can keep basically stable. This work reveals the IMCs evolution of solder joints containing crystalline/amorphous Co-P coatings during mechanical-thermal fatigue. Combining the analysis of nanoindentation test results, it is found that the amorphous structure of the Co-15 at.% P coating leads to a low-hardness Co-Sn IMCs, which is the key to maintaining the stability of the joint interface. The soft Co-Sn IMCs bear a large amount of plastic deformation in the fatigue load, and improve the mechanical properties of the solder joint interface.

articleTitle: Chemical Reduction Preparation of Multi-Morphology Micro-Nano Silver Powders and their Performance in Solar Cell Conductive Silver Pastes
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, there has been rapid development in the photovoltaic industry both domestically and internationally. Heterojunction cells (HJT) are considered the next generation of solar cells due to their high photoelectric conversion efficiency and simple manufacturing process. However, the amorphous layer in HJT cells requires the silver paste curing temperature to stay below 250°C. Hence, controlling the growth process of silver powder, the primary and crucial component of the silver paste, holds significant scientific importance and industrial application value. We employed a chemical reduction method to regulate the growth of silver powder in (100), (111), and (200) directions, resulting in the production of nanoscale spherical, sphere-like, flaky, and square silver powders, as well as micron-scale spherical and flaky silver powders. The presence of nano-folds on the surface of the silver powder enhances its sintering activity. Furthermore, we successfully mixed and rolled these silver powders into various composite silver pastes with different shapes, achieving low-temperature curing.

articleTitle: Failure analysis and improvement research on flexible termination multilayer ceramic capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flexible termination multilayer ceramic capacitors (FTMLCCs) denote a distinct class of capacitors that incorporate an additional resin-conductive filler layer into the terminal electrode of surface-mount capacitors, establishing a flexible electrode layer. This layer is designed to absorb thermal and mechanical stresses incurred during soldering, consequently reducing the risk of ceramic body cracking. By assimilating flexible termination technology into MLCCs, we can diminish failure risks associated with external stresses without expanding the capacitor’s size or diminishing its capacitance. It is crucial to identify potential failure mechanisms when leveraging FTMLCCs for packaging or assembly operations. In this study, we dissect the termination structure, failure modes, and the efficacy of attempted improvements in two types of FTMLCCs. We scrutinized the interface structure of end-termination layers and the characteristic structure of the conductive-epoxy layer using advanced scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and 3D structure reconstruction via focused ion beam (FIB) techniques.

articleTitle: Effects of additive interactions on electroplating profile of IC substrate copper pillars
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Copper pillars exhibit great performance advantages beyond ball gird array (BGA) for large-area, finepitched and high-density interconnects in flip-chips, system in package (SiP) and 3D packaging. The development of miniaturized chips and heterogeneous integration demand for both high efficiency and high quality in electroplated copper pillars. A controllable flat or dished pillar profile is in favor of stabilizing solder balls during reflow, otherwise molten solder may flow off. Developing high-performance organic additives, including accelerators, suppressors and levelers, grains much attention in copper electroplating industry, which plays an important role in affecting electrode kinetics and deposit morphologies. However, as high current densities (>8 Adm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>) are applied in copper pillar electroplating, it brings a challenge to profile control that its top surface tend to dome due to breakdown of inhibitory additive ensembles. In present work, a self-developed copolymeric leveler is formulated with prototypical bis- (sodium sulfopropyl)-disulfide (SPS) accelerator and polyethylene glycol (PEG) suppressor to electroplate integrated circuits (IC) substrate copper pillar, with the multi-additive adsorption and interaction mechanisms revealed. As a result, flat copper pillars (size: 180×240 μm) can be achieved within a high current density range of 15 Adm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. Moreover, domed to dished profile of copper pillars are found to depend on the pattern size and can be tuned by tuning controlling the accelerator-to-leveler ratio.

articleTitle: Thermal Finite Element Simulation of Ultrafine Pitch Chip-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid bonding is a promising solution for three-dimensional(3D) integration because it can achieve ultrafine pitch interconnection. This paper design and simulate the expansion and shrinkage of Cu caused by temperature change during annealing by finite element analysis. The effect of pad shape/size/depth, initial dishing depth, and annealing temperature of Cu pad on the expansion deformation are studied in detail. In addition to the deformation, emphasis is placed on the peeling stress, which includes SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface peeling caused by the Cu expansion in the heating stage and Cu interface peeling caused by the Cu shrinkage in the cooling stage. These two peeling stresses bring the risk of interfacial de-bonding respectively. Especially, the pad arrangement arrays of triangular, square and hexagon are designed to study the difference of overall interface stress distribution.

articleTitle: Research on sliding mode control algorithm of permanent magnet synchronous linear motor based on fuzzy switching gain adjustment
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous linear motors (PMLSM) are widely used in chip packaging, aerospace, CNC machine tools and other related fields due to their high speed and high precision performance and simple structure. However, PMLSM also omits the traditional "ball screw + rotary motor" structure, which makes PMLSM unusually sensitive to external disturbances and internal parameter changes, and poorly adapts to the complex surrounding environment, thus making the system difficult to control accurately and seriously affecting the servo performance. The conventional PID controller has the disadvantages of poor robustness, low accuracy and high coupling, which is difficult to meet the requirements of high-speed and high-precision motion control. The sliding mode variable structure control has strong anti-regulation and anti-disturbance capability, which can significantly enhance the immunity and control accuracy of PMLSM servo system, and reduce the complexity of the system parameter identification, while for the inherent jitter problem of the sliding mode control method, fuzzy control is used to achieve online adjustment of the switching gain of the sliding mode controller based on fuzzy rules, thus greatly reducing the jitter brought by the sliding mode control. And soften the control signal, so that the control system to ensure the strong robustness of the sliding mode control, but also can play a good role in reducing jitter. The PI controller is used for both the speed and current loops, which can quickly offset the disturbance and eliminate the static difference. Finally, the designed control scheme is simulated using MATLAB software. The simulation results verify that the sliding mode control strategy possesses a good suppression effect on the disturbance of the system, and also show that compared with the sliding mode controller and PID controller, the designed fuzzy sliding mode controller can significantly improve the anti-load anti-disturbance capability of the system, which is insensitive to external disturbances and further improves the position control accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: Improve the high-temperature reliability of epoxy encapsulation with copper substrates through a copper thiolate complex layer
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The need to reduce the size of power modules has driven the shift from gel encapsulation to epoxy encapsulation. To ensure reliability, epoxy encapsulation must bond well with inside substrates, dies, and wires. Previous studies have shown that epoxy encapsulation failure is mainly due to the epoxy materials' low glass-transition temperature (Tg) and mismatch of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) with the metal substrate. Therefore, optimizing epoxy materials has been the focus of many previous studies. However, our study found that even high-end epoxy materials failed during high-temperature storage tests (HST) due to copper-catalyzed thermal oxidation degradation. As a result, preventing copper-catalyzed thermal oxidation degradation is critical for epoxy encapsulation. In this study, we proposed a solution for improving reliability by coating the copper substrate with a copper thiolate complex layer. It shows that this layer can improve the initial bonding strength with epoxy and also keeps the bonding strength after HST.

articleTitle: Research on the electromigration failure of W interconnects under high-temperature environment
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The aviation, aerospace, oil and gas exploration, automotive electronics and nuclear industries are increasingly demanding electronic components such as sensors, signal processors and specialized integrated circuits (IC) that can withstand high-temperature environments. This paper comprehensively analyzes the failure mechanisms of electromigration of copper (Cu) and tungsten (W) interconnects based on atomic density integration algorithms, taking into account multiple driving mechanisms such as ‘electronic wind’, temperature gradient, and stress gradient. It conducts in-depth research on the failure mechanisms of metal interconnect electromigration under high temperature, and provides guidance for the design of high-temperature interconnect structures resistant to electromigration. The results show that, under the joint action of a current density of 3.18×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a high-temperature environment of 250℃, W has a more excellent ability to resist electromigration than Cu. The joule heating generated by the interconnects under higher current densities (3.18×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) broke through the environmental temperature of 250 ℃ and accelerated the failure of electromigration. At low temperatures, W interconnects are difficult to happen electromigration, but the phenomenon becomes more pronounced as the environmental temperature increases. Moreover, the driving effect of mechanisms such as ‘electronic wind’ and stress gradients is more severe with increasing environmental temperature.

articleTitle: Rough Interface Effect on High-Temperature Reliability of TSV for Electronic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The most potential three dimensional packaging method is through silicon via due to the excellent electrical performance. Nevertheless, the mismatch of CTE between SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Cu becomes the main failure form of TSV structure. In addition, the rough Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface caused by the etching process accelerates crack expansion, which reduces the high-temperature reliability of power devices. In order to investigate the failure mechanism caused by interface roughness, a novel TSV rough interface modeling method by using W-M fractal function was proposed. The reliability of TSV structure with rough interfaces under different annealing temperatures was studied. The results indicate that a high annealing temperature will contribute to greater deformation and accelerate the overflow of TSV-Cu. There is a deformation fluctuation in the rough interface area, which exacerbate the expansion of cracks. Due to the plastic deformation, with the annealing temperature increases, TSV structure tends to exhibit shear failure in the Y direction. In addition, the stress concentration caused by rough interfaces cannot be ignored, which will immensely reduce the reliability of high-power devices.

articleTitle: Structure control and comprehensive properties study of UV-curable epoxy resins
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence and internet of thing etc, flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) has been an important package type to support these high-end applications. Thereinto, solder resist (SR) with good Cu migration resistance, excellent photo lithography resolution as well as outstanding comprehensive performance of high T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>, Low CTE, high thermal resistance and superior mechanical performance has been widely employed in FCBGA. Typically, SR consists of photosensitive resin, photo-initiator, active diluent, fillers, and other additives. The photosensitive resin in UV-curable SR is a polymer with unsaturated functional groups, usually derived from epoxy resin, and modified with unsaturated and alkaline-soluble groups. It is one of the main components of SR and plays a decisive role in the lithographic, thermal, and mechanical properties of the solder resist ink. As a result, it is quite important to deeply understand the comprehensive properties of photosensitive and alkaline developable epoxy. Herein, the effects of the controlled modification of photosensitive resin on the lithographic performance, thermal, and mechanical properties of SR are carefully explored. Firstly, a series of modified epoxy resins were prepared by introducing acrylic groups to phenolic epoxy resin at a molar ratio of 1:1 and subsequently incorporating different amounts (50%, 75%, 100%, and 125%) of anhydride to achieve various degrees of modification. Then, the modified resins were dissolved with photoinitiator, reactive diluent, and other additives to obtain solder resist ink, by characterizing its properties, a solder resist ink with better comprehensive performance is obtained, the asprepared acid-modified epoxy resin is a promising choice for the application in high-performance solder resist of FCBGA.

articleTitle: Mode I fracture of graphene reinforced Sn-Ag-Cu solder joints
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Mode Ⅰ fracture behaviors of graphene nanosheets (GNSs) reinforced Sn-3. 0Ag-0. 5Cu(SAC305) were investigated based on T-Peel test in this paper. By mechanical mixture of GNSs with SAC305, an enhanced mode Ⅰ fracture toughness is obtained at content of 0. 10 wt% GNSs. Mode Ⅰ fracture toughness of SAC305 with different contents of GNSs has been investigated. Upon adding the proper GNSs, the cracking path in SAC305 turns to be cohesive cracking easily, which leads to increase of mode Ⅰ fracture toughness. The average critical energy release rate obtained at content of 0. 10 wt % GNSs sac305 has been increased by 94. 56% and the maximum critical energy release rate was increased to 2. 2 times that of average condition in SAC305 without additive. The enhancement mechanism and agglomeration effect of GNSs are discussed , the different microstructural characteristics of the sample after mode Ⅰ fracture are introduced. The fracture properties of SAC305 with different graphene additive contents are discussed and clarified. The sintering method proposed in this paper meets the requirements of solder joint interconnection technology. This study presents a new insight for adding carbon-based nanomaterials to electronic packages to improve the mode I fracture of SAC305 solder.

articleTitle: Solution to Optimize Warpage performance for 2.5D Fanout Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In 2.5D fan-out wafer-level packaging, due to the high CTE mismatch between the Die material and EMC, warpage is inevitable during the manufacturing process. big warpage may cause high risk such as chip non-wetting or bump bridge when fanout chip attach on Substrate. Therefore, the warpage optimization is especially important for fanout chip onto substarte. The paper explores the machanism and the effect of different glass carrier, Wafer thickness, EMC materials on wafer warpage improvement. The optimization effect through warpage simulation and actual warpage data was confirmed, by monitoring the warpage change during assembly process. Base on the DOE result, we clarify an optimal matching mode of process, dimension, materials, and process parameters, which can provide the warpage optimization direction for the 2.5D fanout packaging.

articleTitle: Optimal design of the stress-buffering structure in MEMS resonant accelerometer package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: MEMS resonant accelerometer measures the acceleration by detecting the resonant frequency variation of the resonator before and after the external acceleration is applied. It has the advantages of small volume, light weight, low power consumption, high measurement accuracy, good stability, quasi-digital output and so on, and has become one of the important development directions of inertial sensors. However, due to its working principle, the measurement accuracy error of MEMS resonant accelerometer caused by the change of ambient temperature is the key factor that restricts the performance improvement and application of the accelerometer sensor. Therefore, how to reduce the thermally induced frequency drift of MEMS resonant accelerometer is one of the key problems to be urgently solved. In this paper, three types of MEMS resonant accelerometer packages with different stress-buffering structures were proposed. By means of finite element simulations, the stress isolation effects of the proposed packages were systematically investigated and compared within the temperature range of 25 to 125 °C. Finally, the optimal package structure was picked out, which can effectively relax the thermal stress transmitted into the resonator, and reduce the frequency drift of MEMS resonant accelerometer.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling of High Power DUV LED Chips Based on New Thin Film Packaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The encapsulation technology of DUV-LED lamps is a current research hotspot in the field of photoelectric detection, and metal inorganic encapsulation materials are favored by researchers in this field because of their superior airtightness and thermal conductivity. The aluminum-based metal film is one of the typical inorganic materials, which has the advantages of UV resistance and reliability, and has broad application prospects in extreme environments and special scenarios. Based on this, this paper uses Comsol software to simulate and study the bonding and shear strength of the aluminum-based metal film and analyze the stress distribution and displacement changes. The results show that the stress distribution of the aluminum-based metal film is uniform and the reliability is subsequently improved under the protection of oxide film. This paper is expected to provide reference and feasible suggestions for the packaging of DUV-LEDs.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-thin 90° bent vapor chamber for heat dissipation in multi-heat source electronic devices
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the high development of miniaturization, lightweight, and integration of the miniature electronic manufacturing industry, the traditional heat dissipation methods have been difficult to satisfy the high-power density heat dissipation challenges of multi-heat source electronic devices in a narrow space. At the same time, the amount of power chips on the PCB in electronic devices has increased dramatically, and the phenomenon that the heated and condensation parts are not in the same plane is becoming more and more general. The phase change heat transfer heat sink, which uses the latent heat of liquid medium to transfer heat through phase change, is the most efficient heat transfer device to solve the high heat flux heat dissipation problem. Herein, based on the phase change heat transfer heat sink, an ultra-thin 90° bent vapor chamber (UTBVC) that achieves up to 50 W of heat dissipation from multiple heat sources and has not yet reached the critical power of the heat sink is proposed. Furthermore, the study delves into how the heat transfer capability of UTVCs changes depending on their filling ratios and examines how their thermal resistance is affected by bending. In this work, the UTBVC is shown to have an excellent heat transfer performance, which reduced the heat source temperature by 23.44°C at 50 W with a maximum temperature difference of less than 1°C at the evaporation surface. In this study, a novel and feasible solution to heat dissipation in a narrow space with multiple heat sources is provided by the UTBVC, and a brave design for the bent vapor chambers in different planes is also offered.

articleTitle: Cascode GaN device’s Electrical Performance Failure Caused by Package Degradation under Repetitive Power Cycling Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, the electrical characteristics’ failure due to the chip-level damage and its relationship with the package-level degradation have been investigated for the Cascode GaN device under long-term repetitive power cycling test (PCT). At first, it is found that, the device’s transfer characteristics and threshold voltages have not changed until 8000-cycle PCT, while its on-state current decreases as the increases in cycles number. Meanwhile, the device’s gate-to-source leakage have not changed even after 8000-cycle PCT, but there is a significant increase in drain-to-source leakage. The above phenomenon has been attributed to the structural damage in the gate region of GaN HEMT, which has been verified by TCAD simulation and EMMI analysis. Then, it is found that the device’s thermal resistance is increased after the repetitive power cycling test, which is due to the package-level degradation. The increased thermal resistance will lead to the increase of heat accumulation, which has been verified by TCAD simulation, subsequently leading to the chip-level damage and electrical performance failure for Cascode GaN device.

articleTitle: Fan-Out Embedded Bridge Solution for Chiplet/HBM Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper will provide an overview of memory integration evolution trends seen in the industry across different package platform, including memory on PCB, in SiP and in chip module. From viewpoint of electrical/ stress and CM warpage performance, It figured out major advantage of FO-EB (Embedded Bridge) and FO-EB-T (w/ TSV) with HBM integration respectively compared to 2.5D platform. At the same time, we also exhibited chip module bonding guide-line according to methodology benchmark between traditional DB/MR and TCB process. Finally, under larger CM size and TCB adoption, FO-EB-T package level reliability w/ HBM integration also be demonstrated successfully.

articleTitle: Cu/SiC heterogeneous interconnection with high-frequency ultrasound at low-temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, 1-μm Sn-3.5Ag-2Ti(0.5La) alloy powder was used as a solder for Cu/SiC heterogeneous interconnects at three different temperature gradients assisted by high-frequency ultrasound at 35 KHz in ambient atmosphere. The results showed that more stable Cu/SiC solder joints were formed at 230 ℃, 240 ℃ and 250 ℃. The Cu/solder side was observed to generate the interface IMC (Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>), with its thickness increasing as the temperature increased. The connection to the SiC side occurred through diffusion of Ti atoms from the SiC/solder side. The study found that the shear strength increases continuously with an increase in temperature. At 230 ℃, the shear strength was measured to be 20.43 MPa, which slightly increased to 24.29 MPa when the temperature rose to 240 ℃, representing an 18.9% rise from 230 ℃. As the temperature was raised to 250 ℃, the strength experienced a further increase to 33.29 MPa, exhibiting a remarkable rise of 62.9% from the previous value recorded at 230 ℃. Meanwhile, the fracture morphology indicated that an increase in temperature led to higher amounts of solder residue on the surface of SiC joints, resulting in a more reactive environment. Additionally, the fracture location progressively shifted from the SiC side to the middle of the solder during this process.

articleTitle: Preparation of Nano-foam Sheet and Its Application in High Temperature Packaging of Power Chips
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC), a wide bandgap semiconductor material, has excellent characteristics such as high thermal and electrical conductivity. Nano foam sheet was prepared by dealloying, and used to bond chip and substrate by sintering at low temperature. Microstructure, interfacial composition, mechanical properties and fracture of the sintered joint were characterized and analyzed. AgCu alloy was selected as the precursor, and the bicontinuous ligament/channel structure was formed on the surface of precursor after dealloying. With the extension of etching time, the etching depth gradually increased. The nano foam sheet was used as bonding material, and could realize metallurgical reaction between substrate and chip at a sintering temperature of 300 °C. The joint had high shear strength, and could meet the strength requirement of standard.

articleTitle: Reliability study of Through Glass Vias under high current density
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through glass vias (TGVs) interconnection technology based on glass interposer shows a great application prospect in RF devices, MEMS packaging and other fields due to its excellent high-frequency electrical characteristics, outstanding mechanical stability, and lower cost. Electromigration is one of the common failure modes in electronic components, so it is important to study the reliability of TGV interconnection structures under high current density. In this paper, the electromigration of an RDL-TGV has been investigated by finite element simulation and experiment. Simulation results show that RDL-TGV junction is the most vulnerable area for failure. The experimental results show that the electromigration voids are concentrated on the RDL side near the TGV-RDL junction. The growth mechanism of the electromigration voids in the RDL-TGV structure is summarized. The results of simulation and experiment can provide guidance for the study of electromigration reliability of TGV interconnection.

articleTitle: Theoretical Studies and Root Cause Identification of the Pinhole Defects on Al Bondpads in Wafer Fabrication and Packaging Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, we will study a case of NSOP failure and identify the root causes. Through research, we determined and concluded that NSOP was due to the pinhole defects on Al bondpads and the pinhole defects were caused by galvanic corrosion and silicon dust corrosion. Moreover, we found that it was introduced in wafer fab process, but during wafer sawing process step, the corrosion was enhanced and got worse at assembly house. We propose and present theoretical models of galvanic corrosion (Al-Cu cell) in wafer fab and silicon dust corrosion during wafer sawing process; also discuss failure mechanisms and key characteristics of these defects chemically and physically; and how to eliminate them so as to improve yields in wafer fabrication and advanced packaging processes.

Author Keywords: Galvanic corrosion and Silicon dust corrosion

articleTitle: Simplified Evaluation on Cooling Performance of Silicon Microfluidic Interposer
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: simplified evaluation methods for the analysis on the thermal and hydraulic properties of the silicon microfluidic interposer for GaN power device cooling are proposed in this work. The microjet-microchannel hybrid structure and the parallel microchannel structure are analyzed and compared based on the theoretical and empirical equations. It is depicted that water realizes the best cooling performance among the common coolants driven by the identical pressure in the parallel microchannel structure. The convective heat transfer thermal resistance and heat transfer coefficient of the microjet-microchannel hybrid structure exhibit 22.4 % decrease and 2.24 times enhancement in comparison to the parallel microchannel structure on the conditions of the identical pressure and volume flow rate, respectively.

articleTitle: Directly Electroplated Metallization on Through Glass Via (TGV) Using Silver Nanowires Conductive Composite as Seed Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Glass interposer has attracted ever-increasing attention in 2.5D/3D advanced packaging field due to its excellent mechanical performance, thermal stability, easy manufacturing process and low cost. However, the poor adhesion between the glass surface and the deposited metal layer is a severe issue resulting from the smoothness of the glass surface, which limits its widespread applications. Herein, a novel method for realizing the direct copper electroplating on TGV is presented on the basis of a silver nanowire (AgNW) conductive composite. A pre-coat containing resin is firstly applied to the glass substrate as an adhesion layer. The glass substrate, on the other hand, requires only a simple cleaning process. The AgNW is then coated on the resin layer to form the conductive seed layer. Finally, the metallization of the TGV surface is rapidly achieved by direct copper electroplating. For TGVs with a diameter of 100 μm and a thickness of 500 μm, the surface morphology characterization indicates AgNW conductive composite is successfully coated on the TGV surface with a sheet resistance of approx. 39 Ω sq<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, leading to rapid activation of the copper electroplating. The metallographic microscopy proves the asplated copper exhibits excellent coverage and plating uniformity across the TGV at 2 A/dm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for 40 min. To further evaluate the practical performance of the as-plated copper on glass, the adhesion of the deposited copper is conducted by tape-test technique under ASTM D3359-02. The results show the copper layer has strong adhesion to the glass. Our work provides an efficacious method to directly achieve the metallization of TGV with the advantages of high metal adhesion, simple and cost-effective process. Therefore, this approach has prominent potential for application in 2.5D/3D advanced packaging.

articleTitle: Thermal performance optimization analysis of double-sided heat dissipation SiC power module for vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) devices have shown great technical advantages and market potential in the field of new energy vehicles due to their advantages of low stray inductance, high switching frequency and high temperature operation. The mechanical, electrothermal and packaging performance of power devices determines the reliable development of devices. The design and development of SiC device packaging structure that can meet the need for high temperature and high frequency is a research hotspot in China. In this paper, the vehicle SiC power module is taken as the research object, and the double-sided heat dissipation package structure is established. The three factors of chip solder layer thickness, buffer layer thickness and DBC ceramic layer thickness are taken as the research variables, and the maximum junction temperature and maximum equivalent stress of the chip are taken as the optimization target. The three-factor three-level orthogonal test table is established. Based on ANSYS software, the thermal-mechanical coupling simulation of nine groups of factor-level combinations is carried out. The influence of different thicknesses of solder layer, buffer layer and DBC ceramic layer on the maximum junction temperature and maximum equivalent stress of the chip is sorted by range analysis and variance analysis table. In addition, the Box-Behnken design in the response surface design method is used to generate the surface response diagram of the three factors. The influence of each factor on the maximum junction temperature and the maximum equivalent stress of the chip in the orthogonal test is verified, and the best factor level combination that meets the design requirements is selected. Through simulation analysis, it is concluded that the influence of three factors on the maximum junction temperature of the chip from large to small is buffer layer thickness, solder layer thickness and DBC ceramic layer thickness ; the influence of the maximum equivalent stress of the chip from large to small is : solder layer thickness, buffer layer thickness, DBC ceramic layer thickness. The combination of three factors was optimized by response surface design, and the maximum equivalent stress of the chip was reduced by 42.5% compared with the initial value. The research results provide a reference for the thermal performance analysis of the double-sided heat dissipation SiC packaging module for vehicles, and provide new ideas and methods for improving the reliability of the packaging module.

articleTitle: The Influence of Total Dose Irradiation and Annealing Experiments on Three Types of SiC Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: SiC MOSFETs have gained widespread application and attention due to their superior performance, but their reliability is still a problem that must be solved in application. This work focuses on the characterization test and analysis of main electrical characteristics and defect changes of SiC VDMOS with three structures before and after total dose irradiation and annealing recovery experiment. The experimental results show that the electron-hole pairs generated by <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co-γ rays inside the devices generate interfacial state traps at the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si interface of the gate oxygen layer, and the charge formed by the holes captured by these interfacial state traps at the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si interface causes the threshold voltage of the devices negative drift. The double trench device is most affected by the total dose irradiation experiment, with the most significant changes in threshold voltage, saturation drain current, and number of defects, followed by the asymmetric trench device, and the least change in the planar gate device. The characteristics of the asymmetric trench and planar gate devices basically recovered after room-temperature and high-temperature annealing, while the double trench device was still severely degraded. Analysis is due to the immaturity of etching and oxidation processes in trench gate structure devices, which leads to the poorer radiation resistance of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiC interface at the gate oxide layer compared to the planar gate. While the asymmetric trench structure protects the trench gate oxide layer by forming a P+ region under the gate slot through ion injection, which can alleviate the problem of poor radiation resistance of the trench gate structure to some extent.

articleTitle: A novel 3D packaging technology for high-reliability applications
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A novel 3D packaging technology for high-reliability applications was proposed in this paper. The Kovar pins were set at the bottom of the module, and the soldering area of the pin and the PCB was increased by several times without increasing the X-Y plane size of the 3D packaging module. So the reliability of electrical connection and mechanical connection between the 3D packaging module and PCB could be significantly improved. A 128Gbit solid-state memory (SSM) module was prepared by the 3D packaging technology, and there were 8 NAND flash dies with a memory capacity of 16 Gbit were stacked in the module. The size of module was 19.2mm x 13.6mm x 3.0 mm, and the weight is only 2.1g. The AC/DC parameter test result met the requirements of the chip datasheet, and the function ran without abnormalities. And the SSM module also passed stable baking (+125°C, 72h), temperature cycling (-55~+125°C,10 times), and constant acceleration (30000g, 1min) environmental tests, which could meet the requirements of high-reliability application.

articleTitle: High Speed SerDes Design on Flip Chip Package Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: High speed SerDes design are becoming so fast that signal integrity problems become more prominent. Whether using the non-return to zero (NRZ), or working the 4-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4), substrate design challenges include the impedance discontinuities and the crosstalk. In this paper, we discuss the bump pitch, trace layout pattern, layer define, copper roughness, low loss material, ball size and pitch to improve performance in the aspects of insertion loss, return loss and crosstalk for high speed SerDes application on flip chip package substrate. We scan the gap size of via pad which contributes the impedance discontinuity thus impacts signal integrity. Die bump and BGA pin assignments are the other two key factors in cause of crosstalk.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties and reliability of calcium-doped BaTiO3-based MLCCs with high capacitance
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) with high capacitance have great potentials in the battery charge-discharge circuit field. In this work, we fabricated a series of Ca-doped BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based MLCCs with a high capacity of 47 μF and high reliability. With the incorporation of Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, the temperature coefficient of capacity (TCC) is improved from X5R to X7R standard (EIA, Electronic Industries Alliance). We found that the samples formed the "core-shell" structure by TEM and EDS. Finally, we found that the samples with Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> doping concentration of 1.5 at.% have higher internal stress, which is responsible for the good temperature characteristics of the "core-shell" structure. Furthermore, the exceptional enhancement in the highly accelerated lifetime and reduction of oxygen vacancies confirm that the Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> dopant significantly enhances the reliability of dielectric ceramics in MLCCs. This study offers valuable insights and recommendations for further research on dielectric materials aimed at achieving high-performance and high-reliability MLCCs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Heat Source Arrangement for 3D ICs with irregular structures using machine learning methods
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D ICs) with irregular structures are recognized as a promising direction for the future development of heterogeneously integrated devices. Due to its high level of integration, 3D ICs encompass an increasing number of stacked chips and heat sources per chip layer, thereby rendering the internal temperature of 3D ICs susceptible to thermal interactions both between and within the layers. Consequently, the optimization of heat source placement on each layer assumes critical importance in order to minimize the maximum temperature and temperature gradient. In this paper, we propose a methodology to optimize the arrangement of heat sources in a three-layer irregular structure 3D ICs. Our approach efficiently combines COMSOL and MATLAB, utilizing a large number of initial samples that are subsequently streamlined through constrained sampling. By assigning diverse weights, we convert the multi-objective optimization problem into a single-objective optimization. Ultimately, we leverage a combination of artificial neural networks and genetic algorithms to achieve the optimal arrangement of six heat sources. To validate the accuracy of our proposed methodology, we conduct a comparative analysis against results obtained from finite element simulation. The comparison highlights the capability of our methodology to rapidly and precisely determine the optimal arrangement of heat source positions, with a maximum temperature deviation of merely 0.24%.

articleTitle: A fast and simple method to place sub-die under Chip-let architecture based on thermal simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The traditional system on chip (SoC) puts all functions on a single silicon. With the evolution of advanced manufacturing process, the more functions of Soc, the larger the size of silicon die. Besides, the number of transistors increases and the physical size of the transistors decreases, the quantum effect and the rapid rise of manufacturing costs are a series of problem. The industry has been looking for a solution to the problem of SoC, and one possible solution is to design a chip using chip-let architecture. The chip-let is to distribute large-size multi-core design onto tiny raw die, and then encapsulate multiple chip-let in the same package with high-density interconnection provided by advanced packaging technology to form a chip system. When Chip-let architecture system contains a lot of small die, despite the advantages of flexible design and cost savings in chip-let architecture, the serious thermal issue and reliability problems caused by the unreasonable distribution of small die. Therefore, this paper propose a simple and fast method to determine the number of chip-let sub-die and sub-die distribution. The thermal simulation of the chip-let system in advance can provide a key reference for circuit design and system packaging, and provide important reference information such as the thermal peak value and temperature gradient distribution of the circuit for the reliability of the chip. In this paper a three-dimensional(3D) physical model is established and thermal simulation is completed by using MATLAB and COMSOL software. Then, to select the material properties, boundary conditions and heat transfer model of chip-let system. Finally the temperature distribution and thermal behavior in chip-let architecture are analyzed under the 3D model. It is very convenient to analyze the overall heat distribution of the chip-let architecture system instead of actually producing the die. In this way, the performance and reliability of the chip-let system can fast and simple be solved due to the excessive number or unreasonable distribution of die under the chiplet architecture, which may lead to the increase of system heat or local temperature.

articleTitle: Interfacial Engineering of ZnO/CdS Heterostructure for Long Cycle Life Li-O2 Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Li-O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> batteries are very promising battery devices with a super high theoretical energy density. However, there are still some issues that need to be addressed such as poor cycle life and sluggish reaction kinetics. Therefore, we prepared ZnO/CdS core-shell heterostructure by surface-functionalized method. Similar lattice matching ensures successful coupling at the heterogeneous interface, and the built-in electric field promotes charge transfer within the material, thus facilitating the electrode reaction. The ZnO/CdS electrode achieved a long life of 140 cycles at 100 mA g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with a fixed specific capacity of 1000 mAh g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, far exceeding the 25 cycles for ZnO and 20 cycles for CdS. This work provides a new perspective on the interface design of cathode catalysts of LOBs.

articleTitle: A New Numerical Algorithm to Estimate the Average Travel Time of Workpiece in Packaging Equipments or Reliability Testers
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In order to reduce costs and improve the efficiency of production process in modern advanced manufacturing, one of premises in technology is to do some accurate travel-time estimations [1], [2] of wrokpieces in machine systems. In this paper, we proposes a numerical algorithm for evaluating the average travel time of workpiece in the packaging equipments or reliability testers. Firstly, the above travel time problem is abstracted into a symbolic idea and expressed by a mathematical model for set-to-set mapping. Secondly, a new numerical algorithm combining both Monte Carlo method [3] and several computational geometry algorithms [4] is designed to solve the relevant travel-time model and mathematical equations as mentioned above. Finally, a numerical analysis is also provided to compare the differences between the new algorithm and the theoretical solution of a numerical example.

articleTitle: A Cooling System based on Wafer-level Microfluidic Channels for the System-on-Wafer Packaging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of electronic products towards high-density integration and high power, the system-on-wafer (SoW) packaging is a promising technology. In this paper, heat dissipation capability of a wafer-level cooling system was researched based on the finite element modelling (FEM). We built a 3D integration model to research heat dissipation capabilities with different flow rates and fluidic channel depths. The results showed that there was a positive correlation between flow rate and heat dissipation capacity of the fluidic channel. With the same water flow rate, the heat dissipation capacity gradually increased as the channel depth decreased. This paper also presents a cooling system based on a wafer-level fluidic channel for the SoW packaging application. A 4-inch silicon wafer with a thickness of 500 µm was used as a substrate of the SoW. Nine dummy heating chips were attached on the wafer to mimic the heat situation when the SoW was working. Compared with an average temperature of 120°C of dummy heating chips with natural air cooling, an average temperature of 55°C was measured using the wafer-level fluidic channels. When the flow rate inside the channel was 1.5 L/min, the heat dissipation capacity of the fluidic channel cooling system was 0.14 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the thermal resistance was 0.141 °C/W. This is a significant improvement in wafer-level cooling performance, indicating that the microfluidic channel cooling system is highly effective in dissipating heat.

articleTitle: Chlorine and sulfur effects on silver bonding wire reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Currently, wire bonding still plays an important role in microelectronic packaging, making electrical connections between chips and leadframe or substrate. Silver (Ag) bonding wire is attracting more and more attention due to its advantages, such as the lower material price compared to gold wire, excellent electrical and thermal conductivity. The IMCs at the Ag and aluminum (Al) pad interface have an essential impact on the reliability. Ag wire are generally applied in consumer products as a reliable low-cost alternative to gold wire. In automotive applications, the materials are often exposed to strict conditions, such as moisture and chlorine (Cl) environment [4]. Therefore, it is necessary to make more effect on the Al wire bond reliability.This paper discusses the Cl effect on the Ag wire bond. Different levels of Cl were purposely added into the epoxy molding compound (EMC). To compare the Cl effect on Ag wire bond reliability, accelerated reliability tests biased highly accelerated stress test (bHAST), pressure cooker test (PCT), and temperature cycle test (TCT) were performed. It is found that Cl served as a catalyst in IMC corrosion under bHAST and PCT tests. However, S did not cause failure in Ag-Al wire bond.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Full Glass Antenna-in-Package by Laser Transmission Welding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: For coming 6G applications, next generation of RF integration architecture is pursuing more compact size and relatively low cost by using new materials and 3D integration methods. In this paper, a full glass TGV-based Antenna in Package (AiP) system has been proposed and fabricated by using laser transmission welding technology to realize the sealing and interconnection simultaneously at overall low temperature. Firstly, a 3D AiP system architecture was designed based on AF32 glass material. The bonding area using bumpless pads was defined on each layer. Secondly, the laser transmission welding technology was introduced and applied for the fabrication of the 3D full glass AiP. Finally, the bonding interface was analyzed in micromorphology which indicates a successful bonding of glass-metal-glass layers. And the bonding shear strength was measured under certain conditions. The results show that the bonding strength can reach about 50MPa and still maintain its strength after environment testing.

articleTitle: Design and H3TRB Test on 650V SiC-JBS Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and fabrication of a 650V/10A silicon carbide Junction Barrier Schottky (SiC JBS) diodes. They underwent a H3TRB test, and the failed devices were analyzed to determine the failure mechanisms. Various optimization strategies were proposed. After the experiments, most of the 39 diodes showed a certain degree of increase in leakage current after the 1000-hour H3TRB test, while their forward characteristics were largely unaffected. Additionally, one device experienced a sharp increase in leakage current and lost its breakdown capability. The failure of the devices can be attributed to a significant increase in leakage current at the terminal ring corners induced by water vapor, leading to thermal accumulation and burn marks. The differential thermal expansion coefficient between the passivation layer and the metal caused the passivation layer to crack and delaminate under thermal stress, ultimately resulting in the loss of breakdown capability and device failure. Different improvement schemes were proposed, including optimizing the terminal ring structure, passivation layer materials, and encapsulation material selection. The research in this paper provides strong guidance for the design of reliable silicon carbide power devices.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of Interface Damage at Cu/Polyimide Interface in Redistribution Layers of Fan-out Wafer Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, fan out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) plays an important role in advanced packaging technology, because of the advantages such as small package size, excellent electric properties and high I/O density and applicable to heterogeneous integration. It can be applied to many devices such as baseband chip, power management IC, radio frequency (RF) switch/RF transceiver, radar, audio codec, micro controller unit, etc. In FOWLP, the redistribution layer (RDL), generally composed of polyimide (PI) and Cu, may rearrange the I/O location of the chip and become an important component of FOWLP structure. During the construction of RDL, it is usually necessary to increase the whole structure of FOWLP to the temperature above 350°C to realize the thermal curing of PI, and then cool it to room temperature for Cu plating. However, due to the large difference in coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) between PI and Cu, the thermal mismatch during cooling process will lead to obvious stress concentration at the Cu/PI interface, which has a great risk of interface delamination and seriously affects the reliability of FOWLP. Therefore, it is very important to study the risk of crack initiation and propagation at Cu/PI interface.In this study, CZM technology was used to simulate the cooling process of the three-layer RDL structure from 350 °C to 25 °C, and the Cu/PI interface in the RDL structure was analyzed. The Cu/PI interface at the corner of all Cu vias in the RDL meets the damage initiation standard, resulting in interface damage. Among them, the Cu/PI interface near the corner of the Cu via in the second layer of RDL has the most serious damage. In the position where the risk of disbonding failure at Cu/PI interface is greatest, the damage factor is always 0 when the temperature is 350~145 °C, indicating that when the cooling does not exceed 205 °C, the interface damage will not occur. The preparation process of RDL can be improved by reducing the PI curing temperature. Increasing the thickness of the Cu trace can slightly reduce the damage degree of Cu/PI interface, but it is not a key factor affecting Cu/PI interface. The change of Cu via height will significantly affect the degree of Cu/PI interface damage, and the Cu/PI interface damage degree of Cu/PI interface with lower height Cu via sidewall is lighter.

articleTitle: 3D FO package technology using bridge die for high number of chiplets integration
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Moore's Law has been reaching its physical limits, while high-performance computing (HPC) market continues to demand for faster processing speeds, lower latency, and higher bandwidth. Many IC designers have disintegrated the functions of the dies into several smaller dies for lower cost, and higher performances. These smaller dies are named as chiplets that will be integrated together via assembly packaging.Since TSMC has been successfully developed 2.5D for Xilinx in 2014; 2.5D package has been overwhelming for the HPC purposes. As it able to integrate multi chiplets into a single module. But, as we pack higher number of chiplets, the size of the module is getting bigger. Accordingly, the residue stress is growing due to CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) mismatch between Through Si Interposer (TSI) and organic substrate. Besides, the number of TSI per wafer is getting lesser. And higher cost is incurred. Additionally, TSI has its parasitic capacitance. This phenomenon is in particularly significant as the processing speed is growing beyond 4 GHz [1].To overcome the 2.5D limitations, in this paper, we have successfully developed a new type of fan-out technology using high-density wiring of Si bridge die to replace the TSI. We validated this packaging technology with one SOC and two I/O dies (IOD). Instead of using TSI, we replace this with Si bridge die. The size of the bridge dies is 6.7 x 5.2 mm2; dies per wafer are 1804 pieces. As compared to 2.5D with similar package, the TSI per wafer are only 66 pieces. Based on 2 bridge dies are used to connect between SOC and IOD, we have increased the die capacity by 13 times. With that reason, the package costs have been improved significantly. This new type of package is named as Fan-Out Embedded Die (FOED). And the package has been developed earlier but with different approaches [2], [3]. And the final package is developed. Since the die to package ratio is low, and the CTE is well matched to the organic substrate, thus, the performance of reliability is better. Details of the process and reliability performances of the package will be discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Prediction of Electromagnetic Leakage from Circuits inside Package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, we use the equivalent sources based on near-field scanning to predict the electromagnetic leakage produced by circuit inside package. First, we use the near-field scanning system to obtain the electromagnetic information above the radiation source. Next, we calculate the equivalent electric and magnetic dipoles array of the radiation source. Finally, we predict the electromagnetic leakage by put the dipoles array into package simulation model. The accuracy of the proposed method has been verified through a practical measurement example.

articleTitle: Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown of 4H-SiC MOSFETs in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The 4H-silicon carbide (SiC) exhibits excellent material characteristics, particularly in high-temperature, high-power, high-frequency applications. However, the reliability of SiC-based devices operating in harsh environments is a critical concern. While time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) in conventional SiC devices has been extensively studied, its behavior in SiC MOSFETs within CMOS technology remains largely unexplored. In this work, we analyzed the effect of temperature and device size on TDDD failure time while employing failure analysis to identify two distinct failure structures. The finding of this research enhances the understanding of TDDB failure mechanisms and provides valuable insights for improving device reliability.

articleTitle: A V Band Ball Grid Array Interconnection Design of Ceramic Package with High-performance
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the advent of 5G era and the rapid development of electronic communication technology, the transmission rate and bandwidth of signal channels are increasingly required. In this paper, by studying the microwave characteristics of quasi-coaxial interconnection in ceramic substrate, a new type of non-vertical interconnection structure is designed. Through the dislocation design of metallized through-holes between ceramic dielectric layers, the impedance mutation of vertical through-holes and horizontal transmission line turns can be improved, which is more conducive to high-frequency signal transmission and further expand the application bandwidth. This paper focuses on the analysis of the transmission structure on the transmission performance, the final design and implementation of broadband low loss interconnection ceramic transmission structure. The test results show that the structure can reach the maximum application frequency of V-band, the insertion loss is less than 1.5 dB and the return loss is more than 15 dB in the DC~50GHz band, and the transmission structure can meet the high-speed signal transmission of over 100Gbps.

articleTitle: Nonvolatile Memory Devices Based on Two-Dimensional WSe2/MoS2 van der Waals Heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Non-volatile memory (NVM) plays a vital role in modern computing and data storage due to its fast read and write speed, high density and low power consumption. With the fast development of information technology, the demand for higher performance and density NVM is increasing. However, with the traditional Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor scaling approaching physical limits, the development of high-performance and high-density NVM faces several challenges. The emerging two-dimensional (2D) materials, such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with their unique electronic and physical properties, have garnered significant attention and have been expected as the potential materials for next-generation NVM devices. Here, we demonstrate a novel NVM device based on 2D WSe2/MoS2 van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH). The device exhibits excellent NVM performances with a maximum memory window of 135 V and the Program/Erase ratio is up to 100 at a low bias of 0.1 V. Meanwhile, nice program/erase retention and endurance performance were achieved. This work reveals the great potential of the WSe2/MoS2 vdWH for next-generation high-performance NVM.

articleTitle: Stealth dicing of SiC using femtosecond laser Bessel beam
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Nowadays, the mainstream way of dicing SiC is diamond or wire saw dicing, which has low dicing efficiency and high dicing loss. The edges of the cuts all have different degrees of chipping and incompleteness. Thus, the existing diamond mechanical cutting process is one of the factors limiting the development of SiC semiconductor process. Femtosecond laser is considered as an alternative to mechanical cutting because of its non-contact, high precision and how heat-affected zone processing characteristics.In this paper, we take advantage of the high penetration of the infrared laser to focus the femtosecond laser beam to form a modified layer inside the SiC. Then the separation of the wafers is achieved with the help of mechanical means. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to observe the microstructure of the modified layer. Raman spectrograms are used to characterize mechanical features such as component changes and residual stresses in the modified layer. Different laser parameters such as laser power and pulse width have an important influence on the modified layer. It further affects the ease of separating the wafers and the quality of the cross section. The increase in pulse width facilitates the formation of modified layers inside the SiC by ranging from 250fs to 5ps. This is because when the pulse width is small, the self-defocusing effect from too high plasma density cannot produce a stable modified layer inside the SiC. Different energy densities form a large difference in the size of the internal modification zone of SiC.

articleTitle: Structural design and optimization of rectifier module based on copper-clip bonding technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The traditional wire bond packaging technology has the problems of uneven distribution of temperature and stress and large parasitic inductance, which is easy to cause failure modes such as bond point breakage and falling off, which seriously affects the reliability of the rectifier module and restricts the electrical properties of the rectifier module. Compared with the traditional wire bonding technology, copper clip bonding has higher current transmission capacity and heat conduction capacity, lower on-resistance and parasitic inductance, moreover its process is simple, the comprehensive cost is relatively low. Based on cooper-clip bonding technology, this paper uses copper sheets instead of bond wires to achieve electrical interconnection and conducts structural design and optimization analysis of the 100V/400A rectifier module. The highest temperature and stress of the chip are selected as the key evaluation indicators, and the difference between the copper-clip package structure and the traditional wire bonding structure is compared using the electric-thermal-mechanical multi-physics coupling simulation analysis. The simulation results show that the maximum temperature and maximum stress of the chip using copper-clip bonding technology and the overall parasitic inductance of the module is 3%, 40.3% and 1.4% respectively, lower than that of the wire bonding rectifier module. Finally, the effects of different width of the copper sheet, the thickness of the copper sheet, the thickness of copper sheet soldering layer and the soldering area ratio of copper sheet on chip maximum temperature, stress and parasitic inductance value were obtained by simulation, and some suggestion of the design of copper-clip rectifier module was given.

articleTitle: The preparation of high-quality W-LED packaged with Sr3-xAl2Si3O12:xEu3+ and YAG:Ce3+
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, a new study trend has been generated by white-light emitting diodes (W-LEDs). Previously yellow phosphor were packaged with blue chip using an organic glue. When common blue chips with yellow phosphors are utilized, the resulting W-LEDs are less red. For solving the above issue. As an effective method that Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>:xEu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> (SASO:xEu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>) for LED lighting is rarely addressed at the moment. Bright red emission under 465nm blue light is displayed by SASO:xEu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> phosphors with great luminous brightness and purity. In this study, YAG:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> yellow phosphor was coupled with SASO:xEu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> red phosphor to compensate for red light. Phosphor with a high luminous performance was made using a high temperature solid phase process. The phase structure of the phosphors was then observed using a scanning electron microscope (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), the chromaticity diagram CIE map was obtained using a photometric integrating sphere, and the photoluminescence (PL) and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectra were tested using a fluorescence spectrometer. Red phosphors were tested at various doping levels, and they reached their greatest light intensity when x = 0.06. It was found that the packaged W-LED had an impressive white light emission characteristic with a high color rendering index CRI (Ra=86.1) and low correlated color temperature CCT (4548 K).

articleTitle: Simulation study of silicon carbide scratching process with double diamond abrasive
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) removal process was simulated by smoothed particle hydrodynamics and finite element method (SPH-FEM) with double diamond abrasive, SPH-FEM could prevent the influence of mesh distortion. The results show that there are three interference modes while scratching: plastic damage interference, plastic damage and lateral crack interference, and lateral crack interference. With the increase of double diamond abrasive distance, the interference region groove width increases linearly, but the interference region groove depth decreases. When the interference mode is stable, the groove depth nearly remains constant. When the interference mode changes, the maximum width to depth ratio of the interference region will change significantly. The average scratching force of SiC will fluctuate with the change of interference mode. In the lateral crack interference mode, the groove width is large, the subsurface damage is small, the width to depth ratio of the interference region is large, which means that the large width to depth ratio helps reduce subsurface damage. It is more conducive to the removal of materials and improve the surface quality after scratching.

articleTitle: A Wire-less SiC Power Module Using Flip-Chip Sintering Method
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As SiC devices move towards lower specific RDS(on) and higher current density, traditional wire bonding SiC power modules are facing serious challenges in thermal management. The top-side of the SiC device of the double-sided cooling (DSC) power module uses a metal surface interconnection instead of the bonding wire point interconnection of the single-sided cooling (SSC) power module, which can effectively improve the current carrying capacity of the devices and significantly reduce the device junction temperature. However, the fragile interconnection structure on the top-side of the SiC devices of the DSC power modules will endure high thermomechanical stress from the upper large-area substrate, leading to significant thermal-mechanical reliability concerns. This paper proposes a flip-chip sintering interconnection method for DSC power modules which strengthens the mechanical interconnection structure between the top-side of the SiC device and the upper substrate. Simultaneously, it further improves the double-sided heat dissipation efficiency and current carrying capacity of the SiC device. Compared with the traditional DSC power modules, the maximum junction temperature of the SiC device of the flip-chip double-sided cooling (FCDSC) power modules is reduced by 14.2%, the effective interconnection area is increased by 60.5%, the maximum thermomechanical stress of the SiC device is reduced by 11.0%, and the maximum current carrying capacity is increased by 5.5%.

articleTitle: Research on Local Heating of Flat Plate Based on Electric Field Distribution Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: At present, heating the local fixed point area of the plate is a research hotspot. This paper introduces a local heating method of the plate based on electric field. The electric field regulates the formation of liquid polymer column, and heat transfer from the bottom substrate electrode to the top electrode plate in contact with the liquid polymer column to realize local heat transfer, and the heat transfer position can be accurately regulated by designing several independent conductive areas of upper electrode. The relationship between the center temperature of liquid column and time is studied. It reaches the highest temperature of 100.7 ℃ when the preset temperature of the heating platform was 135℃.

articleTitle: Laser-induced processing of thermal cloaks enabling heat shielding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal cloaks based on multi-layered structure consisted of laser-induced graphene (LIG) layers, are designed to shield heat from a central region and keep its temperature distribution. Complex thermal cloak structures with tunable thermal conductivities can be precisely processed by programming laser directly scanning method. The effect of laser processing parameters on thermal conductivity of LIG is investigated. To obtain the optimal design of the LIG-based thermal cloak, finite element simulations are performed for monolayer, bilayer and multilayer thermal cloaks. The designed thermal cloaks are assembled by alternating LIG layers and polyimide (PI) layers.
