The neural network was adopted to train prediction models. By using the factor analysis technique, the number of dominant factors is determined to be 40 based on the Scree plot. The value of the common factors corresponding to each material is evaluated, and the load coefficients between the common factors and the material characteristics is formed with the hot image. Following the above regression model and feature engineering, the decision coefficient of 0.80 was obtained for the testing set, indicating that the trained model has good predictive performance. The results provide useful insights for the following screening of low-k dielectric constant crystals.

articleTitle: Newly designed colloidal silica for copper chemical mechanical polishing in electronic packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of IC techniques, it is challenging to follow the Moore’s law any longer for the IC fabrication as the feature size of FETs has been close to the physical limitation for quantum effect. As the technology beyond the Moore’s law, the advanced electronic packaging has become the alternative approach for persisting the enormous increment of FET density in the chips. In the IC fabrication and advanced electronic packaging (RDL), the global planarization of the TSV copper interconnects can only be achieved via the chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). In the Cu-CMP process, the slurry used for the polishing is mainly composed of colloidal silica, oxidizer, coordination ligand, inhibitor and the surfactant. The mechanical abrasion in the CMP is mainly supported by the colloidal silica, where the particle size, size distribution, the zeta potential, and the pH are the main factors that could determine the material removal rate (MRR) and the surface uniformity. In generally, Cu-CMP slurries mainly contains colloidal silica below 100 nm, under which the MRR is inconvenient to be further promoted. On the other hand, the Cu-CMP slurries are always adjusted to low pH (acidic) or large pH (alkalic) dispersions, which is harmful to the CMP instruments or the human health.In this paper, the colloidal silica with monodispersed sub-micron particle size and high purity was synthesized by a new approach assisted by the amino acids. The newly designed colloidal silica has the controllable particle size, monodispersed size distribution, large absolute zeta potential as well as the neutral pH. The CMP experimental results revealed that high MRR, high long-term stability, low surface roughness and low particle residues could be achieved via applying the newly designed colloidal silica, which should be promising for the global planarization of TSV copper interconnects for the advanced electronic packaging.

articleTitle: A Combined Experimental and Analytical Study of Residual Strains Developed in Encapsulated Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A combined experimental and analytical study of strains developed in epoxy encapsulated assemblies during curing and thermal cycle was described. The experimental setup, designed to measure in-situ strains, consisted of thin Kovar tube that was instrumented with strain gages and thermocouples before epoxy curing. After curing, strains were measured over the temperature range of 20°C ~70°C and 20°C ~-40°C. Results showed that for the encapsulant where the outer surfaces were not constrained, the Kovar tube did not pick up mechanically induced strains until the temperature dropped to glass transition temperature, Tg. The stresses and strains developed during gelation, cure and at temperature above Tg were insignificant. The results provided the facts that Tg was the stress free temperature for unconstrained structure. The thermal cycle experiments were then numerically modelled using finite element method. The predicted strains were over estimated when a linear-elastic, temperature-dependent material model was assumed for the encapsulant. Excellent agreement was obtained when a viscoelastic material model was used and a stress free temperature corresponding to the cure temperature was assumed.

articleTitle: Optimization and Research on Warpage of Ultra-thin Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The rigidity of ultra-thin substrate is very small, and they are very sensitive to material selection and matching. During product processing, they are prone to warping and deformation, leading to failure forms such as solder ball solder joints and short circuits. To ensure the yield of ultra-thin products, reasonable material selection and matching must be carried out. In this paper, aiming at the phenomenon of solder ball solder failure after reflow soldering of an ultra-thin packaging product, the influence of different material selection on the warpage of the ultra-thin product was first compared using the workbench simulation, and then the simulation results were verified by experiments. Unlike the traditional method of equivalent material CTE and elastic modulus, this article uses segmented functions to characterize material characteristics during the simulation process, improving reliability and accuracy, solving the problem of virtual soldering in ultra-thin product, and providing a theoretical basis for optimizing the reliability of ultra-thin packaging products.

articleTitle: Modeling Methodology for Mechanical Shock Reliability Enhancement Designs of Ultra-Large BGA Packages
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In a previous study [1], the authors have shown that a well-benchmarked modeling methodology is capable of accurately predicting the maximum principal PCBA strain at BGA corners. The methodology can also be utilized with virtual Design of Experiment (DoE) to conduct sensitivity studies to capture the impact of key design parameters such as package size, PCB thickness, etc. The results of such simulation DOE can be applied to develop design guidelines to enhance BGA shock performance. In this study, the virtual DOE have been extended to include ultra-large package sizes up to 75mm. A review of the previous DOE results showed that the model-predicted-PCB strains normally match the upper bound of the experimental results, which sometimes is desired but may lead to conservative designs. To improve the model prediction, a structural Damping Coefficient (DC) has been introduced based on the shock testing results across different package sizes. With a well-tuned damping coefficient, the model predictions match well with the mean of the testing results of different package sizes, which is useful for studying the impact of different parameters on the variability of shock performance. The comprehensive modeling methodology outlined in this paper can help engineers design more robust products by optimizing geometry, material and process without physically building and testing the parts, which is impossible early in the product design process.

articleTitle: Influence of Cu Nanoparticles on IMCs between Sn/Cu joint during isothermal stage of soldering
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the down-sized of the solder joint, the thickness of the intermetallic compounds (IMCs) layer increases at the interface of the solder joint. In addition, thick IMC layer can be a severe challenge due to its brittleness for the service life of solder joint. In this study, Cu nanoparticles (NPs) was introduced at the interface of Sn/Cu solder joint. Combined with high-pressure air purging liquid solder experiment, the effect of NPs on the growth behaviour of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> at the interface of Sn/Cu solder joint during the heat preservation stage of soldering has been studied. At the beginning of heat preservation stage of soldering, Cu NPs not only provide heterogeneous nucleation sites but also partially dissolve in the liquid solder make the Cu concentration increase, which lead to the increase of the nuclei number of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grains and sharply decrease in the grain size. With the heat preservation stage ongoing, the effect of Cu NPs on growth of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> is governed by two competing mechanisms. On the one hand, the increase of Cu concentration enhances the ripening growth of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>, which promotes the growth of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>; On the other hand, the reaction between Cu NPs and Sn lead to the formation of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> NPs, which adsorb on the surface of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grains, reduce Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> surface energy and slow down the growth rate.

articleTitle: Common Failure Phenomenon of Microwave Components/Modules in Quality Inspection and Measures of Process Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Microwave components/modules are vital parts of communication devices, and their reliability greatly impacts the performance and lifespan of the entire device. Prior to the production and widespread use of communication equipment, product reliability was typically evaluated from various perspectives, with quality inspection being the most common method of assessment. In recent years, there has been a relatively high incidence of loss of efficacy in microwave components/modules during quality inspection, yet few papers and reports have summarized and analyzed their failure modes and causes. This article presents an analysis of 15 cases of loss of efficacy among 51 quality inspection cases of microwave components. The findings indicate that electrical performance decline due to Hydrogen Effect and appearance damage of microwave components after undergoing Salt Spray Test are two common failure modes observed during quality inspection. This article analyzes the reasons behind these two typical failure modes and proposes corresponding suggestions for improving manufacturing technology. For failures caused by Hydrogen Effect, the hydrogen resistance reliability of microwave components/modules can be effectively improved by reasonably selecting hydrogen resistant bare chips, adding hydrogen absorption materials, changing the thickness of passivation layer, high-temperature baking to reduce hydrogen content, and optimizing design of chips and microwave circuit. For failures caused by Salt Spray condition, process improvement should be implemented during the production and packaging process, such as perfecting the surface treatment process before coating, adding chemical polishing procedures during the lead sintering and plating processes for those components with glass insulators, properly selecting the coating material and thickness and Strictly controlling the uniformity of coating. Those means will effectively reduce the incidence of phenomena like Fracture of Leads, coating corrosion and peeling after salt spray test. Based on the process improvement measures proposed in this article, several failure types of microwave components/modules were rectified accordingly. Those rectified components/modules successfully passed the quality inspection of salt spray testing, which further made verification of the effectiveness of those process improvement measures. The research presented in this paper has significant implications for enhancing the reliability of microwave components/modules.

articleTitle: Using Stacked Inverse-Reflective Cup Structure to Improve Vertical Light Output and Ambient Contrast Ratio of Light Emitting Diode Display Device
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: For outdoor displays, high ambient contrast ratio (ACR) and high brightness in the vertical direction of the display screen are crucial. So far, it remains challenging to maintain high ACR while improving vertical brightness output for outdoor display devices. Therefore, we propose a stacked inverse-reflective cup structure to address this problem. The structure comprises a transparent inverse-reflective cup encapsulating the chip and a bottom layer filled with high-scattering TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> scattering layer and a top layer filled with high-absorption graphite extinction layer. By utilizing optical software for simulation, we optimized the stacked inverse-reflective cup structure and revealed the mechanism for achieving low reflectance and high vertical brightness output for the device. By adjusting the tilt angle of the transparent inverse-reflective cup and the thickness of the graphite extinction layer, the vertical output and ACR of the chip can be selectively adjusted. Compared to devices with transparent packaging, devices with stacked inverse-reflective cup structures achieved high ACR, increasing from 114 to 563, a 393% increase (ambient light of 10,000 Lux). At the same time, the vertical brightness output was improved by 113.4%, compared to devices with transparent packaging. Due to the simplicity of the stacked inverse-reflective cup structure, it can be easily integrated into outdoor display devices, achieving excellent ACR and higher vertical brightness output, meeting the extensive application needs of outdoor large-screen displays.

articleTitle: Study of Waveguide Sizes for Silicon based Micro-ring Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the explosive growth of information transmission, optical communication is highly prized for its advantages such as large bandwidth, low latency and high immunity to electromagnetic interference. In this context, it is important to investigate integrated low-cost, high-density photonic devices. In this paper, the effect of optical waveguide sizes on the micro-ring filtering effect is studied by designing an orthogonal experimental analysis method. Three influence factors were designed for this experiment, namely, the waveguide width, the height of the waveguide and the coupling spacing. Among them, each influence factor includes four sets of experimental data. Finally, based on the analysis of simulation results, the waveguide size of 360 nm*200 nm and the coupling pitch of 220 nm are determined. Simultaneously, the parameters of micro-ring performance are as follows: Q=1196.6, FWHM=1.31 nm, FSR=26.1 nm, and F=19.92. At the same time, during the analysis of simulation experiments, it was also found that when the length of Lc gradually increased in steps of 0.1 μm within the range of 0-2 μm, the phase of the output spectrum of the micro-loop filter would shift, with an offset of 6.1 nm. This phenomenon can achieve phase compensation when phase shift occurs due to process issues in the micro-ring fabrication process. The excellent performance of these parameters provides strong theoretical support for achieving efficient, low-cost, and high-density photonic devices.

articleTitle: A High Density QFP With Hybrid Lead
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: HDQFP package is a new package type which combines both QFP (quad flat pack) gull-wing (GW) and PLCC (plastic leaded chip carrier) J lead. It has been mass production and offered 172IO with 16x16 mm body size and 100IO with 10x10 mm body size. This paper will show the advantage of HDQFP as compared to standard LQFP/QFP packages at introduction section. The challenges in manufacturing, designs and concerns of tighter lead pitches for HDQFP are briefly addressed. Sn whisker stress data were collected and shown passing requirements. The board-level solder joint reliability (SJR) data and component level package reliability data have proven passing AEC G1 (Automotive Electronic Council Grade 1) and summarized in this paper. Visual inspection methods and requirements on AOI (Automated Object Inspection) systems on solider joints of J-leads of HDQFP are proposed and results of detecting several failure modes of solder joints are presented. Assembly challenges are briefly described. Future works will also be summarized.

articleTitle: Orientation-related stress analysis of nanotwinned copper in redistributed layer for wafer-level packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the chips continue to develop, the line width and spacing of redistributed layer (RDL) decrease gradually while the number of stack layers increase, resulting in an increased current density and internal thermal stress in Cu lines. Ordinary electroplated copper (OE-Cu) is susceptible to breakage failure at thin point, due to the dual effects of thermal stress and electromigration. In contrast, nanotwinned copper (NT-Cu) haves higher mechanical strength and excellent conductivity. It has the potential to be the next-generation interconnected material because of its high-density randomly distributed twin boundaries. Besides, NT-Cu exhibits significant anisotropy closely related to the growth direction of twinned lamellae. Because of its special structures and physical properties, the stress of NT-Cu in RDL may be very different from that of OE-Cu. Gaining a comprehensive understanding of the stress state of NT-Cu could help to design RDL layout which are more suitable for its structures and physical properties, thereby improving its reliability.In this paper, we studied the thermal stress distribution of a multilayer RDL structure during the curing process of polyimide (PI) by using finite element analysis (FEA). On the basis of accurate elastic-plastic mechanical constitutive, we focused on investigating the influence of NT-Cu orientation and anisotropy on the thermal stress risk of RDL structures. For fine lines, it was found that NT-Cu with different orientations has different thermal stresses, 90°-twin-orientation being the highest, followed by 0°, and 45° being the lowest. Further, we found that OE-Cu had entered into the plastic deformation stage during PI curing process, while NT-Cu remained in elastic stage due to its extremely high yield strength. In addition, the simulation results of anisotropic constitutive behavior indicate that using only the mechanical isotropic data can also obtain relatively accurate results.

articleTitle: Influence of Zn content on properties of Cu/SAC0307+xZn/Al joint by ultrasonic-assisted at low-temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The ultrasonic assisted soldering joint of Cu/SAC0307+xZn powder /Al (x=0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%) at low temperature was studied. In this study, SAC0307 particles of 25-38μm were used as the main solder, and zinc particles of 1μm was mixed as the final solder. The soldered was heated to 180 °C in environmental atmosphere under the ultrasonic-assisted, and bonding of Cu/Al was successfully achieved. The results show that a complete and continuous Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> compound was formed at the Cu-side interface, and a solid solution was formed between the base metal and Zn at the aluminum side. In the absence of Zn, the shear strength of joints was only 2.44MPa. When the content of Zn was 30%, the Zn particles were bonded tightly with SAC particles under the action of ultrasound, and the shear strength of joints reached the maximum with 19.23MPa, which is 688.1% higher than that of the joint without Zn.

articleTitle: In-situ observation of microscale crack-tip strain field evolution in underfill with different toughening agents via SEM-DIC coupled method
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, a digital image correlation (DIC) based strain mapping technology was combined with scanning electron microscope (SEM) to track the crack-tip strain field evolution with sub-micron spatial resolution and sub-nanometer displacement accuracy. The crack-tip strain field evolution at a microscale was established on single edge notch bend (SENB) testing through a miniature loading platform in SEM. The SEM-DIC coupled method were used to investigate the effect of filler and toughening agent on the crack-tip strain field evolution of underfill.

articleTitle: Study on the effects of surface hydroxyl of silica fillers on the mechanical properties of underfills
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the flip-chip bump becomes smaller, the filler in underfill becomes nano-sized silica particles. However, there are few studies on the influence of the surface chemical state of silica on the mechanical properties of underfills. To explore this point, we prepared calcined and uncalcined SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, respectively, and then used them to fabricate two types of epoxy-based composites. And we compared the mechanical and thermal properties of two different composite materials. We found that the -OH-free SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> filled composite materials have better properties. The SEM image of the cross-section shows that the compatibility of -OH-free SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with epoxy resin matrix is better. Therefore, the surface hydroxyl groups of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> have a deteriorated effect on the reliability of the underfills. Finally, the reasons were explored through section analysis and thermodynamic analysis.

articleTitle: Effects of Porosity on Thermal Resistance Aging at Submicron Silver Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The thermally conductive silver adhesive is widely used as a thermal interface material for thermal management of electronic device packaging. In engineering applications, the evolution of holes inside the silver adhesive interface seriously affects its service life. In this paper, we designed high-temperature accelerated aging experiments for submicron silver adhesive interfaces. The evolution of the pores during interfacial aging was characterized by X-ray scanning and scanning electron microscopy and counting the porosity. The temperature fields of interfaces with different porosities were simulated using finite element simulation. Both experimental and simulation results show that the increase in porosity accelerates the aging of the silver-glue interface. When the porosity is increased to 30%, the simulated equivalent thermal conductivity reduces by 52.50%, and the experimentally tested interfacial thermal resistance increases by 71.58%. The experimental test results of the interfacial thermal resistance are more significant than the simulated results, indicating that porosity is not the only factor influencing accelerated interfacial aging. It provides a theoretical and experimental basis for further research on porosity accelerated aging of silver adhesive interfaces.

articleTitle: Research on Genetic Algorithm for Feedforward Parameter Tuning in XY motion platform
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of semiconductor industry, the precision of chip needs to be higher and higher. To meet these needs, XY motion platforms with high precision and high speed are widely used in semiconductor packaging and other industries. For XY platform, it must have the characteristics of high precision positioning, high speed, high acceleration and smooth movement to improve the precision of processed products. Permanent magnet synchronous linear motor has been widely used in the field of microelectronics packaging. It has the advantages of fast speed, high precision and large thrust. But because the motion is easily affected by nonlinear effect and external interference, the traditional PID control method is difficult to meet the high speed and high precision motion control requirements. In order to solve this problem, a compound control method of "feedforward + feedback" is proposed in this paper. In this method, the planned velocity, acceleration and acceleration are put into the feedforward controller to generate feedforward control signals to achieve fast response and high precision position tracking of the system. At the same time, genetic algorithm is introduced to automatically adjust the three feedforward parameters to obtain the optimal feedforward parameter values. On this basis, the high speed and high precision servo system is established, and the third order S-curve position planning algorithm is adopted. Through the design of individual fitness function in the algorithm, the dynamic or static segment of the system can be optimized with bias according to the different motion occasions of the motor. The mathematical model of permanent magnet linear motor is also established and Simulink model is used for simulation. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the robustness and fast response ability of the system, reduce the static and dynamic errors of the system, and provide a reliable technical support for the application of permanent magnet synchronous linear motor in the field of microelectronics packaging.

articleTitle: Effect of isopropyl alcohol, acetic acid and sodium dodecyl sulfate on the etching rate and surface roughness of Z-cut quartz etched by BOE solution
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Quartz crystals, with their unique piezoelectric, mechanical, and electrical insulation properties, are a popular choice for Micro-Electro-Mechanical System (MEMS) resonators. Z-cut quartz, in particular, is the most promising for fabricating microsensors and microactuators because of its high etching rate. Wet etching is the most common patterning process for quartz, and the buffered oxide etch (BOE) solution is the commonly used etchant, but its low etching rate and high surface roughness of the etched quartz blanks can affect the electrical properties of the subsequently fabricated quartz devices. To address this issue, three additives were tested: isopropyl alcohol (IPA), glacial acetic acid, and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Each additive was added at varying concentrations ranging from 5% v/v to 20% v/v, while the etching temperature was maintained at 80±1°C. The BOE solution was used as a mixture of 49 wt% HF and 40 wt% NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F with a volume ratio of 1:6. The study investigated the effects of the different additives with different concentrations on the etching rate and surface morphology of quartz. The results indicated that all three additives contributed to accelerating the etching rate and reducing the surface roughness of quartz to a certain degree. However, excessively high additive concentrations could lead to poor etching results. The addition of 10% v/v IPA to the BOE solution resulted in the fastest etching rate, increasing it from 10.71µm/h to 27.73µm/h. On the other hand, the lowest surface roughness occurred when 15% v/v SDS was added to the BOE solution, reducing the quartz surface roughness from 416nm to 125nm, which is approximately two-thirds of the original value. This finding presents a promising new approach to elevate the surface quality of etched quartz, with potential implications for the further development of quartz MEMS devices.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Temperature Cycle Failure at MLCC Welding End
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC) are common passive devices in electronic devices, consisting of three parts: inner electrode, ceramic layer, and end electrode. They are a monolithic structure based on the working principle of flat plate capacitors. MLCC has many advantages, such as wide capacity range, good frequency characteristics, high temperature and pressure resistance, small size, long life, low cost, and so on. It is widely used in industries such as automatic instruments, digital household appliances, automotive appliances, communications, and computers. MLCC is one of the largest passive components currently used, mainly for oscillation, coupling, and filter bypass circuits in various types of electronic equipment. Therefore, studying the reliability of MLCC welding is of great significance for improving the stability and reliability of electronic equipment. Based on finite element simulation, this paper simulates the temperature cycle at the welding end of MLCC. Due to the influence of thermal stress, inelastic strain occurs in the solder. The results show that the highest strain occurs in a thin solder layer below the capacitor, and after 900 temperature cycles, the weld end failure phenomenon occurs. The structure MLCC is produced through a high-temperature co fired ceramic production line and temperature cycle tests are conducted. The simulation and experimental results are basically consistent, Compared to traditional test methods, simulation has the advantages of short time, low cost, and being able to locate specific failure locations. Based on the simulation results, control and optimization of design improvements, process methods, and assembly and welding processes are conducted to improve the reliability of MLCC welding.

articleTitle: Micro Solder Defect Inspection Using Infrared Sequence and Deep Learning Omni-scale CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The chip on PCBA is developing towards miniaturization and high density. It becomes more difficult to detect micro solder bump defects inside the electronic package and soldering defects cause 71% of electronic package problems. However, fault diagnosis in the industrial manufacturing scenario is more complex and diverse involving the detection and location of solder bump defects at the IC level. As an attractive option to package inspection, X-ray may seriously affect the service life of ICs. Our group proposed a nondestructive diagnosis method on the basis of active thermography. In the recorded thermal image, the solder ball was segmented for the classification analysis. Due to the large size of PCBA, the narrow gap laser is limited to industrial applications. Because of the inefficiency and low identification rate of current detection, here we propose a detection method using infrared thermal imaging and Omni-scale CNN deep learning algorithm. We take the real chip as the experimental target. The infrared thermal sequence is collected to analyze the temperature evolution of different defect types. We use the target region segmentation to extract features to distinguish the invisible solder defects in infrared images. With the hyperparameter optimization, the Omni-scale CNN classification model realizes efficient and highly accurate detection of different solder (400μm-500μm) defect types.

articleTitle: Comparison of electroless plating interconnection of different reducing agent systems
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The interconnection between a chip and a package substrate plays a critical role in microelectronic packaging. Traditional advanced packaging methods often involve high temperatures and high pressures, which can potentially damage the chip's internal structure and compromise the reliability of solder joints. In recent years, the concept of chemical deposition has been proposed as a means to achieve low-temperature, pressure-free interconnections by depositing interconnect metal between the chip and the package substrate. However, the reducing agent traditionally used in chemical deposition, primarily formaldehyde, poses risks to both the natural environment and human health. This study aims to identify a harmless and environmentally friendly reducing agent suitable for electroless plating interconnection. Two reducing agent systems, sodium hypophosphite and glyoxylic acid, are examined, comparing their coating morphology, plating speed, electrochemical properties, and coating quality. The study utilizes a microfluidic channel device to conduct electroless plating interconnections, exploring the influence of flow fields on the two reducing agent systems. The results indicate that in static plating baths, the sodium hypophosphite system exhibits a faster plating speed, and due to the presence of reactivator nickel sulfate, which results in the inclusion of some nickel in the coating. On the other hand, the glyoxylic acid system produces a flat coating with smaller grains, better uniformity, pure copper without impurities, albeit with a slower plating speed and lower plating solution stability. In the microfluidic channel, the solder joints formed by the sodium hypophosphite system exhibit some holes, while the glyoxylic acid system, with its spherical shape at the top of the copper column of the chip, forms hole-free interconnect solder joints. Overall, for meeting the requirements of low resistance and high accuracy demanded by microelectronic interconnection, the glyoxylic acid system demonstrates better performance as a reducing agent system.

articleTitle: Thermal Cycle Reliability of Microwave Components in CBGA Package with Different Dispensing Methods for Spaceborne Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of active plased array antannas towards miniaturization, high integration and lightweight, there is an inevitable shift from modularization to system level package (SIP) for microwave components. Ceramic ball grid array (CBGA) is one of the most common device packaging methods, and it has become the preferred packaging method for microwave components such as T/R modules. Due to their extensive use in commercial applications, the thermal cycling characteristics of CBGA and other SIPs have been extensively reported in the literature. However, very limited data is available for thermal cycling behavior of microwave components with CBGA package commonly used for spaceborne applications. This paper analyzes and investigates the solder joint reliability of CBGA packaging devices with different dispensing methods under thermal cycles (-50°C~100°C). Optical microscopy (OM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to study the crack growth and failure analysis of CBGA packages with and without adhesive. The results demonstrated that a large CTE adhesive (adhesive A) can actually cause earlier failure than packages without adhesive reinforcement. CBGA packages with edge-bond adhesive C and corner staking adhesive B can improve thermal cycle reliability. A CTE almost matching the CTE for printed circuit board (PCB) and ceramic substrates proved to be the most effective in improving board-level reliability of microwave components. Edge-bond adhesive C provides 3~4 times improvement of temperature cycle life compared to be the no-edge bonding condition. Moreover, long L-type adhesive can improve the board-level reliability of CBGA more effectively than the short L-type adhesive.

articleTitle: A Lossy Filter Using Quarter-mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide and Coplanar Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A novel lossy bandpass filter is designed by using quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide and coplanar waveguide in this paper. Compared with the traditional substrate integrated waveguide cavity resonator, a quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW)is utilized to decrease the filter dimension by 75%. This structure can further reduce the overall volume, allowing for better design freedom in practical applications. Two coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission lines across the cavity are added to the filter to improve the upper stopband of the filter. Firstly, a second-order lossless filter is designed using a hybrid structure of QMSIW and CPW. Then a second-order lossy filter in the form of insertion resistance coupling is investigated. The center frequency of both filters is 5GHz. For the lossless filter, its insertion loss is 0.4dB, with the relative fractional bandwidth of 35% from 4.6 to 5.3GHz, and its return loss is greater than 27dB. After loading a resistor coupling for the lossy filter leading to 1dB insertion loss, the relative fractional bandwidth increases to 40% with passband between 4.5 and 5.39GHz, and the return loss is better than 33dB. It is obviously found that the bandwidth for the lossy filter increases nearly 200MHz, and a 6dB return loss within the passband is improved at the expense of 0.6dB insertion loss in the passband by introducing resistor coupling, which gives rise to an improved passband and sideband performance.

articleTitle: Case Analysis and Improvement of Silver Migration in Resistors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A large system has successively found that the output of the control module is abnormal and the fault performance is similar. After troubleshooting, the problem is located in an abnormality in a resistor of a certain type of board. Analysis was conducted on the abnormal resistor. Through surface observation, it was found that the surface of the resistor was poorly covered with conformal coating, and there were black foreign matters near one end of the resistor. Scanning electron microscopy and energy dispersive spectroscopy analysis confirmed that it was a silver migration, and some of it was sulfurized. Further, the metallographic section analysis found that there was a gap between the resistance electrode end and the surface covering layer, forming a channel for silver migration, and this poor bonding was commonly found in the resistance exclusion of similar packaging structures on the board. Ion chromatography analysis showed a high ion content on the plate surface. Therefore, we can conclude that due to inadequate protection of the electrode end of the resistor, silver migration in a corrosive environment leads to the failure of the resistor, resulting in abnormal module output. The failure mechanism has been verified through high temperature and humidity tests. Finally, based on the failure mechanism, the article proposes measures to strengthen the environmental corrosion resistance of the control module. First of all, it is necessary to strengthen the screening and verification of the resistance to corrosion of resistor materials, and ensure that the area where the resistor is located is fully covered with conformal coating, so as to prevent the migration of silver in the resistor in the environment.

articleTitle: The Effect of Etching Lead Frame on QFN Package Delamination
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Package delamination is a key concern in semiconductor industry, such as lead frame (LF) to epoxy molding compound (EMC) and die attach material to EMC delamination. When interface delamination occurs, it will become sensitive to mechanical force and moisture can penetrate into the package, resulting in mold cracks or corrosion, thus affecting package reliability.Lead frame material is a key factor on delamination performance, a lot of effort been spent in LF industry on reduce delamination, such as surface roughening, LF dimple, V groove, etc. For Quad Flat No Lead (QFN) package, the mechanical force applied onto LF to EMC interface with blade cutting, so the singulation process has a critical influence on package delamination.In this study, delamination reduction is studied with QFN as test vehicle. Focusing on Cu raw material mechanical property and LF connection bar dimension influence on delamination. The result shows that: (1). Cu raw material mechanical properties, such as tensile strength and yield strength show obvious correlation to delamination, the lower tensile strength the least delamination; (2). The narrow connection bar and thin connection bar can reduce the blade mechanical force between the LF and EMC during singulation, thus narrow connection bar width has less delamination performance; (3). Even for normal PPF LF, still need to pay attention to surface roughness, higher roughness helps to reduce package delamination.

articleTitle: Suppression of Kirkendall Voids at the Interface of Sn/nc-Cu Solder Joint
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electroplated Cu film plays an important role in electronics, communications, aerospace and other fields. With DC plating, nanocrystalline Cu (nc-Cu) film was prepared by a new plating solution and commercial nanocrystalline Cu (cnc-Cu) film was prepared by a commercial plating solution in this paper. Sn/Cu solder joints formed by reflowing pure tin on the Cu films at 250 °C for 1 min were aged at 150 °C for 50 h, 200 h and 500 h. It was found that no Kirkendall voids formed at the Sn/nc-Cu interface, while a large number of Kirkendall voids formed at the Sn/cnc-Cu interface. More impurities in the cnc-Cu could reduce the vacancy formation energy and then promote the aggregation of vacancies to form voids. Impurities could also hinder the growth of Cu grains, which could produce more grain boundaries and promote the generation of Kirkendall voids at the boundaries. Therefore, the Sn/Cu solder joints prepared by nc-Cu showed significant suppression of Kirkendall voids, which should be benefit to improve the reliability of electronic products in service.

articleTitle: Optimization of stress and related parameters of BGA solder joint with void defect under torsional load
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the BGA welding spot model with void defect is established by Ansys, and the stress simulation analysis and experimental verification are carried out by applying torsion load. The influence of BGA welding spot void size, welding pad size and PCB thickness on the torsion stress strain of welding spot with void is analyzed; Taking the void size, pad size and PCB thickness as variables, nine groups of solder joint models with different horizontal combinations are designed by orthogonal experiment method, and the corresponding torsion stress of solder joint is obtained. Based on the experimental data, the range and variance optimization analysis of the structural parameters of solder joint is carried out. The results show that the positions of the model stress are close to the torsion load, and the maximum stress of BGA welding spot with void defect occurs at the edge of welding spot; Under 95% confidence level, the void size of welding spot has the most significant influence on the welding spot; When the void diameter is 0.07mm, the pad diameter is 0.46mm and the PCB thickness is 1.4mm, it is the optimal welding spot structure parameter combination, and the maximum torsion stress of the optimal welding spot is reduced by 4.946Mpa.

articleTitle: Full-spectrum White Light-emitting Phosphor-in-Glass for blue LED chips by adding Green-Emitting CaY2ZrScAl3O12:Ce3+ Phosphor
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the results of low color-correlated temperatures (CCT) and high color rendering indexes (CRI), white light-emitting diodes (WLEDs) coated with phosphor are ideal for energy-saving and environmental protection solid-statelight source. To further optimize the optical performance of WLEDs, we prepared CaY<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>ZrScAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> green phosphor by solid-phase sintering, and the efforts of doping ratio of Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> in green phosphor were studied. X-ray diffraction (XRD), SEM, Photoluminescence (PL) and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) were used to investigate the crystal phase, microstructure, and photoluminescence properties. CaY<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>ZrScAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> :Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> phosphor can produces green light in a wide emission band from 440 to 700 nm which making up the "cyan gap", thus, Phosphor-in-glass (PiG) with full-visible-spectrum emission was successfully prepared by incorporating commercial CaAlSiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>:Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> red phosphor and CaY<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>ZrScAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> green phosphor in glass matrix at a low sintering temperature, the InGaN blue LED combined with this PiG demonstrates high-quality white light with a high CRI(Ra=92.4) and low correlated CCT(4358K). The results show that WLED using this PiG has a huge potential in full spectrum illumination.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of novel doped heterostructured electromagnetic shielding packaging materials for Current sensor chip applications
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation not only disrupt the use of equipment such as sensors, electronic components and precision instruments and affects their normal operation, but also leads to the leakage of important data and even reduces their reliability. It is still challenging to significantly improve the anti-electromagnetic interference performance from the chip packaging material level. Doped polyaniline (PANI) is considered as one of the most potent electromagnetic shielding materials as its easy synthesis, stable performance, unique chemical and electromagnetic properties.to address the technical challenges of chip anti-interference in complex electromagnetic environment and make full use of the advantages of doped PANI in electromagnetic shielding, this thesis uses doped PANI, carbon fiber, metal particles, etc. to prepare heterogeneous structure composite electromagnetic shielding packaging materials. Through the modification of the material and the construction of the shielding structure, the influence of the content of functional components, the size and structure of the reflective cavity on its electromagnetic properties is systematically studied, and the mechanism of the regulation of the electromagnetic shielding performance of the material is revealed. A series of CF/PANI heterogeneous structure composite electromagnetic shielding materials were obtained by in situ polymerization of carbon fiber surface coated with PANI, through optimization of components, structure and properties. Based on the excellent electrical properties of PANI and the characteristic of no electromagnetic loss, the reflective layer is constructed inside the material, and the effects of carbon fiber and metal particle content and morphology on the conductivity and dielectric behavior of CF/PANI are systematically investigated to enhance the dielectric loss and absorption loss of the material and improve the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of the material through multiple reflective interfaces of electromagnetic waves. With the increase of carbon fiber content, the conductivity of the material shows a trend of increasing and then decreasing, and the change of skinning depth is the opposite. When the mass ratio of carbon fiber to PANI was 6:4, the sample has the highest conductivity (10.32 ± 0.29 S/cm) and the Electromagnetic shielding efficiency values achieved 63dB. The above excellent performance gives the CF/PANI /EP composite material potential applications in the packaging of magnetic sensors, current sensing chips, SRAM and other chips.

articleTitle: Finite Element Simulation Study of the Effects of Kirkendall Voids in IMC Layer on Interfacial Crack and Reliability of Cu–Sn Solder Joint
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The past decade has seen increasing attention to Cu–Sn solid-liquid interdiffusion (SLID) bonding technology, which can be applied to achieve bonding at a low temperature and the bonded interconnect (joint) is capable of withstanding high service temperatures. However, due to different diffusion rates between Cu and Sn atoms, Kirkendall voids arise in interfacial intermetallic compound (IMC) layers, then crack may initiate in the region with large Kirkendall voids near the Cu/IMC interface, which has become a serious concern for the SLID bonding technology. In the present work, the propagation behavior of crack caused by voids at the Cu/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn interfaces is studied by three-dimensional (3D) finite element analysis via virtual crack closure technique (VCCT). By calculating fracture mechanics parameters (such as energy release rate, G) at the crack tip, the influence of Kirkendall void distribution and different phase thicknesses in the solder joint on the tendency of crack propagation is investigated. The effects of crack length and temperature on fracture propagation tendency are also studied. The simulation results manifest that crack at the interface of Cu/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn is more likely to propagate than inside intermetallic compound (Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn) layer. Moreover, a void-type crack has a higher energy release rate than an interfacial crack. The average value of G increases significantly with expansion of the void area, while G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> tends to decrease at the crack tip. The increase in thickness of both Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> layers promotes the propagation of crack. Besides, the thickness of Cu layer also influences crack propagation greatly. G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> increases with increasing thickness of Cu (UBM) layer from 0.5 μm to 1.1 μm, while decreasing rapidly as Cu layer continues to thicken.

articleTitle: TGV filling process based on low temperature conductive silver paste
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Through Glass Vias (TGV) interconnection has a wide range of applications in three-dimensional packaging and integrated passive devices due to its excellent electrical properties. The nano conductive silver paste as a common bonding conductive material has good bonding strength with glass and excellent electrical properties, which is a promising alternative to electroplating to fill through-holes with a depth to width ratio of 10:1 or more. In this paper, we demonstrated the feasibility of filling silver paste in 100μm diameter, 400μm deep through-holes and tested the filling effect of the nano-silver paste inside the glass through-hole. Daisy chain and coplanar waveguide structures were fabricated on the glass surface by printing and tested to obtain the I-V curves and S-parameters. The resistivity of the silver paste in the through-hole is 2.56×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> Ω•m and the forward transmission coefficient of the coplanar waveguide with the through-hole structure at 3.3Ghz is -0.11dB, which fits well with the simulated value and proves its good property. Combined with simple process flow and low process cost, paste filling process has great potential for applications in 3D packaging and integrated passive devices.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Interface Materials on Thermal Performance and Reliability of Large Size Flip Chips
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of AI and high-performance processor, chip power consumption and power density continue to increase, and the heat dissipation of electronic packages faces great challenges. Thermal interface materials (TIMs) are used between the chip and the heatsink to improve the interface contact by filling the gap and exhaust air. Therefore, it is important to improve the heat dissipation performance of package. In addition to the excellent thermal properties, TIMs are also required to have good reliability. Due to package warpage and other mechanical stresses, a TIM will experience a range of compressive and tensile loads during package assembly and end use conditions, which even cause delamination and cracking in TIMs.In this work, we created a typical flip chip ball grid array (FCBGA) simulation model with a package size of 52.5 × 52.5mm. ANSYS ICEPAK was used for thermal analysis to discuss the effects of thermal conductivity, bond line thickness (BLT), coverage and other parameters of TIMs on chip heat dissipation performance. Besides, a Die-TIM-Lid sandwich model was established to investigate the effect of porosity and void size on junction temperature and hotspot concentration. Finally, quarter FCBGA models based on finite element method were employed to analyse the stress of TIMs on large size package. The distance between the lower surface of lid and the upper surface of die was measured to obtain the BLT.

articleTitle: Additive Fabrication of 3D Surface Conformal Circuits Using a Modified Screen-Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 3D surface conformal circuits are widely utilized in the fabrication of communication, automotive, medical and confidential electronic products. Special techniques, like the three-dimensional molded interconnect devices (3D-MID) technology, have been developed for manufacturing of the conformal circuits on the surfaces of injection molded plastic structures with complicated 3D shapes. However, the 3D-MID fabrication of conformal circuits involves an electro-/chemical plating process. Due to environmental protection requirements and its incompatibility with traditional electronic manufacturing processes, the application of this technique is largely limited. In this work, surface conformal circuits were fabricated additively by a modified screen-printing technology. An adaptive partition principle was proposed for reconstructing the complex 3D structure surfaces. Flexible screen receptacles were used instead of the traditional rigid ones. Nano-silver pastes were applied for the circuit printing. The obtained conformal circuit has a length range of 142~300 mm and a maximum aspect ratio of 320:1. The circuit thickness could be controlled in the range of 3-10 μm . Line width deviation was less than ± 50 μm. Linewidth consistency was better than ± 43 μm. The resistivity of the connection wires printed by the nano-silver paste were 16.2 ± 0.2 μΩ•cm. The curvatures of the 3D surfaces covered by the conformal circuits changed from -1000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> to 1000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. After being stored at - 40 °C and 150 °C for 72 hours, no obvious deformation, peel-off and degradation in electrical properties were detected. By using conformal circuits, the structural design of an LED luminaire has been improved to achieve miniaturization and better heat dissipation. The modified screen-printing technology presented is a cheap and reliable method for fabricating complex 3D conformal circuits and it is well compatible to traditional electronic manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: A novel lead-free NaNbO3-based relaxation ferroelectric ceramics for energy storage application
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In order to stay away from fossil fuels and avoid the inherent unpredictability of clean energy, it is necessary to combine energy collection technology with energy storage equipment. In energy storage devices, batteries, electrochemical supercapacitors and electrostatic capacitors can be found everywhere. Currently, dielectric energy storage capacitors with high power density and high energy storage efficiency are required to meet the requirements of portable electronic devices. The materials used for dielectric energy storage capacitors mainly include ceramics, polymers, glass ceramics, ceramic/polymer composites and so on. Compared with other dielectric energy storage materials, dielectric ceramics have the advantages of large dielectric constant, low dielectric loss, medium breakdown electric field, good temperature stability, and good fatigue resistance. Therefore, dielectric energy storage ceramics have good application prospects. As a typical relaxation ferroelectric material in dielectric ceramic materials, it has the characteristics of electric field induced phase transition. It can be applied to portable electronic devices with high energy density and high power density. However, from the perspective of current technological development, it is still challenging to develop a lead-free relaxation ferroelectric material with appropriate power density and breakdown field strength. In this paper, based on the NaNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, (1-x)Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.97</inf>Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.01</inf>NbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-x(Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)(Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> were prepared using traditional solid-state sintering. It can be observed that the surface grains of the materials are tightly arranged and have low porosity by SEM. At room temperature and at a frequency of 10 Hz, the hysteresis loops of different samples were measured by the ferroelectric tester. Adjust the external electric field to 410 kV/cm, When x=0.06, the component exhibits the maximum effective energy storage density W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rec</inf> is 2.62 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the maximum energy storage efficiency η is 84.31%. At a frequency of 10 Hz, adjust the temperature to 30—80 °C, test the corresponding bipolar P-E curves, the prepared relaxation ferroelectric ceramic materials still maintains a good and no obvious deformation hysteresis loop, and the energy storage efficiency fluctuates by less than 10%. At a temperature of 25 °C, adjust the frequencies to 10—250 Hz, test the corresponding bipolar P-E curves, the prepared relaxation ferroelectric ceramic materials still maintains a good hysteresis loop without obvious deformation, and the energy storage efficiency fluctuates by less than 6%, so the materials have good stability of temperature and frequency. As mentioned above, the prepared ceramics have good prospects in energy storage applications.

articleTitle: Ripple-control Multi-port Step-down Power Converter Design in Outdoor Power Supply Application
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Outdoor power supplies have become increasingly popular in recent years owing to the increasing popularity of outdoor camping and hiking. To convert the energy stored in lithium batteries into various portable forms of consumption, many power converter topology and control strategies are being proposed and studied recently. The virtue of lightweight, adaptive, stable should be taken into consideration in power converter design according to special needs of outdoor power supplies. In this paper, a ripple-control multi-port step-down power converter is proposed. The proposed design converts 42V~56V(16xLiFePO4) from lithium battery bank to a 21V~28V first stage output for charge controller (SW3516/SW3526) and a 12V second stage output for cigarette lighter output. The topology incorporates a 2:1 step-down charge pump and introduces a parasitic CCM Buck converter to provide two outputs of different voltage levels without introducing additional active circuitry, thus shrinks the overall solution size, cost and EMI emission. The primary output is optimized for efficiency, while the secondary output is optimized for load regulation. A ripple injection circuit is used to indirectly sense inductor current, which is a Thevenin equivalent of the CF-type3(parallel RC-filter) feedback controller, being capable of effectively predict inductor current. This virtual peak current control method greatly reduces output ripple without introducing resistive losses commonly associated with a true current sensor while preserving transient responsiveness. LTspice simulation is used to compare and analyze the proposed converter topology with a comparison set in terms of ripple injection feedback and loop control in details. Thanks to the superior performance of the proposed power converter, a small 3x2.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (5cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding connectors) prototype based on GreenPAK programmable CMIC SLG46855 is fabricated, which is capable of delivering up to 288W of output at a relatively high efficiency, performing high coincidence with theory analysis and simulation. This paper not only gives a practical solution for portable outdoor power supply application but also provides compatibility and extensibility for other multi-port ripple-control based converter design.

articleTitle: Simulation on Microstructural Evolution under Electromigration in Backside Power Delivery Network
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: A state-of-art design, so-called backside power delivery network (BS-PDN), has been proposed for future logic scaling enablement. Nevertheless, electromigration (EM) can be a potential risk causing an increase of electric resistance or even an open circuit failure (OCF) inside the BS-PDN. Here, we use a phase field model to investigate the interplay between microstructural evolution and EM damage in the BS-PDNs. One typical configuration of a BS-PDN, which consists of a nano through-silicon-via (n-TSV), a buried power rail (BPR) and a local metal interconnect (LMI), is referenced to construct the model geometry. The areas near the cathode side interface of each component are regarded as the critical regions where most of EM damages develop. The grain structures in the critical regions, the anisotropic grain boundary (GB) mobility and the material choice for BPR are considered as influential factors on EM reliability. Three criteria on the EM reliability can be put forward, amongst which the most important criterion is the material choice for the BPR because the time to the OCF increases significantly in the BS-PDN with Ru-BPR. The other two criteria are the number of GBs intersecting with the BPR-LMI interface and whether or not these GBs are high angle GBs.

articleTitle: Effect of Er and Ni-CNTs on the interfacial reaction and growth behavior of Sn58Bi/Cu intermetallic compound layers
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The interface reaction of Sn58Bi solder with 0.1% Er (0%, 0.01%, 0.03%, 0.05% and 0.1% ni-cnts) was studied after refluxing and solid aging. The results show that the growth of IMC layer is inhibited by Er and Ni-CNTs. After aging at 100 °C for 200 and 400 h, the addition of Er and Ni-CNTs inhibited the growth of total IMC layer and Cu3Sn layer was inhibited by the addition of Er and Ni-CNTs. During aging process, the thickness of interface (Cu,Ni) 6Sn5 layer under Ni-CNTs and Er addition is always thinner than that under Er addition, because Ni-CNTs can effectively reduce the CTE of SnBi solder. The reason why the growth rate of Cu3Sn with Er and Ni-CNTs is lower than that with Er alone is that the stability of (Cu, Ni) 6Sn5 is improved with the increase of Ni content in Ni-CNTs. In addition, the IMC growth rate of composite weld decreases with the increase of Ni-CNTs content.

articleTitle: CPU Socket Interposer Component Level and PCBA Manufacturability Study and Part 2: iNEMI 2023 Board Assembly – CPU Socket Technology Roadmap
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This article is Part 1 and Part 2 of a series of studies on a new generation of CPU socket challenges and component interconnect technology for high-end computer product applications. These products encompass computer server and data storage for cloud computing applications at the Data Center as well as core routers for service providers, edge, and branch routers for enterprise networking companies. All these cloud computing products require high data speed in Gigabytes per second and high signal integrity for the massive mobile users and IoT applications whenever and wherever the user wishes to connect. As the finer 3nm semiconductor process is progressively migrated into mass production in the chip fabrication industry to enhance transistor density, increase speed and lower the power consumption of the chip, there are great technical challenges in component packaging design with the circuit board. With CPU and memory frequency requirements increasing, the signal integrity challenge is exerted from differential signaling in parallel buses, the robustness of design and manufacturability of the new generation of socket interposer are the keys for the success of electronic evolution.The purpose of the Part 1 study is to look into the next generation of CPU socket design correlation with its interconnection system and PCBA manufacturability. Socket pin configuration related to pin true position and common bent pin issue due to transportation stress and material handling are very critical variables. Socket packaging design especially the cover will be carefully examined to avoid laser light leaking/reflection issue so as to avoid pick and place problems in device placement in the PCBA process. Past experience tells us the contamination at the contact pin interface such as particulate, process material residue and oxidation are very important variables to be controlled to avoid contact resistance issues. Socket material selection and mechanical construction are major contributors to package flatness and correlated warpage between the socket package and PCB. This correlated warpage will be assessed to avoid causing many very difficult soldering issues such as head-in-pillow and solder bridging. Thermal aging of socket material due to environmental stress and CPU operational temperature will be studied by the accelerated thermal cycling test while contact resistance between socket contact and CPU pad is under real-time monitoring when a daisy chained test vehicle is running in the environment chamber. Meanwhile there is a trend of using direct solder attach to interconnect CPU chip with PCB directly. The warpage problem from correlated chip and PCB causing high defect rate in PCBA manufacturing will be also reviewed.The purpose of the Part 2 study is to look into the next generation of CPU socket design correlation with its interconnection system and PCBA manufacturability through a technical forum in the iNEMI (International Manufacturing Initiative) 2023 Board Assembly--CPU socket interconnect technology roadmap. A team of experts from CPU suppliers, socket material researchers, ODM companies initiated a review to brainstorm key technology trends for next ten years, to identify the technical needs, gaps, and challenges, and then propose potential solutions for the major technical issues. Over the next decade, there is a projected exponential increase in computer data rate in Gb/s due to the IoT from the massive mobile users in the field for their whenever and wherever needs. In such a trend, the socket pin count will be in exponential growth over time, mainly driven by the increase in total computer power, memory and input/output signaling bandwidth. With this exponential increase in pin count, there is a trend to push the similar increase in LGA socket mechanical loading. This increase in loading affects hardware complexity, costs and socket keep out area on the board which in turn could impact overall computation density per motherboard. The data rate increase overtime is forcing lower height sockets to meet the high speed signaling integrity requirement. This reduction in height can promote more complexity to the LGA pin design to meet mechanical requirements as well as forcing larger warpage in socket which can be an interconnect issue at the LGA and motherboard interface.

articleTitle: Green and high-efficiency CMP Slurry for Cu planarization
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization/polishing (CMP) is an important process for Through-silicon-via (TSV) technology in 2.5D and 3D integration and is the only technology that can balance the global and local surface planarization. In recent years, there is an urgent need to develop new CMP slurry with environmental friendly and non-toxic components because traditional CMP slurry contains strong acids, alkalis, or harmful and toxic chemicals, which are detrimental to the environment, and harmful to the public health. The low or none toxic amino acids and other substances may be the promising candidates to replace the harmful chemicals normally used in the CMP slurries.In this paper, we proposed a CMP slurry with high material removal rate and non-toxic chemicals for Cu planarization. In this green slurry, silica sol was used as the abrasive, and the amino acids and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) were used as the coordination and the oxidization regents, respectively. Adenine (AD) and chitosan (CTS) are used as corrosion inhibitors. The experimental results of CMP showed that the material removal rate of copper could be stabilized at about 1100 nm/min with the synergistic effect of glycine (Gly) and sarcosine (Sar), and Sar could also promote the post-CMP cleaning by modifying the copper surface. The material removal rate of copper decreased rapidly (from ~1000 to ~ 400 nm/min) after the introduction of a single corrosion inhibitor AD, and the material removal rate was effectively stabilized by using a mixture of AD and CTS, and the combination of 0.20 wt% AD and 0.20 wt% CTS corrosion inhibitors resulted in a material removal rate of 621.27 nm/min. The surface morphology of the copper was determined by atomic force microscopy, and the surface roughness could be significantly reduced via BTA utilization (from ~ 4.75 to ~ 1.4 nm), and then was further reduced to less than 1 nm by using the combined inhibitor, i.e., AD and CTS. The results of static etch experiments showed that the introduction of Sar in the slurry can effectively inhibit the over-corrosion of the copper surface and homogenize the corrosion pits on the etched copper surface. Electrochemical analysis showed that both AD and CTS can effectively coordinate with copper cations and form passivation films to protect the surface. The qualitative composition XPS analysis for the high-resolution Cu 2p3/2 spectra revealed that the coordinated Cu-Gly, Cu-Sar, Cu-AD, Cu-CTS and Cu-BTA were present in the corresponding solutions. Therefore, high material removal rate (~ 600 nm/min) and low surface roughness (<1 nm) after Cu CMP could be achieved by applying the developed green and high-efficiency slurry composed of promising complexing and inhibition agents.

articleTitle: Molecular dynamics simulation of copper paste sintering for chip interconnection
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Micron or nano-scale copper particles paste as a new generation of packaging materials, with low temperature sintering and high temperature service characteristics. The interconnect layer structure formed using copper paste after sintering is capable achieve unique high temperature resistance characteristics, excellent electrical conductivity, suitable for SiC chips, GaN chips and other chips using for power electronics devices. Unfortunately, the diffusion mechanism of adjacent copper particles in copper paste during sintering process in copper paste is still unclear. In this paper, we use the kinetic simulation software Lammps for different sintering processes of copper particles with different sizes, as well as the growth behavior and mean-square displacement(MSD) of the sintering neck was used, to analyze the atomic stacking condition, the distance between the centres during different sintering periods, and the atomic ordering of copper atoms with temperature. The trend of the local crystal structure changes around the copper atoms and the crystal defects during the different sintering periods were analysed using crystal structure. The result indicated that the melting point decreased with the size of the sintered copper particles decreased, so does the sintering temperature, the radius distribution function(RDF) is relative to the size of copper particle, during the sintering process, the copper particles tend to produce an amorphous structure and accelerate the densification of the voids. The growth pattern of the sintered neck is generally similar at different periods of sintering, but depend on the different sizes of copper particles. This study provides a theoretical basis for the development of copper paste sintering interconnection.

articleTitle: Solder Selection Simulation Of IGBT Module Based On Thermal - Mechanical Coupling Field
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) is a key component in power converters widely used in emerging fields such as electric vehicles, renewable energy generation, and smart grids. Solder, as a crucial part of the IGBT module packaging process, serves as both a critical connecting element within the module’s internal structure and one of the main channels for heat dissipation. However, under the influence of current and temperature loads, the solder layer may undergo irreversible changes that lead to a decrease in thermal conductivity, making it one of the vulnerable links in the packaging structure. Currently, interconnection technologies in IGBT modules mainly include soldering, transient liquid phase diffusion bonding, and nano-silver low-temperature sintering.
