Optimizing the soldering process and selecting appropriate solder materials are of great significance in improving the reliability of IGBT modules. This paper analyzes the requirements for selecting solder materials in IGBT module packaging based on the development of solder materials for IGBT modules in recent years both domestically and internationally. It conducts simulated studies on nano-silver solder, SnCu0.7 solder, Sn3.0Ag0.5Cu solder, 92.5Pb5Sn2.5Ag solder, and Sn63Pb37 solder. A three-dimensional geometric model of the IGBT is constructed based on heat conduction theory. Thermal-mechanical coupled simulations of the IGBT module are performed using the ANSYS Workbench platform, comparing the temperature distribution and mechanical properties of different solder materials in the solder layer. The heat dissipation path and thermal stress variation characteristics of different solder materials are analyzed. The research results show that the type of solder material directly affects the thermal conductivity efficiency and conduction direction of the IGBT module, thereby indirectly influencing the overall junction temperature. Among them, nano-silver solder exhibits the best thermal conductivity and excellent resistance to thermal deformation. However, the presence of intermetallic compounds (IMCs) in the 92.5Pb5Sn2.5Ag solder, Sn3.0Ag0.5Cu solder, SnCu0.7 solder, and Sn63Pb37 solder subjects the solder layer to greater thermal stress and shows more pronounced stress concentration, making the solder layer more prone to damage. These findings provide us with a new perspective on understanding the selection of solder materials for IGBT module packaging and have important guiding significance for improving its performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Life Prediction of Solder Interconnects under Harsh Thermal Cycling from Microstructural Degradation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Designing dependable solar PV systems that last a long time and function in a wide variety of temperatures in low earth orbit requires precise forecast of solder interconnect lifespans, yet useful prediction methodology has rarely been studied. Here, a strategy for measuring the solder interconnects' fatigue life was established using experimental, computational, and analytical methodologies. Thermal aging, material characterization, and thermal cycling were used to explore the physics of failure. Equilibrium liquid surface simulation and finite element modeling were used to establish the geometry of the solder interconnects, and to obtain the strain distribution. To accurately predict the lifespan of solder interconnects, microstructure evolution modeling, constitutive equation fitting, and fatigue model calibration were performed. We have demonstrated that increasing the stand-off height of solder interconnects can delay the onset of fatigue cracks and prolong total fatigue life in photovoltaic systems using this integrated approach to busbar-to-wire solder interconnects. Interconnects with large solder quantity have a long life due to slow crack propagation with low averaged plastic work, but they have about the same number of cycles to fatigue crack initiation due to relatively stable plastic strain range during heat cycling. The proposed approach could be used to motivate the design of strong interconnects in photovoltaic systems that can withstand rigorous thermal cycling.

articleTitle: Study on Defect Detection and Impact on Heat Dissipation in Nanosilver Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Sintered silver is a new interconnect material with many advantages, such as low sintering temperature, high thermal conductivity and high service temperature, which can increase the heat dissipation capacity of the silver interconnect layer and enable high power modules to be used for long term service. However, sintered silver tends to form different defects during long-term service, which can affect the module’s thermal capability. In this paper, we prefabricated different sintered silver substrates and used ANSYS Workbench to build a finite element model of the substrates for investigating the effect of the size, distribution and shape of defects in the connection interface on the thermal performance of the module, comparing the size of the thermal resistance of the connection layer between the finite element model and the actual substrate to verify the scientific and reasonable nature of the simulation results. The simulation results show that excessively large defects can seriously affect the heat distribution of the chip, causing an increase in temperature amplitude, and the difference of temperature distribution depending on the location of the defects. The computational analysis shows that as the defect size increases, the thermal conductivity of the connection layer decreases, and these effects eventually lead to an increase in the temperature of the whole module. Finally, the S-parameter network test further reveals the effect of defects on the module. The test results show that an increase in defects leads to an increase in the impedance of the module, and that the resonant frequency also tends to increase with defects. In summary, thermal model simulations for different defect levels are developed and a defect assessment method based on S-parameter analysis is proposed. Our results show that controlling the defect size and distribution is essential to optimise the thermal performance of sintered silver interconnect materials.

articleTitle: Fabrication of 45-Degree Integrated Mirrors for Three-Dimensional Board-Level Optical Interconnects Realizing Efficient Light Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Efficient (low-loss) and robust technologies for optical in- and out-coupling from integrated waveguides at different interconnection levels is a prerequisite. A suitable beam delivery scheme is required in out-of-plane coupling configurations to reduce the losses originated from the beam divergence along the free space optical path. In this work, to realize a high coupling efficiency of inter-chip connection for three-dimensional (3-D) optical interconnects, mechanical dicing process was conducted to fabricate out-of-plane mirrors for light beam turning. A 45-degree optical interface for light 90-degree beam turning into/out of the waveguide with up-turned mirrors were demonstrated. Characterizations of the surface topographies and sloping angles revealed that relatively smooth 45-degree interface was achieved. Surprisingly, the angle deviation of the 45-degree reflector was within ± 1 -degree, and the surface roughness was approach to 170 nm. A theoretical model specified for the optical link was developed to theoretically calculate the link loss of the 3-D optical interconnects based on the waveguide with 45-degree mirrors. The coupling loss of the 45-degree interface at the Tx and Rx side was experimentally investigated. The results showed that the total link loss was 7.77 dB for a 110-mm-long waveguides and the excess loss calculated for the mirror coupling was 2.56 dB for the Tx side and 2.86 dB for the Rx side. Besides, the Fresnel reflection originated from the horizontally fiber and the 90-degree end face was 0.7 dB. Misalignment tolerance results indicated that the fabricated 45-degree end face beam turning structure has relatively loose alignment requirements for the optics in the X-direction. The measured of 1 dB lateral alignment tolerance amounted to ± 17 µm in the X-direction. The functional optical performance indicated that the up-turned mirrors were suitable for practical printed circuit boards (OPCB) applications where an optical I/O-interface to couple light in or out of waveguides to surface-mounted VCSEL or photodiode was required. This work presented here also provided a promising technology to implement optical interconnects on PCBs, for realizing the anticipated high coupling efficiency 3-D interconnected optical polymer waveguide links.

articleTitle: A Thin Film Metallization Process Development for Silicon Nitride Ceramic Substrates in Power Electronics Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the power electronics packaging, the substrate is not only responsible for the electrical connection and mechanical support but also significant to the thermal management and reliability. Recently, silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) ceramic has been receiving much attention, for having excellent mechanical properties, such as high bending strength and high fracture toughness. It can significantly improve the mechanical reliability of the substrate for power electronics, under the circumstances of power cycling and thermal impact. This opens up a new research direction of high-performance power electronics substrate for silicon carbide (SiC) devices. However, the surface metallization technique of Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramic substrates is not as mature as its counterpart, such as alumina (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) or aluminum nitride (AlN) ceramics, in direct-bond copper (DBC) and direct-bond alumina (DBA) technologies. Therefore, how to implement metallization on Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramic surfaces and improve the interfacial strength of the metallization layers has become interesting topics for many researchers.In this paper, we proposed a novel thin-film process for Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramic substrate metallization, which deposited titanium as a transition layer and silver as a conductive layer by magnetron sputtering technique. Titanium was selected due to its high chemical reactivity and good diffusion performance. The titanium reaction with Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> substrate is beneficial to the increase of bonding strength between metal film layers and ceramic substrate. With low electrical resistivity and high temperature stabilities, silver is preferably selected as the conductive layer, which can be further used as a seeding layer in the electroplating process or a high-temperature bonding layer in transient liquid phase (TLP) technology. Therefore, the current work is inherently compatible with direct plated copper (DPC), silver nano-sintering and TLP technologies. In addition, various materials characterization methods have been utilized to evaluate the quality of the Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramic substrate metallization. The surface morphology and resistivity of the films were characterized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) and dual electrometry four-probe method, respectively. The interfacial strength of the thin films to Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramics was analyzed using the nano-scratch test method. By studying the effects of the variations of magnetron sputtering parameters, this work provides useful guidance for the process development of Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramic substrate metallization in the field of power electronics packaging.

articleTitle: Research on the electrical performance of flexible metal arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The demand for diverse sensors has been on a steady rise with the ongoing advancement of digital health technologies. In contrast to conventional rigid sensors, flexible sensors possess a distinctive advantage in measuring dynamic and non-planar objects, owing to their exceptional mechanical flexibility. Among them, flexible resistive sensors have been widely used in health monitoring, intelligent equipment, human-machine interaction, and other fields because of their high sensitivity, short response time, and good stability. However, the interface sensing performance between the flexible sensing layer microstructure and metal electrode layer structure was limited by function material and microstructure characteristics, which presented a saturation trend under high loads and could not satisfy the sensitivity requirements. Theoretical and numerical methods have been used to solve the problem in this article, the electrical sensing mechanism of micro metal array was revealed. Furthermore, the interface piezoresistance performance was investigated with different flexible microstructure sizes and morphology designs. Finite element (FE) method was used for multi-physics coupling analysis, the electrical properties of interconnection microstructures between flexible conductive interfaces under different load pressures were analyzed. Meanwhile, the theoretical analysis results were verified. In addition, this work also explored the electrical performance of different microstructure array morphologies by introducing a biomimetic random structure. Numerical simulation results showed that the interface interconnection structure could present high electrical sensitivity under high loads. Hence, it provides a new route and methods for the interconnection structures design of flexible sensor interface.

articleTitle: Electro-Thermal-Mechanical simulation of a three-dimensional stacked flexible circuit interconnects structure and its comparative analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the power module, smaller package size, lower parasitic inductance, higher reliability, and higher thermal dissipation capability are crucial factors in package design. In this paper, a three-dimensional stacked flexible circuit interconnection structure is designed and proposed to replace traditional wire bonding. It is compared and analyzed with the other two flexible circuit interconnection-based modules and conventional wire bonding types. The DSC structure can improve the heat dissipation capability. In the temperature cycling, the lifetime of the other three modules decreases compared to the wire bonding, and the plastic strain of all four modules is accumulated at the corners and edges of the chip. Under power cycling, the three-dimensional stacked flexible circuit interconnect module has up to four times the lifetime of the double-sided nano-silver sintered module, and the other three modules have higher power loading capacity and lower parasitic inductance than conventional modules.

articleTitle: Investigation on Transient Failure Mode of Asymmetric Trench Gate SiC MOSFET Under Single-Pulse Avalanche Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this article, the avalanche withstand capability and transient failure model of commercial 1200 V asymmetric trench gate SiC MOSFETs are investigated by experiment and simulation under single-pulse unclamped inductive switching (UIS) conditions. The limiting avalanche current and limiting avalanche energy of the device are determined by evaluating the voltage and current waveforms, the power dissipation, and the avalanche energy curves before and during avalanche failure. Then, by using the calibrated simulation model, the sequence between the critical electric field stress and critical thermal stress suffered by the device is revealed, and the transient failure mode of the device is proved to be the thermal runaway. Moreover, after decapping the failed device, the failure mode of the device is further confirmed by analyzing the failure point. Finally, by using the focused ion beam (FIB) technology, the failure mechanism of the device is confirmed as a structural rupture caused by avalanche thermal stress.

articleTitle: High-precision positioning detection technology for large-size fan-out panel-level package chips
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: During the process of large-scale plastic sealing of board-level packages, significant deformations can occur due to differences in thermal expansion coefficients between the carrier board, adhesive film, and sealing layer after cooling. These deformations can cause deviations in the positions of the chips from the ideal design drawings, which can affect the quality of the subsequent wiring layer production. To address this issue, a chip offset detection method has been proposed that combines a motion platform and an industrial camera to visually inspect chips on the carrier board and calculate offset data to improve the quality of subsequent wiring layer production. The method involves measuring the positioning error of the motion platform and establishing a geometric error model for error compensation. An improved Edge Drawing algorithm is used to extract pixel-level edges from the chip image, and sub-pixel edge detection based on Zernike moments is used to improve edge detection accuracy. Using the least squares method to fit the edge of the chip, a carrier board coordinate system is established based on reference points, and the angular deviation between the chip coordinates and the carrier board coordinate system is solved using the homogeneous transformation matrix. This proposed chip position detection system is of great significance and can effectively solve the problem of chip position deviation in large-scale panel-level packaging. Experimental results demonstrate that the motion platform error compensation model can effectively reduce platform motion errors, and the chip position repeat positioning accuracy reaches 0.06mm, meeting industrial requirements.

articleTitle: Design and Integration Approach of Low-Inductance Vertical Interconnection Structure for Gallium-Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In Gallium-nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) packages, the topside interconnection structures not only play a key role in electrical interconnection but significantly impact the switching performance and heat dissipation efficiency of the dies. Conventional wire bonding technology makes it difficult for GaN HEMT to exploit its potential in high-frequency applications scenarios sufficiently and requires additional package footprint. For the GaN HEMT package, this paper proposes a flip-chip sintering low-inductance interconnection approach based on the DBC/PCB hybrid package structure. The thermal performance and thermal-mechanical reliability of modules under two different processes are evaluated and analyzed through the finite element method (FEM). The results show that the steady-state operation temperature of GaN power modules fabricated by silver sintering is 2.2 °C lower and the maximum thermomechanical stress in the die interconnection layer is 64.9% lower. The optimized gate loop and power loop layouts are analyzed and the power loop inductance is only 0.65 nH. A GaN half-bridge module is fabricated based on this integration scheme, and the static characteristics of the die used for fabrication and the integrated module are compared, and the double-pulse test (DPT) is used to evaluate its switching performance to verify the feasibility of the integration approach.

articleTitle: Research on short-term power prediction and energy storage capacity allocation of wind and photovoltaic power based on Elman neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the power system, renewable energy resources such as wind power and PV power has the characteristics of fluctuation and instability in its output due to the influence of natural conditions. So as to improve the absorption of wind and PV power generation, it’s required to equip the electrical power systems with energy storage units, which can suppress fluctuations caused by wind and PV power generation and ensure stable operation of the power system. This article mainly used the Elman neural network algorithm to predict the short-term power of wind and PV power in the electricity distribution network. Through the forecasted results, research is conducted on the configuration of mobile energy storage capacity. By dynamic configuration of mobile energy storage units, the integration of wind and PV power generation in the electricity distribution network is improved. Finally, the effectiveness of the forecast methodology and the feasibility of energy storage capacity configuration are demonstrated through simulation experiments. The findings of the study provide reference for improving the stability of power systems containing a high proportion of renewable energy sources like wind and PV and for optimized capacity planning of their power system storage devices.

Author Keywords: Short-term power forecasts for wind and photovoltaic power

articleTitle: Improvement of the solderability of aluminum alloy, nickel, stainless steel and copper by metallization of silver and nickel for power semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles and aerospace electronics, wide band gap (WBG) power devices' harsh working environments pose significant challenges to packaging materials. Therefore, there is an urgent need to investigate novel materials and connecting techniques in order to enhance die-attach strength. In this paper, the effects of various silver plating thicknesses and coating types on the mechanical properties of joints have been researched. The findings presented in this work indicate that pure silver plating on materials with low solderability has no appreciable impact on the bonding strength of their joints, which is attributed to the poor combination between the sheets and the silver layer, as confirmed by additional microscopic investigations. But the shear strength of aluminum alloy and stainless steel joints can be increased to more than four times the initial value with a mixed coating of 300 nm nickel and 2 μm silver. This study is anticipated to offer recommendations for coating materials to increase their solderability, despite the fact that there are numerous different coating types and thicknesses that need to be further investigated.

articleTitle: Design of Optoelectronic Chip Packaging and Integration Method Based on SiP Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The current optoelectronic chip packaging integration model is generally set in a single stage form, and the integration efficiency is affected, resulting in a gradual decline in the chip yield. Therefore, the design and verification analysis of the optoelectronic chip packaging integration method based on SiP technology is proposed. According to the actual measurement requirements and standards, carry out chip visible light measurement and frequency modulation processing. At the same time of chip loading, adopt the processing mode of keys and lines, adopt the multi-level form, improve the integration efficiency, establish a multi-level SiP packaging integration model, and use PCB wiring processing to achieve packaging integration processing. The final test results show that after six times of packaging and integration tests for optoelectronic chips, the final chip loading yield can reach more than 96.99%, which indicates that the packaging and integration processing effect of this method is relatively good. Under the complex background environment, the set optoelectronic chip packaging and integration tasks can be completed more quickly and timely, and the speed is fast. The integration error is controllable, which improves the efficiency and quality of optoelectronic chip packaging and integration to a certain extent, and has practical application value.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniature High-Gain Quasi-Resonant Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Following the rapid increasing adoption of wide band-gap power semiconductor devices, the corresponding high voltage test equipment becomes indispensable nowadays. As one of the most important power semiconductor devices test, HTRB (high temperature reverse bias) puts the power semiconductor devices under high temperature environment with reverse-bias voltage applied to evaluate their projected anticipated lifetime. In this paper, a microminiaturized high-gain quasi-resonance flyback converter based on GreenPAK programmable chip SLG46855 is designed for HTRB testing of kV-level SiC power semiconductor devices and other related high voltage test applications. The converter topology couples an flyback circuit with two transformers, forming a differential charge pump-based voltage-multiplier to convert 5V~12V input to 800V~1600V output with higher voltage gain, lower stress on transformer, less diodes and smaller output capacitors, correspondingly less pre-charge time considerably. Quasi-resonant soft switching is applied in steady state DCM to realize higher voltage gain and lower power loss drastically. A new quasi-resonant voltage valley detection circuit leveraging the input pin characteristic of SLG46855 is designed to capture the rising edge of drain voltage to trigger the turn-on signal of MOSFET switch, while magnetizing current detection triggers the turn-off signal. A secondary current cancellation circuit is designed to eliminate the reflected charge pump current, thus allowing accurate detection of the true magnetizing current. Meanwhile, to implement high-speed magnetizing current detection without the use of an expensive and power hungry high speed comparator, an self-calibrating biasing circuit is introduced to elevate the detection signal to near trigger threshold of the input port of SLG46855. The combination mimics the behavior of a mV-level comparator with ns-level response time. Smooth mode switching is realized during startup, balancing voltage rising ratio and power heat. In this paper, the converter operation principal and SPICE simulation will be demonstrated around its topology, related control and detection methods correspondingly. A 3.0x1.8 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> miniature prototype is made and evaluated, seeing high performance and advantages in HTRB test application.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization of Multi-energy Complementary System via Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the reformation of the energy market, the integrated multi-energy complementary system has achieved rapid development during the past decade. By coupling and interconnecting different energy sources, the integrated energy system has shown great potential in enhancing energy efficiency and diminishing carbon emissions. In this work, we constructed a multi-energy microgrid model that includes electricity, heat, cooling, gas, and a hydro-solar-wind multi-energy complementary system. Subsequently, a collaborative optimization model for multi-microgrid energy sharing is established, which is decomposed into sub-problems of microgrid alliance cost minimization and power trading. To ensure a fair and mutually beneficial interaction between the comprehensive energy system and users, we adopted game theory principles. By incorporating the complementary properties of hydro, solar, and wind energy, our approach enhances the efficiency and environmental sustainability of the integrated energy system through the day-ahead scheduling. To achieve this, the mixed integer linear programming is employed to optimize microgrid systems by considering multiple economic and environmental indicators. Additionally, the concept of Nash equilibrium game theory from economics is employed to guide peer-to-peer energy trading among multiple microgrid systems. Ultimately, through collaborative optimization among multiple microgrids, the renewable energy consumption rate of the system is increased to 100%. Simultaneously, the operating costs of the three microgrids are reduced by 40.98%, 65.74%, and 34.69% respectively, effectively enhancing the environmental sustainability of the system and lowering energy costs for users.

articleTitle: Effect of dimension and defects on the flexibility of ultra-thin chips for wearable electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Flexible packages had already been extensively investigated for use in wearable electronics, for example, chip on flex(COF) packages using anisotropic conductive film as the interconnection materials. But it is difficult to achieve highly flexible COF packages due to the brittle nature of silicon chips used in them. There are a lot of factors that could affect the flexibility of the brittle silicon chip, thickness, dimension and defects which were produced by the thinning process of silicon chip. In this paper, in order to achieve more flexible packages, the silicon chip properties were studied. The thickness of silicon chip was fixed with 50μm using DBG process. There were 3 types of potential crack initiation at silicon chips: dicing saw marks, edge chipping and surface defects. 3 kinds of silicon dimension were used 16mm x 16mm, 16mm x 8mm and 16mm x 1.5mm respectively. The flexibility was determined by bending radius which evaluated by four point bending method. At the same time, the main factor affecting the flexibility of silicon chip was also defined, then physical surface treatment and chemical etching were used to improve the defect and examination.It was found that the bending radius was the same as a theoretical value in terms of dimension by the simulation result of finite element analysis(FEA), because the silicon chip was with the same modulus, but it was different from the experiment result that the bending radius became smaller from 8mm(16mm x 16mm) to 5mm(16mm x 1.5mm), because the larger dimension with bigger bending area had more grinding saw marks confirmed by AFM, and grinding saw marks were the main factor affected the flexibility analyzed by the four point bending method. And depending on the degree of variation in bending radius of a silicon chip, in relation to its dimensions, it could be concluded that the chips with smaller bending area from square shape to rectangular shape exhibit fewer surface defect and greater flexibility. To conduct a thorough analysis of surface defects in silicon chip flexibility, the widely used Sopori etch method was employed, which utilizes a chemical etch to create etch pits at the locations where surface emergence occurs. The number of defects was analyzed based on different etch time and surface condition, and the bending radius of the etched Si chip with different number of surface defects was then confirmed. As a result, the rectangular chips with fewer defects were found to be less likely to affect flexibility and are recommended as the future wearable device packages.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Ultra-thin Conformal EMI Shielding Coatings on SiP Modules by Inkjet Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for achieving ultra-thin conformal electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding for System-in-Package (SiP) using inkjet printing technology. First, the nano-silver ink is deposited on the surface of the SiP modules by inkjet printing. And then the heat treatment process is carried out to form a dense and uniform conductive coating through the low-temperature sintering of nano-silver particles, for shielding the EM waves. This process offers superior conductivity compared to sprayed conformal EMI shielding. It only requires half the thickness to achieve the same EMI SE. In addition, a near-field probe is used to evaluate the SE simulating the SiP surface. After covering the conformal EMI shielding coating, the intensity of the EM wave decreased significantly near the SiP surface. Overall, inkjet printing technology provides a high material utilization, area selectivity, high efficiency and flexibility conformal EMI shielding solution for SiP.

articleTitle: Study on Picosecond Pulsed Laser Grooving Technology for Low-k Silicon Wafer
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous reduction of chip manufacturing process, more and more low dielectric constant (low-k) materials are introduced into wafer manufacturing to replace the traditional dielectric material (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Due to the low mechanical strength and hard and brittle features of low-k materials, it is easy to cause defects such as peeling and topside chipping during blade dicing. Hence the blade dicing is no longer suitable for the product, laser grooving process comes into being. In this study, the influence of key parameters of laser grooving, such as laser power, feed speed and scanning times on the grooving characteristics is researched by the orthogonal experiment. High power optical microscope, OLS5100 are used to inspection in this study. The orthogonal experiment results show that the depth of the groove depends mainly on the laser power and feed speed. The width is greatly affected by scanning times and laser power, and the feed speed has the least effect. The results of single factor experiment show that a higher laser fluence results to higher the groove depth and a larger groove bottom surface roughness under the condition of fixed grooving speed and scanning times, the maximum values can reach 12.493μm and 0.477μm, respectively. Besides groove width is basically unchanged, depending on laser spot diameter.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Manual Splitting on Thermal Fatigue Reliability of PBGA Solder Joints
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Manual panel splitting stress can inevitably harm the reliability of surface mount solder joints, but it is difficult to detect using conventional quality analysis methods. In this paper, the same temperature cycle test is carried out using the two kinds of PBGA board level interconnection solder joints with/without manual splitting, and the impact of manual board splitting on the thermal fatigue reliability of PBGA solder joints is quantitatively analyzed, which can provide quantitative reference for relevant engineering practices.

articleTitle: The application of Developing Low-warpage Bonding Pair by Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Facing with the significant reduction on mechanical strength of ultra-thin wafer, temporary bonding and de-bonding (TBDB) process was developed to ensure that wafers could successfully and safely complete the subsequent processes. Unfortunately, the mismatch in coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) between the carrier wafer and device wafer (Si) would produce significant mechanical stress as the bonding pair experienced a huge temperature variation. To resolve this, a series of finite element analysis (FEA) simulations and experiments were carried out in this paper. Hypermesh and Abaqus were employed to construct the model of bonding pair. Firstly, a cooling load (130~25℃) was applied, the bonding pair behaved like a symmetrically bowl-shape (low in the middle and high at the edges) and the warpage was 6.39 mm. Then a series of single factor studies (SFS) of each parameter (E, CTE and ν) for TBM-1 were carried out. The results showed that only E has a great impact on warpage, especially when it was lower than 1 MPa, the warpage ranged from 3.83 mm to 6.39 mm. While SFS were performed on CTE (300~420 ppm/k) and ν (0.17~0.47), the warpage variation was negligible. Therefore, we redesigned and synthesized another low modulus material (TBM-2). And the warpage of the bonding pair made with TBM-2 was lower than that made with TBM-1, and it has been proven under different high temperature processes. In addition, a series FEA were conducted on the influence of glass wafer, TBM, silicon wafer’s thickness on warpage, and it has been proven that as the thickness of glass wafer, TBM and silicon wafer increased, the warpage value of bonding pairs reduced gradually.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Radiation Degradation of Metal Can Packaged Bipolar Transistor*
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, the radiation damage of the metal can-packaged discrete bipolar transistors is investigated with <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co ionizing radiation source under the high total dose environment. The experimental results of up to 1Mrad(Si) dose irradiation with dose rate of 100rad(Si)/s show that the degradation of all tested electrical parameters of the PNP transistors did not exceed the rated range of the device with the increase of the dose, and it has good radiation resistance under high total ionizing dose irradiation. Both saturation voltage drop and breakdown voltage increase to varying degrees, while reverse leakage is insensitive to ionizing radiation, current gain is the most sensitive parameter due to the modified electric field distribution in the device by the creation of radiation-induced traps. The results provide valuable reference information for assessing the radiation damage potential of bipolar devices intended for space applications. By studying the radiation-induced effects on electrical parameters, this research contributes to the understanding of how bipolar transistors perform under high total ionizing dose irradiation conditions, aiding in the development of radiation-tolerant electronic systems for space exploration.

articleTitle: Prediction of bonding strength for sintered Ag/DBA joints based on cohesive zone model
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of semiconductor technology, sintered silver is considered as the most suitable interconnect material due to its advantages such as high melting point. However, the interface between sintered silver layer and substrate is easy to fail under harsh service conditions of SiC power module. Compared with copper substrates, DBA (Direct Bonded Aluminum) substrates have higher thermal stability are widely used in the interconnection of third generation power devices. But the reliability of sintered silver/aluminum interface is still the bottleneck problem restricting the reliability of high temperature interconnection. In this paper, the influence of different metallized layers on the bonding strength between sintered nano silver and DBA substrate was studied. And on the basis of considering the influence of different metallized layers, the reverse analysis of the test results was carried out, and the CZM traction separation rule was proposed. The CZM model given in this paper can be used to analyze the shear strength of sintered silver/DBA joints. The performance of metallized layers was proposed to optimize the packaging process and improve the thermal mechanical reliability of the sintered silver/ DBA joints.

articleTitle: Analysis of 3D stacking technology and TSV technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: semiconductor technology must continue to develop in order to increase IC performance and function, reduce chip size, and reduce power consumption and cost. At present, we have developed innovative, small-size, cost-effective three-dimensional wire interconnection technology to meet the above needs. Through silicon via (TSV) technology can accelerate the application of wafer stacking technology due to its three-dimensional interconnection method, especially in the integration of heterogeneous components. 3D stacking technology is a very useful solution for multi wafer integration, but there are still many technical challenges to be overcome. Starting from the basic overview of 3D stacking technology and TSV technology, this paper analyzes 3D stacking technology and TSV technology in detail, in order to promote the high-quality development of enterprises.

articleTitle: Transmission Structures Using Parylene C and TSV for Silicon-based Low-loss and Low-profile Heterogeneous Integrations at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As wireless communication technology advances towards higher frequency bands, RF systems become more integrated and package sizes scale down. This paper proposed two low-profile and low-loss Ka-band RF transmission structures based on eSiFO technology: CPW and SIW. The impact of the width of the trenches and the dielectric Parylene C on the RF transmission performance in the eSiFO process was considered in both design and simulation. The results showed that in the Ka-band, the loss of CPW designed in this paper was less than 0.5 dB/mm, and the loss of SIW was less than 1 dB with an 8 mm length. And the eSiFO package had little impact on the transmission performance of these two structures. Different interconnection structures could be selected according to different requirements, and the eSiFO process had little effect on transmission line performance. Therefore, this paper laid the foundation for the design and optimization of eSiFO interconnections in the Ka-band.

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of SiC power assembly by using time-series analysis of acoustic emission during power cycling tests
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Condition monitoring using acoustic emission (AE) technology is a widely used method for detecting failures and analyzing working conditions in various industrial facilities. However, there has been limited research conducted on utilizing AE for monitoring the condition of power devices. In this study, we implemented AE-based online monitoring during a power cycling test of a SiC power assembly and successfully captured a significant amount of AE signals. Through the analysis of the power assembly failures, it was determined that the AE signals originated from stress waves caused by solder layer cracking. We also compared the AE monitoring to traditional condition monitoring methods that rely on thermal signals such as junction temperature and thermal resistance. The obtained AE signals demonstrated superior sensitivity in identifying initial cracking. Furthermore, we investigated the variations in AE peak frequency centroid and AE energy as the power cycling test progressed, which provided multiple dimensions for understanding the failure process of the power assembly.

articleTitle: Numerical study of the effect of epoxy molding compound gradation on the thermo-mechanical properties of package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The warpage behavior of the package component is one of the important issues in the packing technology, which can induce surface defects and finally lead to the degradation of the product reliability. The warpage is mainly caused by the mismatch of thermal-mechanic properties of different materials. In this paper, we take advantage of a multi-scaled simulation for the packing component, focusing on the effect of epoxy molding compound (EMC) characteristics on the warpage, whose main filler is commonly based on silica. Firstly, a meso-scaled numerical model of silica-based epoxy composites is generated with randomly dispersed particulate fillers. The effective modulus and coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) are simulated numerically considering various filler percentage, filler size, particle size distribution, size shape and size type. Based on the homogenization of the thermal mechanic properties of EMC, we further investigate the warpage behavior of the package component by finite element method (FEM). Thus, the dependence of the silica filler characteristics on the warpage is analyzed, which benefits the design of the formula of EMC in the future.

articleTitle: Optimizing conformal shielding scheme with quantitative analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Conformal shielding has emerged as a promising technique in recent years due to its advantages such as seamless shielding, minimal SiP area occupation, and good heat dissipation performance. However, the exploration of the effects of various structural parameters on shielding performance in conformal shielding schemes for SiP packaging, including material type, cavity thickness, and cavity defects, has been limited to qualitative analysis, which hinders actual production. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a quantitative analysis method to evaluate the factors affecting shielding effectiveness. The proposed method is used to optimize the conformal shielding structure design scheme, and test samples are prepared using this optimized scheme. The simulation and test results are in good agreement which demonstrates the effectiveness of the quantitative analysis method, verifying its feasibility for guiding actual design and production activities.

articleTitle: Research on AI-Based Gold Removal Technology for Aviation Connector Cup Cavity Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The surface of the solder cup of the aviation connectors is coated with a layer of gold plating. To avoid gold embrittlement after soldering, it is necessary to remove the gold layer before soldering. Currently, the gold removal process for aviation connectors involves manually heating the eutectic tin-lead solder to dissolve the gold layer and then using a desoldering wick to remove the solder with the dissolved gold layer. To address the problems of low yield, poor gold removal effect, and inconsistent performance of the current gold removal method, an intelligent tinning and gold removal system based on machine vision, artificial intelligence, robot motion control, and laser soft soldering technology has been developed. This article introduces the design scheme, hardware system, and software system of the system. To achieve automation, it is essential to address the challenges of identifying, positioning, and determining the opening direction of each solder cup of the aviation connector. This article proposes an artificial intelligence approach that takes into account the unique characteristics of the aviation connector and introduces the AIC algorithm. The AIC algorithm is designed to improve the accuracy and consistency of the automated process. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments and analysis. This research provides a valuable contribution to the field of automated tinning and gold removal systems for aviation connectors. Initially, the aviation connector is photographed, and the AIC algorithm is applied to identify each solder cup and calculate its coordinates accurately. The algorithm also locates the opening position of each solder cup. This information is then sent to the six-axis robot, which acts as the executive mechanism. The success rate of identification and positioning is achieved at 98%. This research presents a significant breakthrough in the automation of tinning and gold removal systems for aviation connectors. The proposed approach demonstrates remarkable accuracy and consistency, which is crucial for efficient and reliable production processes. The proposed approach for automated tinning and gold removal systems for aviation connectors employs laser as the heat source, eutectic tin-lead solder wire as the gold removal material, and an automated feeding mechanism for the solder wire. The feeding mechanism is integrated with the laser at the end of a six-axis robot arm. The six-axis robot moves to the solder cup of the aviation connector that requires gold removal, guided by the results of the AIC algorithm. The feeding mechanism feeds the solder wire through the opening of the solder cup, and the laser melts the eutectic tin-lead solder wire. The molten alloy dissolves the gold layer on the surface of the solder cup, which is then extracted along with the molten alloy. This achieves the desired gold removal effect. The proposed method offers a reliable and efficient solution for the automation of tinning and gold removal processes for aviation connectors. The six-axis robot automatically executes the gold removal action based on the data obtained from the recognition step, achieving full automation. Testing of the system indicates a recognition accuracy of 0.05mm and a precision of 0.1mm for the executive mechanism. For aviation connector solder cups with a gold layer thickness of 2.54μm or less, two gold removal cycles were performed using the proposed system. The EDS method was employed to test for the presence of gold elements, but none were detected. Thus, the system described in this study satisfies the gold removal requirements for aviation connector solder cups and improves efficiency by over 100%.

articleTitle: Effect of Solder Thick on the Interfacial Reaction in Cu/Sn/Ni Solder Joints
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous development of electronic packaging technology in the direction of miniaturization, micro bumps in three-dimensional integrated circuit (3D-IC) packaging have become a key technology to meet various requirements. At present, Cu/Sn/Ni structure solder joints are a common interconnect form in packaging. As the size of the solder joints continues to decrease, the interfaces on both sides of the solder joint are no longer independent systems, but interact and restrict each other. Ni and Cu atoms can diffuse across the solder to the other side and affect the interfacial reaction on that side. In this paper, the effects of Cu-Ni crossinteraction on the type and morphology of the interfacial intermetallic compounds (IMCs) is observed during the interfacial reaction of Cu/Sn/Ni solder joints with three pitch sizes of 100 µm, 50 µm and 30 µm at 260 °C. The focus of this study is the effect of solder thickness on the growth and microstructure of interfacial IMCs. According to energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) results, the interfacial IMCs in Cu/Sn/Ni solder joints at both interfaces is (Cu,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> at 260 C for different time. The thickness of IMCs increases with the increasing of the soldering time. The asymmetric growth of IMCs can be clearly observed, i.e., the thickness of IMC on the Ni interface is always thicker than that on the Cu interface, under three different solder thickness. According to the EDX results, Ni atoms affect the morphology of (Cu,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> IMCs at the interface, and the critical concentration for causing the transition of the two morphologies is 11 at.%. Furthermore, when the content of Ni atoms is greater than the critical concentration, the (Cu,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> IMCs is needle shaped, and when the content of Ni atoms is less than the critical concentration, the (Cu,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> IMCs is scallop shaped.

articleTitle: An accurate numerical prediction for the thermal conductivity of thermal interface materials
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Particulate composites are widely utilized in the electronic packaging field. To enhance the thermal dissipation in the packaging component, the interfacial thermal materials (TIMs) are commonly employed between chip and heat sink, which compose of thermal-conductive particulate fillers. The accurate prediction of the thermal conductivity of TIMs benefits the design of their formula. In this paper, we introduce the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder and diamond particles in silicone matrix to improve the thermal conductivity of TIMs. Firstly, the filler-matrix and filler-filler interfacial thermal resistance (ITR) in the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-diamond/silicone composites are identified taking advantage of the high-throughput numerical simulation, machine learning algorithm as well as simple experiment measurements. The accuracy determination of the ITRs is further validated by the comparison of thermal conductivity of binary composites between the numerical prediction and experiment measurements. Finally, the thermal conductivities of the TIMs with a series of gradation are numerically predicted, showing good agreement with the measured thermal conductivity of the corresponding experimental samples, presenting the values as high as 5.7 W/mK.

articleTitle: A digital twin framework of reflow soldering based on a novel high dimension surrogate model
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The concept of digital twins is to have a digital model that can replicate the behavior of a physical asset in real time. However, using digital models to reflect the structural performance of physical assets usually faces high computational costs, which makes it difficult for the model to satisfy real-time requirements. As a technique to replace expensive simulations, surrogate models have great potential to solve this problem. However, the optimal single surrogate model (SSM) applied to a given problem usually changes as factors change, and this can be mitigated by integrating multiple SSMs. Therefore, this study proposes a digital twin framework of reflow soldering based on a novel high dimension surrogate model. This method not only provides robust approximation but also reduces the additional cost brought by the experiment of the reflow soldering. Moreover, based on the characteristics of the experiment method, a finite element model (FEM), which provides scalability for the construction of a digital model, is established. That is, the number of FEM can be customized to not only decrease the computational cost by reducing elements but also obtain the key information by customizing the design of the reflow soldering. Numerical experiments are employed to verify the performance of the proposed digital twin framework of reflow soldering. A reflow soldering design case is used as an example to build a high dimension digital twin, which proves the feasibility and effectiveness of the framework.

articleTitle: Investigations on the Batch Fluctuations of an Epoxy Diluent via Encapsualtion Stress Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Reactive diluent plays an important role in epoxy encapsulant formulations. Contents of epoxide and impurities like inorganic chlorine and saponified chlorine are the major chemical parameters for the reactive diluents and have an impact on the property of epoxy, including the curing residue stress which is unavoidable and could be devastating if it is not handled well. In current work, we analyzed the variations of the chemical parameters of a reactive diluent, as well as the major processing and thermos-mechanical properties of the corresponding epoxy resin. Fluctuations of the reactive diluents were demonstrated by the notable content of chloride. One major influence of the batch fluctuations of the reactive diluents was disclosed upon the varying gel time of the epoxy. Furthermore, evolution of epoxy curing stress was monitored by a straightforward strain gage based method, which showed varying evolving behaviors as a function of time due to the batch fluctuations of the diluents. The higher content of saponified chloride of the reactive diluent delayed the curing reaction, leading to a higher curing shrinkage induced stress during the non-isothermal curing process and a lower thermal-induced stress within the following cooling process, which may result in unexpected fracture in the encapsulation potentially. These results demonstrated the critical effect of the saponified chloride content of the raw materials in the epoxy encapsulant on the consistent performance of the encapsulation. Our novel method to measure the curing residual stress appeared to be a simple and efficient way to monitor the batch fluctuations of raw materials by differentiating the curing behaviors.

articleTitle: Reliability study of fine pitch Cu-Sn micro-bump structure electromigration test by Finite Element Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As 3D stacking of memory products leads the trend, dimension of micro-bump scales down. General microbump pitch has been reduced to 20~40μm, which is almost one order of magnitude smaller than flip chip solder ball. Current density flowing through the micro-bump will increase dramatically under the same supply current when chips are stacked together. It can be seen that electromigration failure of micro-bump will become a severe issue. Investigation of electromigration reliability for fine pitch micro-bump is urgently needed. However, due to the extremely narrow gap between micro-bumps, reliability study through experimental methods is usually resource-consuming. Therefore, numerical simulation method is particularly important to study electromigration reliability. In this paper, a 3D stacked test vehicle model with Cu-Sn micro-bump as interlayer connection is established. Atomic Flux Divergence (AFD) method is used to investigate the dominate migration principle in Cu-Sn micronstructure under different working conditions. Results reveal the behavior of electronic migration, thermal migration, and stress migration under different electromigration test conditions. Stress migration is observed larger than electronic migration and thermal migration when current density=1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, temperature=150℃, which is in accordance with the experiment under the same condition. Besides, stress migration is observed always having great influence on electromigration process with different current density when test temperature is high (150℃). Low test temperature is suggested if the effect of electronic migration needs to be manifested in final experiment result.

articleTitle: Study on mechanical properties and microstructure reliability of composite solder under multiple reflow and high-temperature storage
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of integrated circuit packaging from single chip packaging to multi-chip packaging, the number of interconnection levels increases and the number of welding increases significantly. The problem of solder joint remelting becomes more and more serious in the process of multistage interconnection. Transient liquid phase composite solder has attracted wide attention due to its low temperature welding and high temperature service performance, but there are few studies on its reliability under long-term service conditions. SnPb solder plays an important role in highly reliable integrated circuits because of its good tin whisker inhibition and electromigration resistance. In this paper, two SnPb-Cu composite solders were welded and stored at high temperature for many times, and their mechanical properties and microstructure were obtained. The experimental results show that: (1) with the increase of reflow times, the shear strength of solder joint increases first and then decreases, and the shear strength reaches the maximum after one reflow. The fracture mode of solder joint is a mixture of ductile fracture and brittle fracture. (2) The IMC thickness of the welding interface increases with the increase of the number of reflow, which is proportional to the square root of the number of reflow. (3) The shear strength of solder joint decreases with the increase of storage time, and remains stable after a certain time. (4) The microstructure in the solder joint coarsened obviously with the process of high temperature storage, and the interface IMC thickened.

articleTitle: The microstructure of Cu joint soldered with a new Cu coated Ni foam reinforced Sn composite solder
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: It is imperative to develop a high-performance Sn-based lead-free solder to obtain high strength, high temperature resistance and high precision Cu connections. In this study, Cu joints were soldered with a new Cu coated Ni foam reinforced Sn composite solder, and the effects of metal foam composition and soldering time on the microstructure and mechanical properties of joints were revealed. The molten Sn matrix was consumed in under 60 min, as a result of the rapid metallurgical reaction with both the high surface area of the Cu coated Ni foam skeletons and also with the Cu substrates. This is accompanied by the formation of the high melting point (Cu,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn phases. The results show that Cu coated Ni foam reinforced Sn composite solder can improve the shear strength of Cu joints that have potential to serve at high temperature.

articleTitle: Integrated Data Acquisition Module based on CPO packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed Data Acquisition CPO (Co-packaged Optics) module which collect and convert 2 channels IF signal to digital signals within a very compact size. The module consists of an IF filter, digital step attenuator, balun, ADC, drivers, 8 channel lasers and a fiber array connector. The input IF signal of each channel will be converted into four 204B streams and then directly injected into the LD driver, added to the biasing current of the VCSELs. With co-packaged optics technology, we fabricated a Data Acquisition module, the board size is 30mm × 30mm. We demonstrated that analog IF signal sampling could be correctly converted into output digital signals, the dynamic range of the input signal is -70dBm~ 5.3dBm. The SFDR is 57dBc. And the maximum power accuracy over 1.3~2.3GHz is 0.3dB, the IM2 and IM3 distortion is -61dBc and -66.2dBc, respectively

articleTitle: The influence of pattern size on the profile and microstructure of electroplated copper pad, redistribution layer and via for advanced packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the packaging technology is developing towards miniaturization, the size reduction of the interconnection structure might affect their properties and reliability of the packaging. Therefore, the influence of pattern size on the profile and microstructure of electroplated copper was explored in this study. Different sizes of pads (40~105μm in diameter), redistributed layers (RDL, 8~20μm in width) and via (outer diameter in the range of 40~105μm, inner diameter in the range of 20~85μm) were electroplated by a commercial electrolyte. Firstly, the pattern size had a important effect on the flatness. As analyzed by confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM). The flatness of pad was 24 % ~ 34.5 %, and showed a decreasing tendency with the increase of diameter. The flatness of RDL was 16.5 % ~ 34 %, and gradually deteriorated with the line width increases. The via cannot be completely filled when the outer diameter is greater than 60μm. And the flatness of via firstly decreased (from convex to flat), then increased (from flat to concave). Secondly, the microstructure of electroplated copper with different patterns was characterized by focused ion beam (FIB), which showed a little difference when the pattern size changed. Finally, thermal shock reliability test was also conducted on the samples to evaluate their thermal mismatch situation. It seemed that small pads can induce larger thermal mismatch under thermal shock test.

articleTitle: 4x4 Millimeter-Wave Patch Antenna Array for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Antenna-in-package(AiP) has been extensive used in millimeter wave(mm wave) system integration. Fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) can improve electrical performance, reduce thickness and thermal resistance, making it become the best suited packaging for mm wave applications. This paper presented a 4x4 series fed patch antenna array which consists of four patch antennas fed by a 1-to-4 feeding network. The proposed antenna uses HFSS software for simulation, and this designed array showed a high gain directional wide side radiation pattern of 15.83 dBi at 28 GHz. The performance of the proposed array is adequate for 5G mm wave communication applications at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: A Ka Band Tile T/R Module based on Silicon Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Silicon interposers have been applied in 2.5D packaging especially for millimeter wave application recently, which have the advantages of high precision, high integration and low cost with mass production over traditional ceramic or plastic packaging by multichip module technology. This article aims at to develop a tile T/R module in Ka band by using silicon advanced packaging technology to minimize the size of the package and reduce the weight. In this paper, a Ka band tile T/R module is designed based on TSV silicon interposer 2.5D packaging technology. The channel link and signal transmission model are optimized by simulation analysis. The T/R module is completed by silicon packaging technology. The RF chips are integrated on the silicon interposer, and hermetic sealing is achieved by wafer lever packaging with silicon cap wafer. The size of fabricated Ka band tile T/R module based on silicon packaging is 14mm (length)×13mm (width)×2.1mm (height) and its weight is 0.5g, which greatly reduce the size and weight. Finally, the performance of single channel tile T/R module is tested and the receive gain(⩾17dB) and transmitted power(⩾23dBm) are measured in the range of 33~37GHz.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis for IIH leakage on 7nm FinFFT Technology Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of advanced manufacturing technology, leakage caused by transistors damage poses a major challenge to wafer level failure localization. It is also noted that DC parameters failures are increasing in recent years. This paper mainly studies wafer level fault location for IIH leakage by using advanced failure analysis methods, providing a high-efficiency failure analysis method to locate defects fastly. In the method, Low KV passive voltage and nanoprobe device parameter measurements were used to define the leaking transistor location, and then transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to confirm that the failure was caused by the damage of the barrier layer during automate test equipment.

articleTitle: Phosphor-in-glass film on AlN substrate for high-luminance white laser Lighting
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Phosphor-in-glass (PiG) has been regarded as an excellent inorganic phosphor converter in white laser lighting. However, the luminescence saturation induced mainly by thermal quenching makes it hard to achieve high-brightness luminance under high power laser excitation. Therefore, a high-saturation phosphor converter of PiG film on AlN ceramic substrate (PiF-AlN) was prepared for high-brightness white laser lighting. The laser-spot-regulated opto-thermal performance of PiF-AlN converter was investigated. Owing to the enhancement of high thermal conductivity AlN plate, the PiF-AlN converter achieves a high saturation laser power of 37.06 W at 2.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where the converter realizes a high luminous flux (LF) of 1845 lm. Moreover, the PiF-AlN converter achieves a relatively low surface temperature of 105°C when driven by laser of 10.32 W with laser spot of 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The prepared PiF-AlN converter displays high-saturation and high-performance, which suggests that it is an ideal phosphor converter for high-brightness white laser lighting.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Conversion Benefits of Hybrid Wind Power and Concentrating Solar Power System Based on Time-of-use Electricity Price
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Northwestern area of China has abundant wind and solar resources. Constructing the concentrating solar power (CSP) plant nearing the wind farm will become a common form of energy exploiting. In order to evaluate the energy conversion efficiency of the wind power-concentrating solar power (WP-CSP) system, based on the operational characteristics of WP-CSP system and the output characteristics of each subsystem, and considering the influence of electricity price, a quantitative evaluation model of the energy conversion benefits of WP-CSP system based on the time-of-use electricity pricing is established to study the influence of CSP plant on wind power peak load shifting in WP-CSP system. The simulation calculation results show that under the influence of the time-of-use electricity pricing policy, the cheap electricity in the low hours is converted into precious electricity in the peak hours, and the WP-CSP system achieves good economic benefits; also, it can also effectively smooth the wind farm power and reduce the volatility of grid connection.

articleTitle: Effects of Ge addition on the growth of interfacial Ni3Sn4 IMC in the Sn58Bi/Ni solder joint: First-principles and Experimental Investigations
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Interfacial intermetallic compound (IMC) is an important interconnection medium in soldering, and its brittleness makes it the most failure-prone region in soldered joints, Therefore, the growth and evolution of interfacial IMCs has been a focus of attention in electronic packaging. The conventional Cu-Sn system gradually generates Cu3Sn. The resulting Kirkendall voids affect the reliability of solder joints during service. An effective way to alleviate such a situation is to add Ni as a diffusion barrier layer. Therefore, it is necessary to study the reaction between Sn-based solder and Ni substrate and the growth of intermetallic compounds at the interface, which are crucial for design the bonding material composition and optimize the bonding parameters during the bonding process.In high-density packaging, the choice of solder needs to meet the requirements of multi-level interconnections. Sn58Bi solder alloy with its excellent properties has become a promising low-temperature solder in the field of high-density gradient packaging.Therefore, this paper investigated the evolution of interfacial IMC at the Sn58Bi/Ni solder joint and researched the effect of Ge element on the growth of interfacial IMC. Besides, the diffusion rates of Sn, Ni and Ge atoms in Ni-Sn IMC were calculated using density functional theory (DFT). The effect of Ge element addition on the composition and structure of Ni-Sn-based IMCs interconnected with Sn58Bi/Ni substrates was researched. The results show that the addition of Ge element promotes the IMC growth, and the growth pattern obtained from DFT was verified by the reflowing experiments. A reliable calculation model to predict the thickness of interfacial IMC was proposed.

articleTitle: Research on Packaging Reliability of LTCC High Density Packaging Substrate with High-CTE
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: LTCC packaging substrate has attracted more and more attention in the industry because of its good signal transmission characteristics and conductivity. High-CTE LTCC packaging substrate is widely used in high-density large-scale integrated circuit packaging because of its good thermal matching with PCB, which ensures the reliability of secondary packaging. However, the bending strength of LTCC with high-CTE is about 200MPa, which is only half of that of traditional HTCC. At the same time, the larger CTE also increases the risk of failure with silicon chip. In this paper, the high-density LTCC packaging substrate and the corresponding verification chip are used to complete the packaging, and a series of reliability tests are carried out. The results show that the high-density LTCC packaging substrate has passed the electrical performance test after completing the temperature cycle, mechanical impact and other tests under the specified conditions, which can meet the general reliability requirements of the devices. However, the chip shear and pull-off strength is only about 1/2 of the HTCC substrate packaging structure. Research on the welding strength is an important direction to improve the application effect of LTCC. The conclusion of this paper provides a reference for the application of high-CTE LTCC.

articleTitle: Computational and experimental study of a novel L-Cysteine hydrochloride leveler for copper electroplated via fill in redistribution layers
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Redistribution layers (RDL) is a key interconnect structure between IC chips and packaging substrate. Copper electroplating is a conventional but important process in RDL manufacture. A copper electroplating bath consists of a virgin-make-up solution of copper sulfate, sulfuric acid and chloride, plus organic additives such as suppressor, accelerator and leveler for control of plating morphologies and material properties. L-Cysteine hydrochloride (CYS) is a natural and non-toxic agent commonly added in foods, medicines and cosmetics. Its chemical structure contains ammonium and thiol groups which are in favor of surface adsorption on copper. In this study, for the first time, CYS is applied and studied as a copper electroplating leveler, together with prototypical suppressor polyethylene glycol (PEG) and sodium bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS), to electroplate RDL vias. The adsorption and interactions of CYS are characterized with electrochemical measurements and analyzed with numerical simulations. With the PEG-SPS-CYS additive combination, the via fill performances and the crystallographic orientation are measured. The results indicate that CYS levelers exhibit strong adsorption activity and stability on cathode. At a current density of 5 ASD, it exhibits a good RDL via filling rate of 82%. By quantum chemical calculations, it is found that CYS has an appropriate energy gap allowing a high adsorbing activity. This work provides an inexpensive, nontoxic and environmental-friendly leveler for copper electroplating in advanced packaging

articleTitle: The correlation between the microstructure and mechanical property of low temperature sintering nano Ag paste
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Power electronics are developing towards miniaturization, high power and high density. In respond, the increasing operation temperature brought by high packaging density and power density imposes higher requirements on die attachment. Ag nanoparticle paste is a promising interfacial material in high-power electronic packaging, which meet the demand of low-temperature bonding and high-temperature service.
