The power loss is evenly distributed to the slow-wave circuit to obtain the temperature distribution. When the TWT is in continuous wave operation and the output power is approximately 176 W, the highest temperature at the end of the slow-wave circuit is 174.98 °C, which is far below the melting point of HCOFC and meets the design requirements of the terahertz TWT. The calculated stress distribution shows a maximum value of 20 MPa. The research in this article has some guiding significance for the quality and reliability of TWTs in engineering applications.

articleTitle: Thermal Management Method of Three-dimensional Integrated Inductors Based on Dielectric-cavity TSV Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper proposes a 3D passive inductor model based on dielectric-cavity TSV technology and investigates its thermal management. Compared to a TSV-based 3D inductor in silicon substrate, it has a 20% higher Q-factor, but also experiences a 700% increase in peak temperature. Finite element simulation and analysis indicates that the upper insulation layer mainly hinders heat conduction. Thus, a thermal TSV is added for heat dissipation. Through finite element analysis, theoptimized dielectric-cavity-TSV inductorexhibited a temperature peak value approximately 20% lower than the original model.

articleTitle: Study on Effect of Sintering Temperature on Decomposition Process of Organic System and Evolution of Sintered Tissues
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of sintering temperature on the decomposition process of organic system and the microstructure of the corresponding sintered tissues in three different silver pastes. In order to verify the evolution process and decomposition temperature of organic system, the burnout of the organic system in the three different silver pastes is analyzed using a thermogravimetric ananlyzer. Then, silver films were prepared at different sintering temperatures, and the corresponding microstructures are compared and analyzed. The results show that the types and contents of organic system in different silver pastes are different, and the decomposition process during sintering is also different, which leads to different microscopic morphology of the corresponding sintered tissues.

articleTitle: Package Warpage and Low-k Stress Investigation under Thermo-Compression Bonding with Non-Conductive Paste Process
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With development of integrated circuits, the pitch of bump on flip chip become finer. Although copper pillar technology can meet the requirements of high density interconnection, the chip-package interaction (CPI) is a key challenge during assembly because the copper pillar is stiffer than traditional solder bumps. These make thermo-compression bonding with non-conductive paste a promising solution for high density interconnection. In this study, quarter finite element models are built to analyze package warpage and sub-model technique is used to analyze the stress in low-k layer. For different assembly processes, reflow and TCB-NCP, package warpage and low-k stress are discussed. The material properties, package structure and process conditions are investigated for less warpage and lower low-k stress. As a result, the package warpage of TCB-NCP process is reduced by 19.4% and maximum value of maximum principal stress of low-k layer is reduced by 19.0% compared with the reflow process. Using the optimized parameters obtained by DOE method, the package warpage can be reduced by 74.9%, and the maximum value of maximum principal stress of low-k layer can be reduced by 14.4%.

articleTitle: Temperature prediction model of sheep barn in winter based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid development of large-scale sheep farming in recent years, the issue of environmental control in sheep housing has become increasingly prominent. Due to the complex mechanism of internal thermodynamics in sheep sheds, the temperature of sheep sheds is affected by a variety of factors, especially the influence of the external ambient temperature, and shows obvious non-linear characteristics that make modelling difficult. In this paper, the collected temperature data is viewed as a time series and the neural network is used to predict the future temperature trend, which is used to control the heating equipment. The BP feedforward network and Elman dynamic network were used to predict the temperature trend in the next 6 hours using the data of the first 48 hours respectively. Compared with the BP network, the recurrent neural network Elman adds a context layer, which serves to allow the network to have a memory function and to better adapt to dynamic changes in the data input. The prediction results show that the Elman prediction model has higher accuracy and better fitting effect, and can meet the demand of sheep barn temperature control.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis and prediction for thermal stress of sintered silver interconnection structure based on modified Suhir's solution
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper analyzes the thermal stress of sintered silver interconnection structure using both theoretical and finite element analysis methods. The interconnection structure of SiC power modules is composed of SiC chip layer, die-attached layer (sintered silver), and substrate layer with copper. The shearing stresses form among different interlayers of the interconnection due to discrepancies of thermal expansion coefficients (CTE) of different layered materials, which can affect the thermo-mechanical reliability of electron device. This study is to predict the stress distribution characteristics for the SiC chip-sintered silver layer-substrate structure to enhance its thermomechanical reliability. The equations of sintered silver interlayer shearing stress and tearing stress were deduced from Suhir's solution, and a three-layer finite mode model was established in ANASYS to verify the equations. The loading temperature was increased from 25 °C to 125 °C, while the porosity of sintered silver and interlayer thickness were varied. The theoretical predictions were compared to the numerical results of the finite element simulation, and accuracy of theoretical prediction was verified. This study provides insights into the stress distributions among different interlayers of the interconnection, which can aid in the development of reliable SiC power modules.

articleTitle: An ultra-thin vapor chamber with oriented spiral woven wick for microelectronic heat dissipation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The development of microelectronic devices is severely limited by the bottleneck of heat dissipation. To address this issue, nowadays, the ultra-thin vapor chamber (UTVC) shows great potential as a new type of element for efficient heat dissipation. However, the rapid backflow of working fluid has been a difficult problem in the ultra-thin capillary wick of UTVC. Herein, an ultra-thin vapor chamber (UTVC) as thin as 0.45 mm is proposed. The novel oriented spiral woven wick (SWW) is designed for this UTVC, which proves a near linear transport of working liquid to accelerate the liquid return for two-phase circulation. The SWW demonstrates excellent superhydrophilic property and has superior capillary performance. The thermal transfer characteristics of UTVC were investigated under three typical operating conditions, namely, horizon, gravity, and anti-gravity state. Based on the design of SWW, SWW-UTVC shows excellent anti-gravity performance. The lowest thermal resistance of SWW-UTVC is 0.77°C/W at 7 W under gravity state. The maximum equivalent thermal conductivity of SWW-UTVC is as high as 13553.3 W/(m•K) under gravity state, which is 33.9 times that of copper (about 400 W/(m•K)). This UTVC with the oriented spiral woven wick is an ideal element for the heat dissipation of microelectronic, especially in the extreme limited space less than 1 mm.

articleTitle: Studies of Atomic Force Microscopy and Application in Advanced Packaging, Materials Characterization and Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) techniques are increasingly used in material characterization and failure analysis. Many researchers at home and abroad have successfully applied AFM technology to the analysis and detection of microscopic surface morphology and performance. For example, AFM is used to characterize and analyze the microscopic surface morphology and properties of samples and use nano-indentation technology to measure and analyze the hardness of the sample surface; it can also be used to do some failure location analysis in the case of charged operation. AFM can also be used to measure the surface morphology and phase separation of polymers, crystallization, mechanical properties, friction properties, characterize their molecular weight, etc.In this paper, we further investigate the AFM technique and its application to a wide range of materials characterization and failure analysis. The surface of the sample is characterized by an atomic force microscope to find the cause of failure caused by surface roughness, hardness, or electrical properties.

articleTitle: Research on Structure Reliability Design Technology of High Power Ceramic Based Microsystem package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, China has made rapid progress in the field of microsystem technology through independent innovation, which has also led to profound changes in the design concept of electronic information system architecture. It has begun to move from the research stage of basic theory to the stage of engineering research and development, especially in the field of high-power microsystems, and has made breakthrough progress. Due to the large number of integrated chips, high density, and high reliability requirements of microsystems, most microsystems adopt ceramic solder pillar array CCGA package with high package density, good thermal performance, and good airtightness. The package and substrate are designed as an integrated design, greatly saving layout space. As the carrier of microsystems, the structural reliability of ceramic package plays a crucial role in the performance of microsystems. Therefore, based on the high-density multi-layer co fired ceramic technology system, this paper uses finite element analysis software to conduct a systematic simulation study on the structural reliability of microsystem package, forming structural design rules for large-sized and highly reliable package suitable for microsystem package. In this paper, multi-level parts matching technology is mainly used to solve the thermal stress problem caused by the large difference of coefficient of thermal expansion between different parts of the large-scale micro system package. Microsystems designed using this technology have advantages such as high reliability, high density, and high performance, low power consumption, and short design cycles.

articleTitle: The Effect of Epoxy Molding Compound Dispensing Uniformity on PoP Warpage
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The package on package (PoP) assembly technology plays a significant role in the semiconductor packaging industry. Because of its strict requirements on thickness, the research of warpage is also paid much attention to it. In this paper, the impact of the assembly process on package warpage is the key idea. Three groups of experiment designs are to analyze the epoxy molding compound (EMC) dusting uniformity in the molding process whether affects the warpage value of the package. By analyzing the box plot of area visual inspection (AVI) warpage data at room temperature and the filler content of the package cross section, it is concluded that the filler content will be effected due to different EMC dispensing uniformity and thus have an impact on package warpage.

articleTitle: Application of ANSYS Sherlock in the fatigue lifetime evaluation of board level solder joint
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the widespread application of 5G products, the reliability of the products is also receiving increasing attention. The traffic load is changing within the product, with the combination of the ambient temperature, one major failure for electronic component is the solder joint crack issue due to the thermal stress and strain caused by the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch between printed circuit board (PCB) and components. The simulation evaluation method of solder joint reliability mainly focuses on using the finite element methods (FEM) to simulate and calculate the strain and energy solder joints. As it’s difficult to do lifetime evaluation for solder joint of entire board level, in this paper, we introduced ANSYS Sherlock software as a new prediction module for solder joint reliability risk evaluation on entire PCB board. After we found the risk component package with solder joint risk by Sherlock, we use FEM simulation for further check and plan long term temperature cycling test (LTC) for verification. FEM output the similar result as Sherlock. Solder crack issue was also found after LTC test which validated our simulation results.

articleTitle: Study of the ErP Directive EU 2019/1781 on the Ecological Assessment of Three-phase Asynchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The EU ErP Directive sets a framework of eco-design requirements for energy-using products covering the entire life cycle. In this paper, we studied the ecological assessment technology of three-phase asynchronous motor products, and considered the environmental impact of each stage of the product life cycle from design, manufacturing, transportation to end-of-life disposal, and conducted quantitative analysis of three-phase asynchronous motors by using special software for ecological design. Among the main components of the product, the three components (stator components, rotor components and junction box) have the greatest impact on the environment. The technical improvement of the product has significantly improved the energy efficiency level of the product

articleTitle: Deposition Efficiency Study on Wafer Level Gold Plating based on Cyanide-free Electrolyte
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Gold plating process is widely used in semiconductor industry. Due to environmental and safety issues, more and more wafer packaging factories began to devote themselves to the development of cyanide-free gold plating process. However, the current efficiency is a big challenge for the cyanide-free electrolyte plating process. This study focused on the increase of gold deposition efficiency on entire wafer. The gold plating process is achieved on the mass production tool from ACM with the mass production type electrolyte from EEJA. The gold film deposition efficiency is investigated by using various Paddle agitation speed. In the experiment, the motor speed was set to 0mm/s (no extra agitation), 120mm/s, 240mm/s, and 360mm/s. It was found that the agitation of paddle helped to increase the deposition thickness of the gold film, which reached a maximum when the paddle motion velocity was 240mm/s. Besides the above, 13 points were also measured on the whole wafer for plating uniformity. According to the experimental results, the agitation of the paddle also improved the uniformity of electroplating, achieving the best uniformity at a paddle speed of 240mm/s. The above improvement in current efficiency and electroplating uniformity can be attributed to the fact that paddle stirring accelerates the supplement of Au<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> on the wafer surface and makes the distribution of Au<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> concentration on the wafer surface more uniform.

articleTitle: A Novel Circular Position Sensitive Detector for Continuously High-Precision Angle Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Rotation angle measurement of servo motors is critical in the field of ultra-precision machining. Optical or magnetic encoders are usually used for angle measurement, with the disadvantages of poor immunity to interference, mechanical fragility, complex construction and high cost. In this paper, we proposed a novel circular position sensitive detector (CPSD) structure for robust measurement of the rotation angle with high accuracy and high resolution. The detection area of the CPSD is continuous, enabling full range detection from 0° to 360°. The calculation formula is analyzed using the current superposition principle, and an artificial neural network is constructed for error optimization. The average detection accuracy and resolution is simulated to be 2.96″ 1.62″, respectively. We have also designed the signal processing circuit for the CPSD, including I/V amplifier, analogue-to-digital converter and the FPGA development board. These results strongly illustrate the application potential of CPSD for rotational angle measurements with high accuracy, high resolution and high reliability.

articleTitle: Design Optimization for Dual Clip Flat Lead Package Assembly by Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Copper clip package plays a critical role in meeting the increasing requirement for high power density and high frequency switching applications. The dual clips concept with two dies within small outline package comes in place to meet the high customer’s requirements for power automotive application. As one of the challenges in package assembly design, the effect of clip and die design on function and reliability can be considered during the initial phase of package concept feasibility study. This paper focus on these factor effect for robust clip package design at initial stage of new package development by simulation. Simulation models are set up by considering different factors, such as to access the design for manufacturability, max device ratings, product and reliability performance such as thermal resistance and die stress performance during temperature cycle test (TCT). Comprehensive thermal, electrical and mechanical analyses are performed based on simulation results to show effect of these factors for selection of die design, single die with dual bond pads or two separated individual dies. This paper demonstrates a good case of simulation driven clip and die design selection for new package development of dual clip in small outline of flat lead package in Nexperia. Key learning from this study can be used to formulate simulation database and design guidelines for future product enhancement, reduce the design-to-implementation cycle time, identify high risk before fabrication and troubleshooting during production.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Oval Flip Chip Solder Bump
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the actual demand of the market, the miniaturized high density packaging of components is becoming more and more common. System ln a package enables higher density and more functional integration in limited space. Flip chip is a new surface mounting technology for microelectronics manufacturing. In terms of packaging substrate design, the traditional circular FC Bump substrate design has many layers of substrate and high cost. In this paper, a new oval FC solder bump is introduced to reduce the number of layers required in the substrate design, reduce the cost and improve the production efficiency of the FC substrate.

articleTitle: Case analysis on the fracture of deformed leads of the ceramic flat package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The leads of ceramic flat package (CFP) or ceramic quad flat package (CQFP) should be deformed before the component with such package is electronic assembled, and the deformation effect would directly influence the assembly reliability. The paper analyzes two failure cases of lead fracture after deformation and lead breaking after mechanical test. The mechanism of grain boundary weakness resulting from the solder element penetration is confirmed. Suggestions about developing, guarantee and application are proposed in order to improve the reliability of such leads during application.

articleTitle: The reliability study on electrochemical migration evaluations for common substrates in power electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The miniaturized electronic devices are driving the development of higher density and integration of smaller components, which leads to reliability issues for electronic devices in harsh environments such as high temperature and high voltage. Electrochemical migration (ECM) is an important phenomenon related to the failure of electronic devices, causing short-circuit failures between closed metal surfaces and significantly reducing the reliability of electronic products. Moreover, the complexity of the materials used in modern circuit boards, the increased number of component pins and the reduced spacing of multilayer boards have all increased the risk of failure from electrochemical migration, making it an unavoidable failure threat in the reliability of electronic packaging. Recently, silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) ceramics have received wide attentions due to their excellent mechanical properties, such as high bending strength and high fracture toughness. The Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> substrate is not only responsible for electrical connections and mechanical support, but reliability is also important. However, the effect of Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> ceramic substrate on the reliability of electrochemical migration is rarely studied.In this paper, we use the water drop (WD) test to investigate the effect of four commonly used substrate material types (aluminum nitride, alumina, silicon nitride, PCB) and bias voltages on electrochemical migration experiments in electronic products. The WD test was chosen due to the fact that results on the effect of conditions such as electrode spacing, bias voltage, ion type and concentration in the liquid on electrochemical migration can be obtained in a short time. During electrochemical migration, samples were recorded in situ under an ultra-deep field microscope (MPI TS150) for video of the entire WD process. The mean time to failure was determined based on the first sharp increase in current and the dendritic bridges observed under the optical microscope. In addition, the morphology of the dendrites and elemental analysis of the post-experimental samples were carried out by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy spectroscopy (EDS) and XPS, while the statistical electrochemical migration failure times were monitored in real time.

articleTitle: Simulation of Crack Initiation and Propagation in Solder Layer of IGBT Module under Temperature Shock in 3D Model Based on Phase Field Method
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The crack initiation and propagation in the solder layer of 3D IGBT module model under temperature shock test were simulated using the viscoplastic phase field method (PFM). The effects of three positions (corner, edge, and center) of perforating voids in the solder layer on crack initiation and propagation are studied and compared. The crack area and rate of crack growth were also calculated. Results reveal that the crack initiates at the corner of the interface between the chip and solder layer, and extends to the center in arc-shaped, regardless of whether there are perforating voids. The perforating voids at the corner and edge of the solder layer promote the crack propagation slightly in the early stage. However, the voids at the corner have more impact on the crack growth compared to the voids at the edge. Meanwhile, the voids at the center have almost no influence on the crack growth.

articleTitle: Improving Moldability by Regulating Thixotropy of Epoxy Molding Compounds
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In terms of the epoxy molding compound (EMC) fluid, flash length and the formation of the air trap void during molding is highly related to the moldability and rheological properties, which are influenced by the thixotropy of the fluid. It is of significance to study the moldability and rheological properties to provide theoretical guidance for the molding processing. In this work, the relationship between the thixotropy and moldability of the EMC fluid was systematically investigated, and the thixotropy of EMC can be regulated by the introduction of fumed silica in EMC. The thixotropy of the EMC fluid at 175 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C was characterized by a rotational rheometer, and the moldability can be reflected by the flash length test as well as the air trap void inspection with the real package. The rheological results show that with the increase of the fumed silica, the area of thixotropic loop of the EMC fluid is increased, indicating that the thixotropy of the EMC fluid is enhanced with the addition of the fumed silica. The flash length test results display that the flash length of the EMC fluid becomes shorter with increasing the fumed silica. The scanning acoustic microscope (SAM) results of the real package exhibit that when the content of the fumed silica is 0.3wt%, the air trap void defect ratio in package is also less, indicating that this addition amount is the optimal content for moldability. The moldability of EMC can be improved by regulating the thixotropy.

articleTitle: Ad/desorption mechanism of amine-terminated polyoxypropylene suppressor in advanced acid copper electroplating
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Acid copper electroplating is a fundamental process in modern integrated circuits and printed-circuit boards industries, where micro- to nano- sized interconnect patterns (e.g., line, pad or via structures) can be bottom-up manufactured with excellent service reliability and cost performance. Organic additives are indispensable in acid copper electroplating, which not only affects the electrocrystallization process, but also controls the deposit morphologies. However, the interfacial adsorption mechanism of some industrial additives is not clearly understood. For example, suppressor wtih ethylene oxide (EO) and propylene oxide (PO) block copolymers (EPE). In this work, amine-terminated PO and EO suppressors were comparatively studied in acid copper electroplating, formulated with bis-(sodium sulfopropyl)-disulfide (SPS) accelerator and Janus green (JGB). Ad/desorption mechanism of PO in acid copper plating system and its interaction with other additives are revealed by electrochemical and quantum chemical analyses. The morphologies and crystal orientations of copper films electroplated at different current densities (1, 5 and 10 ASD) are characterized. The results demonstrate that due to existence of hydrophobic methyl groups, PO shows dynamic ad/desorption alternation and limited surface coverage. The unique ad/desorption mechanism of PO is believed to synergize with EO in adsorption of EPE suppressors.

articleTitle: High Temperature Storage Simulation and Strain Analysis of Solder Ball in Fan-Out Wafer Level Package (FOWLP)
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: More and more Fan-Out Wafer Level Package (FOWLP) are introduced to the harsh work environment such as high temperature storage. The high temperature storage reliability of packages and solder balls will face more serious challenges. In this paper, the effects of storage time, Epoxy Molding Compounds (EMC) material and EMC thickness on the high temperature storage reliability of FOWLP were investigated. The Garofaro-Arrhenius model is used as the creep constitutive model. The stress and creep strain responses of solder balls during high temperature storage were simulated. The simulation results show that as the storage time increases, the creep strain increases sharply at first and then approaches an equilibrium value slowly. The creep strain of solder ball accumulates continuously. The maximum creep strain solder ball away from the center of the printed circuit board (PCB). The weak position of solder ball is located at the interface between ubm and solder ball on the die side. With the increase of EMC thickness, the creep strain of solder ball decreases gradually. Increasing the thickness of EMC and selecting high Young's modulus EMC materials can improve the reliability of FOWLP in high temperature storage.

articleTitle: Fine Pitch Wafer-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding for Three-Dimensional Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the demand for advanced semiconductor packaging technology continues to rise, achieving precise control of the wafer bonding process becomes increasingly critical for optimal performance. This research paper focuses on the development of a fine-pitch hybrid wafer bonding technique specifically designed for heterogeneous integration applications. The objective is to enable high-density interconnections and enhance electrical performance through the bonding of Cu and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> wafers featuring 15μm spaced Cu pads. The experimental section provides a comprehensive account of the study, covering various aspects such as layout design, preparation, and the bonding process. This includes the fabrication of Cu pads and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> passivation layers, chemical mechanical polishing (CMP), and alignment bonding. Furthermore, the research also investigates Cu-Cu die-to-die bonding utilizing a (100)-oriented single-crystal Cu top die paired with a Si substrate. Microstructure analysis demonstrates a well-fused bonding interface characterized by a highly preferred (100)-oriented Cu film. The insights obtained from this study contribute to the advancement of wafer-level hybrid bonding techniques for three-dimensional integration technology. This research serves as a valuable contribution to the ongoing development and refinement of advanced semiconductor packaging methods.

articleTitle: The crack propagation analysis in an IGBT package under in-service conditions by VCCT
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) are critical power components used in electric vehicles, new energy systems, and industrial automation applications. As the performance requirements for power devices continues to grow, ensuring IGBT reliability has become a significant challenge due to the high currents and severe temperature variations during operation, especially during the long period of working conditions. One of the common failures, i.e., the propagation of cracks in the package, can seriously affect the electrical and thermal performance of IGBTs, such as the reduced efficiency, increased power dissipation, and ultimately device damage. Previous studies have focused on reliability testing with little consideration of the actual operating conditions. Therefore, a deeper understanding of crack propagation under in-service conditions is essential to help improve the reliability of power devices. This study focuses on the crack propagation in a typical IGBT with a transistor outline (TO) package under its in-service conditions. Three-dimensional (3D) structures of the IGBT package were built in Abaqus according to the designed dimensions. A user subroutine was developed to involve the power dissipation on the chip as a function of case temperature to simulate the operating conditions. The crack propagation was predicted along vulnerable interfaces using the 3D virtual crack closure technique (VCCT) which assumes that the energy required to close a crack is the same as that required to create it. The energy release rate calculated along straight crack and quarter circular crack fronts showed that shear modes primarily drive crack propagation and the most vulnerable interface is at between the epoxy molding compound (EMC) and exposed pad.

articleTitle: Effects of Plasma Treatment on Adhesion and Flow Behavior of Underfill in 2.5D Electric Package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Plasma surface treatment technology is widely used in IC packaging industry to enhance the process performance and reliability of underfill. This study investigates the effect of plasma treatment on filling time, void count and flow mark of the underfill in 2.5D package. The filling time of underfill in a dummy TV obtained a reasonable score of 12 min 15 s at 200 s plasma treatment, and the void and flow mark in this dummy TV were significantly improved after this plasma treatment. Meanwhile, the effect of plasma treatment on the interfacial adhesion strength of underfill on PI-coated RDL-interposer was investigated. The interfacial adhesion strength between underfill and PI-coated RDL-interposer peaked with 200s plasma treatment at room temperature, 260 °C and after PCT. The morphology and composition of the untreated and plasma-treated PI-coated RDL-interposer were characterized to investigate the effect of plasma treatment on surface of PI-coated RDL-interposer. This study will aid the optimization of plasma treatment condition to improve the processibility and reliability of underfill, thus increasing the reliability of the 2.5 D package with PI-coated RDL-interposer.

articleTitle: Selective Wet Etching Technology in 3D NAND Flash Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 3D NAND has become one of the most promising storage devices to meet the growing demand for large-capacity data storage. Stacking more Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers in 3D NAND is essential for increasing its storage density. However, as the number of stacked layers increased, technical difficulties including poor etch selectivity, redeposition on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers, and dissolution of poly-Si channel arise in the wet etching process of 3D NAND manufacturing, seriously damaging the performance and reliability of the device. In this paper, we studied the kinetic effects of fluorine- and silane-containing additives on Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> etching. The additives affected the etch rates of Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by changing the activation energies, thereby adjusting the etch selectivity. Additionally, the redeposited colloidal silica gel on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers and the detrimental dissolution of poly-Si channel were characterized. These results will contribute to exploring solutions for challenges in 3D NAND manufacturing.

articleTitle: Lifetime model of copper pillar micro-bump interconnects under bi-directional pulse current stress
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The electromigration life of interconnects under pulsed current will change significantly compared to DC conditions. To accurately predict the reliability life of micro-copper pillar bump under pulsed current stress, in this paper, based on the built electromigration test system, accelerated life tests were carried out at 110°C, 125°C and 140°C temperature coupled 100Hz frequency bidirectional pulsed current 2.5-3.0 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The effects of parameters such as temperature, current density, and forward current percentage on electromigration life were investigated. The reliability life model of micro-copper pillar bump interconnects under bi-directional current stress was successfully established by introducing a damage recovery factor γ into the Black equation. The modeling establishment process entirely considers the effect of the Joule heating effect, fitting the current density index n is 15.52, activation energy Q is 1.09 eV, and the damage recovery coefficient γ is determined to be -0.81. No significant correlation is found between γ and temperature and current density performance. The lifetime model shows that the change in current direction will slow down the electromigration effect of the micro bump but will not eliminate the resulting electrically induced damage. The mathematical relationships the model establishes between parameters such as temperature, current density, time proportion of the forward current, and electromigration lifetime of copper pillar bumps under bidirectional current are important engineering references to support high-density packages' design and lifetime prediction.

articleTitle: A high-performance visible framing ICCD camera base on the image intensifier
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The visible framing ICCD camera is a high-speed 2D image detector that can obtain the low-light emission phenomena, such as explosion imaging, fluorescence imaging, time of flight imaging and surface defects. The framing camera mainly includes an image splitter, four ICCD cameras, the precision delay module and the gate module. A highperformance visible framing intensified charge-coupled device (ICCD) camera was successfully designed and applied to the explosion measurement. The quantum efficiency at the wavelength of 496 nm was 15.72% and the ICCD camera gain was more than 3.0 × 104. Using the designed gate module, the high-voltage pulse width of 53 ns was obtained in the test experiment. Based on the Rayleigh criterion, the spatial resolution of framing ICCD camera was 32 lp/mm. The experimental results shown that the designed framing ICCD camera was an important instrument, which was beneficial for recording and studying on the ultra-fast low light process.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic-assisted soldering of Al alloy using a novel Ni mesh reinforced Sn-9Zn solder
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Ultrasonic-assisted soldering technique has gained extensive application for low-temperature bonding of Al alloys. However, using common Sn-based solders restricts the further improvement of the reliability of Al alloy joints due to their poor mechanical properties. In this study, we developed a novel low-temperature composite solder by incorporating the regular Ni mesh into Sn-9Zn solder and soldered 7075 Al alloy by ultrasonic-assisted soldering technique. The microstructure and shear properties of joints were explored with regard to the effects of soldering time and mesh counts. Results illustrated that solder seams were primarily composed of Ni mesh, Sn-Zn eutectic, β-Sn, η-Zn solid solution, and α-Al solid solution. Among them, α-Al solid solutions increased with extending the soldering time. Meanwhile, the enrichment of Zn and O elements was detected at the Al substrate interface. Significantly, the joints using 250#Ni mesh exhibited superior shear properties than those using 100#Ni mesh. The joint showed the highest shear strength of 74.39 MPa under soldering for 5 s. The above findings would broaden the technical approach of Al alloy bonding and promote engineering applications.

articleTitle: High-efficiency and low-loss thin film lithium niobate modulator
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Recently, lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) modulators have emerged as a promising device in the field of optical communications due to its excellent material properties. However, the lack of an effective optical interface between the LNOI waveguide and the optical fiber makes it difficult to further improve the practicality of LNOI devices. Here, we proposed a high performance LNOI modulator with low loss edge coupler. The edge coupler consists of LN bilayer taper and silica-based PLC. The simulation results show a low coupling loss of 0.11dB/facet, low half-wave voltage product of 2.5 V•cm and a large 3-dB EO bandwidth more than 100 GHz. These results open a path for lithium niobate photonic integration circuit (PIC) and low-cost optical packaging.

articleTitle: Study of flip ultrasonic bonding process with Non-conductive paste
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the process of interconnecting flip chip packages, the reliability of chip interconnection is enhanced by employing underfill technology after the bonding is completed. However, with the continuous reduction in chip pitch and fill gap, the conventional underfill technique utilizing capillary action fails to meet the requirements. This paper investigates a novel filling technique that combines inverted ultrasonic bonding with non-conductive paste. The aim is to achieve high-quality solder joint interconnection interfaces through low-temperature ultrasonic bonding without utilizing the conventional underfill that depend on capillary action. Experimental results demonstrate that a reliable solder joint interconnection with a high-quality interface morphology is formed between the chip and the substrate when employing the bonding process with a bonding head temperature of 100° C, bonding force of 24N, ultrasonic power of 10w, and a duration of 3s, while the substrate remains at room temperature. Furthermore, the study examines the impact of bonding force and ultrasonic time on the formation of a desirable interfacial morphology and discusses the mechanism of non-conductive paste (NCP) in the ultrasonic bonding process.

articleTitle: Enabling Zero Delamination between Lead Frame Surface and Epoxy Molding Compound at Zero-hour and MSL1 in Leaded Package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Automotive product requires high reliability test performance. The surface between lead frame (LF) and epoxy molding compound (EMC) is one of important factors for reducing the delamination at zero hour and moisture sensitivity level I (MSL-1).This work aims to study mold tooling design to eliminate the delamination by optimizing dummy gate and draft angle.The result of study can meet the zero delamination at zero hour and MSL-1.

articleTitle: Development and Prospect of Coaxial Through-Silicon Via in 3D Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Three-dimensional integration technology is characterized by high density, high performance, and multi-function, which has promoted the further development of integrated circuits. At present, there is an increasing demand for novel high-frequency vertical connections in 3D integrated systems. Using conventional through-silicon via (TSV) structures at high frequencies has limitations due to coupling noise and crosstalk. Therefore, coaxial TSV structures with self-shielding capability have great application prospects in wireless communication systems, RF modules, 5G applications, and other fields. Over the past decade, coaxial TSV structures have attracted widespread attention, and significant progress has been made in the study of their parasitic effects, equivalent circuit models, and transmission characteristics, and new structures and materials of coaxial TSV proposed to suit the needs of different three-dimensional integration applications. However, the difficulty of manufacturing has become a key bottleneck restricting the application of coaxial TSV. This article reviews the relevant research literature on coaxial TSVs, classifies and summarizes the main literature in recent years, focusing on the latest progress and challenges in coaxial TSVs in technology and equivalent circuit models, summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of coaxial or quasi coaxial TSVs with new structures or materials, and prospects the research prospects in these fields.

articleTitle: Influence of Cu heat sink on heat dissipation of QFN package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the key factors that contribute to the success of QFN component applications, namely, structural design and thermal analysis. By means of extensive research, we have successfully developed a customized Cu heat sink QFN model that is specifically designed to meet the stringent requirements of package design and assembly. This model incorporates innovative features and considerations derived from our comprehensive investigations, allowing for an optimized thermal management solution within the QFN package. The design and implementation of the Cu heat sink serve to address the increasingly demanding challenges associated with heat dissipation in QFN packages, ensuring efficient thermal performance and enhancing the overall reliability of the package. Through our research efforts, we have made advancements in QFN design and assembly. Using finite element simulation techniques, we are able to analyze the temperature and stress levels of the package, ensuring optimal heat dissipation. Our experimental results have demonstrated that the heat sinks, located both inside and outside of the QFN, are highly effective in reducing QFN temperature while stress vary slightly. It is evident from simulations that adding both internal and external heat sinks in QFN package can significantly improve heat dissipation and enhance packaging reliability.

articleTitle: The EBG Structure for Mutual Coupling Suppression Between Antenna Units
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The fifth generation of mobile communication technology (5G) is developing rapidly, and the 5G mobile communication band is leaping toward high frequency, so it is of great practical significance to study 5G array antennas. In this article, a binary microstrip antenna array with an array element spacing of 0.7λ and a resonant point in the 24.75—27.5 GHz band with a continuous −10 dB bandwidth of 2.56 GHz in the millimeter wave band is designed for the future 5G millimeter wave communication system. However, surface electromagnetic wave can cause coupling, disturb the distribution of antenna ground current and weaken the performance of antenna arrays. Research shows that Electromagnetic Bandgap (EBG) structure is periodic, which has the characteristics of band resistance, slow wave and high resistance, and can stop electromagnetic wave transmission in a certain bandwidth range, therefore, the article mainly studies and designs EBG structure and measures the band gap characteristics of EBG structure using the suspended microstrip line method, and applying the EBG structure to the 5G millimeter wave band antenna array, HFSS simulation results show that loading EBG structure is able to improve the isolation between antenna units.

articleTitle: Wafer-level controllable graphene transfer and electrical characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Two-dimensional carbon material, represented by graphene, possesses inherent advantages, including high electron mobility, high thermal conductivity, and low thermal noise. One of the key solutions to the material selection of the next generation integrated circuit and electronic components is through controllable growth of innovative structure and accurate intercalating doping which open the energy bandgap of graphene, forming excellent electrical properties. Remarkable advancements have been achieved in the controllable growth and precise structure of graphene control, However, the controlled transfer of graphene at the wafer level remains challenging, impeding the large-scale production of graphene-based devices. In this paper, trivial transfer graphene was used to simplify the fabrication process of low-dimensional carbon-based devices. A 4-inch wafer, containing graphene field-effect transistors (FETs), was fabricated with a yield of approximately 90%. It demonstrates the nondestructive transfer of graphene on both flat and stepped surfaces. The simplified fabrication process, along with the electrical characterization, has revealed their crucial roles in the large-scale production of graphene-based devices, thereby highlighting the broad application prospects of graphene-based integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Copper electroplating of through silicon vias (TSV) using a series of nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compounds
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 3D packaging has broad applications due to its high integration, lightweight, small package size and low cost. Through silicon vias (TSV) have attracted much attention as the only packaging technology to achieve vertical interconnection. The quality of superior filling by electroplated copper (Cu) determines the reliability of TSV in electronic devices. As one of the most vital additives, levelers are always the confidential part of electrolyte formulations. In general, a nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound can be employed as a potential leveler for TSV filling, like Janus Green B (JGB). However, the mechanism of the leveler during copper electrodeposition is shrouded in mystery. Whether the nitrogen-nitrogen double bond (-N=N-) or the nitrogen cation (N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) in the JGB molecule take the effect in electroplating is still a hot topic of debate. Here, three levelers with or without -N=N-, containing JGB, phenosafranin (PS) and phenazine methosulfate (PMS), are utilized in the TSV electroplated process to explore the active site of molecules. The filling performance of different levelers were compared. Electrochemical measurements was used to investigate the leveling mechanism. The optical microscope (OM) and ultraviolet spectrophotometer (UV-vis) were used to characterize the filling quality and the change of electrolyte before and after electrodeposition. The results of characterizations confirmed that both -N=N- and N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> play a certain effect in electroplating, the reductive reaction of -N=N- competes with Cu reduction and the electrostatic adsorption of N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and Cl<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> enables the deposition inhibition of Cu at salient sites.

articleTitle: Research of Super Fine Gold Wire Bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous development of electronic packaging technology,microwave multi-chip components are constantly developing toward miniaturization,light weight, multi-function and high reliability. Conventional gold wire is hard to satisfy the requirements of the rapid development of advanced packaging. In this paper, the optimal process parameters of 10 μm gold wire bonding are analyzed with the methods of variance parameters and tests, based on destructive bond pull test results under different parameters. The reliability of 10 μm gold wire bonding is evaluated by studying bond pull test results after environmental test. Meanwhile, the current withstanding capability of 10 μm gold wire is studied, which has a certain guiding significance for the eletrical design of advanced packaging.

articleTitle: Thermal Stress Field of Al2O3/Al-Ni Nanofoil/Ni Solder Joints by Self-propagation Reactions
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The connection between Al2O3 ceramics and metal has always been a difficult problem. In this study, the self-propagating combustion reaction of Al-Ni nanofoils was used as the heat source to interconnect Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramics and metal Ni. Based on Comsol multi-physical field simulation software, the distribution and variation history of temperature and stress in solder joints during self-propagating combustion reaction were simulated and analyzed, including the change of transient temperature and thermal stress with reaction time, and the melting time of filler metal. The influence of solder layer thickness and Al-Ni nanofoils thickness on temperature and stress field of solder joints were investigated.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Solder Ball and RDL on Fan-Out Wafer Level Package under Random Vibration
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of product applications, Fan-Out Wafer Level Package (FOWLP) is increasingly used in the field of portable electronics. In the shipping condition, the portable electronic device is inevitably exposed to vibration load, which will affect the solder ball and redistribution layer (RDL) of the package. In this paper, the random vibration of fan-out package is analyzed by finite element numerical simulation. The stress of solder ball and RDL at different positions on the test board is analyzed. The hazardous package is located in the middle of the test board near the long side, with the maximum equivalent stress on solder ball and RDL. The package with the highest reliability is located in the middle of the test board near the short side, with the minimum equivalent stress on solder ball and RDL. The Steinberg model based on Gaussian distribution is selected to evaluate the cumulative damage index (CDI) of solder ball and RDL, based on Manson-coffin equation and the linear fatigue damage accumulation criterion. The results show that these packages can pass one hour random vibration test based on the current load.

articleTitle: Study on Failure Modes of High Speed Optical Communication PCB
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a converter of photoelectric signals, the optical communication module is the basic component of the 5G network physical layer, and is also the core device for connecting optical equipment and optical fibers. The raw materials required for optical communication module products mainly include optical devices, circuit chips, PCBs, and structural components. As the circuit carrier for packaging optical communication modules, high speed PCB products are the electrical interface, optical interface, and electrical signal transmission carrier of optical modules, as well as the device power supply provider. The quality and reliability of their products directly affect the quality and reliability of the optical module system and the entire machine. Based on the technical characteristics and reliability requirements of high speed optical communication PCBs, this article analyzes the root causes of failures, discusses improvement suggestions, and provides reference for peers in the industry around four common failure cases: wire bonding failure, Conductive anodic filament (CAF) failure, gold finger corrosion failure, and laser blind hole open circuit failure.

articleTitle: Test and evaluation of process adaptability and environmental adaptability for reliability application of a thermal insulation adhesive
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Based on the reliability application requirements of space borne products for thermal insulation adhesives, the process adaptability and environmental adaptability of newly two-component thermal insulation adhesive were tested and evaluated. Through the design and manufacture of the typical BGA device process test piece of the satellite terminal machine. the micro-pore filling process technology is used to fill the thermal insulation adhesive. After the industrial CT scanning detection, the filling void rate is less than 10%. At the same time, the module simulation parts of space borne products were designed and made, and filled with thermal insulation adhesive. The acceptance level environment and reliability tests of the simulated parts were carried out, such as temperature cycle, sinusoidal vibration, random vibration and thermal vacuum. The electrical performance indicators and monitoring process of the simulator before and after the environmental test have no obvious differences. and meet the index design requirements. There are no defects introduced in the process of filling the thermal insulation adhesive in the simulator which verifies that the simulator has the ability to withstand the working stress and environmental stress, and the thermal insulation adhesive has no abnormal impact on the electrical performance index of the simulator, which meets the requirements of heat dissipation and high load resistance of space borne products. and realizes reliable application.

articleTitle: Highly conductive stable grid electrode via electroplating Ni on EHD-printed patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Transparent metal grid electrodes are key components in a variety of optoelectronic devices, including liquid crystal displays (LCDs), organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), organic solar cells (OSCs), and touch screens. However, the resolution of traditional printing technology is relatively low, and it is difficult to achieve a precision below 50 μm. Therefore, in this paper, electrohydrodynamic printing (EHD printing) is used to improve the pattern resolution, and a grid electrode with a linewidth of 30 μm was prepared. The properties of the Ag nanoink and its effect on the printing pattern were explored. Then, the process window for stable cone injection was found. Finally, the method of electroplating Ni was applied to the high-precision pattern of EHD printing to achieve the improvement of conductivity at room temperature.

articleTitle: Impact of Zn Content on Cu/Al Joints with (Cu+Zn+Al) Mixed Particles
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this study, 1-μm Zn particles were mixed with 28-μm Cu particles and 28-μm Al particles as solder to scrutinize the influence of varied Zn content on Cu/Al interconnects. The interconnection of Cu/Al heterogeneous metals is achieved with the use of ultrasonic-assisted. A relationship has been observed between the Zn content and shear strength of joints. Initially, with an increase in Zn content, there is a positive effect on the shear strength; however, after reaching an optimum value, further increases in Zn content leads to a subsequent decline in shear strength. The maximum shear strength of joints was found to be 23.34 MPa at a Zn content of 70%. Due to the increase of Zn content, a more complete and continuous Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> compound can be formed at the Cu-side interface, and more Al-Zn solid solution can also be formed at the Al-side, allowing the solder particles to achieve a tight connection. However, too much Zn can lead to the aggregation of Zn particles after the reaction of Zn particles with Cu and Al in the solder, which fails to generate compounds with Cu and solid solutions with Al, and leads to the loss of strength.

articleTitle: Accurate Assessment of Young's Modulus of Sintered Ag Joints by Nanoindentation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, wide band gap (WBG) semiconductors, represented by SiC and GaN, have been utilized in power devices due to their superior properties. High operating temperatures of WBG devices present a challenge to conventional die-attach materials. Ag sintering technology provides a decent solution for realizing the die attachment of WBG power devices because of the numerous advantages of sintered Ag joints. The low Young's modulus of sintered Ag layer can effectively alleviate the thermal stress Generally, Young's modulus of sintered Ag layer has a close relationship with its microstructure, which is significantly influenced by the sintering process. In order to accurately assess Young's modulus of sintered Ag joints, we designed different methods by modulating the solvent evaporation mode and interfacial contact mode to find a more accurate and convenient way to measure Young's modulus of sintered Ag by nanoindentation. By placing a surface-modified Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) sheet on the sintered Ag layer (the PTFE sheet can be removed after sintering), Young's modulus of the sintered Ag joint can be more accurately and conveniently tested. When comparing sintered Ag joints of different print thicknesses, Young's modulus obtained using this method is close to that of a real sintered Ag joint, with a difference of less than 10%, due to the fact that the microstructure of the samples obtained by this method is close to that of a real joint. In addition, we construct the relationship between print thickness and Young's modulus and find that the print thickness of the sintered Ag joints does not significantly affect Young's modulus due to the similar microstructure of the samples at different thicknesses, which have very similar porosity. We think that this research provides a new perspective on the study of Young's modulus of sintered Ag and can better promote the development of sintering Ag technology.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of TSV with design factors
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: TSV is a technology that connects electrodes by drilling vias in the interposer. TSV technology offers advantages in terms of miniaturization, fast signal transmission, large capacity, and low power consumption. However, as chips become highly integrated, heat dissipation problems are getting severe. In this paper, the heating value of TSV interposer was analyzed by diameter, pitch, and aspect ratio. Icepak of Ansys 2022 R2 was used as an analysis tool, and the model was designed in the form of a 2.5D package including a logic chip and a memory chip. As a result the simulation, among the three design factors, diameter, aspect ratio, and pitch have the greatest influence in the order

articleTitle: Double-decker silsesquioxane-doped benzocyclobutene functionalized siloxane polymer for low k materials
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Benzocyclobutene (BCB) resins have been widely used in the microelectronics industry because of their excellent thermal, mechanical, and low k properties. In our previous work, we have prepared a BCB functionalized silphenylene-siloxane resin with good thermostability (Td5 > 490 °C in nitrogen). However, the dielectric constant of this BCB resin exceeds 2.8 and is expected to decrease. Herein, a linear BCB - functionalized polymer with a double-decker silsesquioxanes (DDSQ) doped silphenylene-siloxane backbone (DDSQ-PhBVSi) has been prepared using a Piers–Rubinsztajn reaction. It was cured at temperatures above 180 °C to obtain a thermoset. DDSQ with two reactive hydrosilyl groups is considered as a potential monomer to decrease the dielectric constant. The BCB group is introduced as a post-curing group to improve thermal and mechanical properties. Owing to the DDSQ units and the highly cross-linked structure, the thermoset exhibits a high initial storage modulus (>1.6 GPa at 25 °C) and good thermostability (Td5 > 495 °C in nitrogen). In addition, it exhibits good dielectric properties with a low k (2.69) and a low dissipation factor (<0.001) at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Effects of dishing and annealing temperature on wafer to wafer hybrid bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding technology is one of the most advanced interconnection techniques in terms of performance and integration density. However, the dishing effects introduced by the chemical mechanical polishing process prior to hybrid bonding can significantly impact the quality of the bonding. In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) was employed to investigate the influence of dishing effects and annealing temperature on the quality of wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding. The simulation of Cu-Cu diffusion bonding process took into consideration the dishing value, annealing temperature, and annealing time. Extending the bonding time could improve the bonding quality. Increasing the bonding temperature could also enhance the degree of interface bonding. However, when the dishing values were 10 Å and 20 Å, even with prolonged bonding time and elevated bonding temperature, it was not possible to ensure a void-free bonding process. The dishing value was the most critical factor determining the presence of voids in the bonded interface. Under a constant annealing temperature, if voids existed at the bonding interface, the volume of interface voids followed a power-law relationship with both the initial dishing values and the annealing time.

articleTitle: A Novel Focused Induction Heating Method For The Interconnection Between High-power Devices And Integrated Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: High-power devices are widely used in power supply, motor drive, medical treatment, and industrial automation. Hence, the interconnection of high-power devices to complicated circuit boards is critical. Due to the presence of large heat dissipation pins in high-power devices, there is a need for high energy input at localized solder joint locations during interconnection. However, there are relatively few localized heating processes suitable for such high-energy input, leading challenges on the interconnection of high-power devices with complex circuit boards. This work proposes a novel focused induction heating method (N-FIHM) combining external magnetizer and internal magnetizer to focus the magnetic field and increase the induction heating efficiency. Results showed that the N-FIHM can better focus the magnetic field at the solder joint position and increase the joint temperature. Compared the traditional induction heating method, the magnetic field density at the solder joint increases by a factor of 7, from 0.02 T to 0.14 T, and the temperature of the solder joint increases significantly by a factor of 6.9 (from 45 °C to 310 °C) with the same coil position and heating time.In addition, the study explores the influence mechanism of the structural parameters of the external tapered magnetizer on the magnetic field focusing and heating efficiency. The structural parameters include the distance between the inner and outer magnetizers, the wall thickness of the outer tapered magnetizer, the distance between the outer tapered magnetizer and the substrate, the height of the outer tapered magnetizer, and the inner diameter of the outer tapered magnetizer. It was found that the distance between inner and outer magnetizers has the greatest impact on heating efficiency. The solder joint temperature increases rapidly from the minimum value of 120 °C to the maximum value of 401 °C.

articleTitle: Influence of pin position on the CDM peak current based on 2.5D and 2D package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The impact of pin position for ESD charged device model (CDM) peak current of two different types of package which are 2.5D CoWoS(50*50mm) and 2D FCBGA(45*45mm) with same die inside is investigated. CDM current waveform properties show a strong dependence on pin location due to package parasitic parameters, the closer to the package center, the higher peak current of CDM. Thus, the inner pins are generally receiving higher stress levels which means that pins with the same ESD circuitry will give different CDM performance depending on their relative position on the package. This phenomenon should be concerned for some pins that are sensitive to CDM current.

articleTitle: Time-of-Flight Mass Spectroscopic Studies of Non-Stick on Pad Issues in Wire Bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Traditional Non-Stick on Pad (NSOP) analysis was typically carried out with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) surface analysis to find out any suspect contamination on the pad that may cause the non-stick issue. However, there are cases, in which their XPS analysis on the NSOP bond pad shows no difference in elemental composition when comparing to a good unit. In this paper, the time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) that has the sensitivity in ppm level much higher than the XPS sensitivity which is usually at 0.1% was used instead for the NSOP analysis. The results revealed there is indeed a very thin organic contamination on top surface of the affected pad when comparing to a good unit. After searching through their process materials and verified with TOF-SIMS test, the contamination was pinpointed to be possibly from the polyethylene glycol originated from the sawing surfactant.

articleTitle: Characterization Tests of Electrodeless Discharge Lamps for Hyperspectral Sensors Spaceborne Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Space-based hyperspectral cameras require onboard light sources for the calibration and degradation monitoring of their detectors. Electrodeless lamps (EDLs) are an interesting solution because they have features of the extremely long life. The high brightness and wide spectral range, which spans from ultraviolet to infrared wavelengths, making light sources with narrow and intense spectral lines are a popular choice for scientific instruments. In this paper, an inductively-coupled krypton lamp was demonstrated as a calibration source, which offers a longer service life compared to traditional calibration sources and demonstrated that these EDLs are suitable for space applications. During testing, the device demonstrated good performance, with the inductor coil’s current peaking at about 8A and the lamp’s start-up time being 200 microseconds.

articleTitle: A novel approach to 3D stacking of power chips with hot-via interconnections
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Eutectic bonding is the primary method of integrated packaging for achieving efficient heat dissipation in power chips. However, for specialized power chips for wire-free packages with hot-via interconnections between upper layer and the backside pads on the lower layer, achieving high-precision, zero-damage, and highly reliable eutectic bonding is challenging using conventional equipment and methods. This paper proposes a simple and efficient approach that employs a specially designed Si-based fixture and thermocompression bonding process to achieve eutectic bonding of such kind of power chips. The fixture is fabricated using MEMS technology and comprises two layers: a structural layer and a thermal barrier layer. The structural layer features numerous micro-cavities that enable effective avoidance of air bridges when power chips are placed face-down. The thermal barrier layer assists in controlling the temperature of the solder layer during back-end co-soldering, thereby enhancing the reliability of the solder joint. Finite element simulations were carried out to analyze the heat transfer path during the eutectic process. The results indicate that when the thickness of the barrier layer is 200 micrometers, the temperature of the bonding tool reaches 300℃, while the temperature of the solder layer reaches 280℃. Finally, we fabricated samples and conducted X-ray inspection, which showed satisfactory results in terms of alignment accuracy and soldering quality. This provides a feasible solution for high-precision and high-quality automated eutectic bonding of power chips in wire-free 3D stacking packages.

articleTitle: A Thermo-mechanical Coupled 3D Crystal Plasticity Finite Element Model for CASTIN Solder Alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As one of the fragile components in the package structure, solder joints are usually subjected to thermo-mechanical coupled loads. Therefore, it is essential to investigate the deformation behavior and constitutive model of solder joints for the reliability prediction of the whole packaging. As a kind of polycrystalline material, solder joints contain multiple grains with different orientations. As the electronic devices gradually decrease in size, the solder joints may only contain one or several grains, the conventional macro-phenomenological constitutive model is not able to describe the deformation at the grain scale caused by crystalline slip. In this paper, a finite element model on the basis of 3D crystal plasticity theory is proposed, in which the behavior of each grain is first investigated, and the overall behavior of the structure is obtained by calculating the average of all elements. Firstly, the models with 10, 40, and 100 grains are established to find out the influence of grains’ numbers on the overall behavior. Then, the strain rate jump experiments of CASTIN solder alloy are simulated using the appropriate model. The CASTIN solder alloy is stretched to 1.5% strain at strain rates of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> under temperatures of -55°C to 125°C, respectively. A comparison is made between the simulation results and the experimental results, the parameters of the established model are obtained through matching the experiment curves, and the effect of the temperature on the parameters is analyzed. The model then is used to investigate the deformation response of CASTIN alloy under the thermo-mechanical cycle tests without changing these parameters. It can be found that the proposed model can give reasonable predictions of CASTIN alloy under thermo-mechanical coupled loads.

articleTitle: A Study on Warpage Behavior of Underfill in Flip Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The reliability of electronic packaging is a systematic project, which involves aspects of the design of packaging structure, packaging process technology, characteristics of packaging materials, and the use of the environment. Various factors take effect on package defects and failures, such as material composition and properties, package design, environmental conditions, and process parameters. However, the phenomenon of warpage caused by the mismatch of thermal expansion coefficients between chips and substrates is one of the most important problems in device reliability research.The paper independently designed a test vehicle structure that simulates an actual chip to study the warpage behavior of underfill during curing and reflow soldering.
