articleTitle: High energy dissipation composite elastomer for application as a thermal interface material through solvent-induced dis-entanglement
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In recent years, miniaturization and integration have become the trend in electronic devices, and the resulting severe thermal bottlenecks cause up to 55% of electronic device failures. The use of functionally filled elastomer composites is the main way to address thermal failures in electronic devices. However, highly filled elastomer composites tend to have brittleness problems. Here, we propose a strategy to optimize the mechanical properties of elastomer composites by solvent-induced disentanglement of molecular chains. The excellent energy dissipation capability of the polymer network after the disentanglement endows the elastomer composites excellent stretchability (450%) and toughness (2.75MJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). The enhanced thermal conductivity is assisted by the high filled of thermal conductive fillers (1.66 W m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>). We believe that our work can provide new ideas for the development of next-generation high-performance elastomeric composites.

articleTitle: On-Chip Substrate Integrated Plasmonic Waveguide Bandpass Filter for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, a glass-based millimeter-wave (mm-W) bandpass filter (BPF) utilizing the half-mode substrate integrated plasmonic waveguide (HMSIPW) structure. The BPF's passband is independently controlled by adjusting the width of the half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) and the length of the HMSIPW slot. To facilitate its fabrication, the proposed BPF is designed based on wafer-level through glass via (TGV) technology. Compared to other integrated circuit (IC) fabrication processes, wafer-level TGV technology offers cost-effectiveness and facilitates mass production. The simulation results show an insertion loss of 0.75 dB at the center frequency of the proposed BPF, with a return loss below -13 dB within the passband.

Author Keywords: half mode substrate integrated plasmonic waveguide

articleTitle: An isogeometric boundary element scheme for transient heat transfer problems in electronic packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of electronic packaging technology, the packaging density of electronic components is increasing, and thermal issues have gradually been a main reason for electronic component failure. This paper proposes a transient isogeometric boundary element method (IGABEM) to solve the transient thermal problem in electronic packaging. The proposed method combines the advantages of isogeometric analysis (IGA) and boundary element method (BEM). Compared with finite element method, only the boundary element is needed in the computation, which reduces the preprocessing time since meshing process inside the computational domain being avoided. The radial integration method (RIM) is used to transform the domain integrals into equivalent boundary integrals. This work uses time marching method to handle equation that involves the time term. Finally, a transient heat transfer problem of a simplified chip-copper pillar bump structure is used to illustrate the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Verification of a Chinese Copper-system LTCC
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology is widely used in aerospace applications and is one of the main technologies for miniaturization of products. However, the current gold-system LTCC technology used in aerospace products is costly and cannot be used as ceramic housings. In this paper, we introduce a new Chinese high bending strength copper-system LTCC technology, which is aimed to solve the problems faced by the current gold-system LTCC. Copper-system LTCC takes advantage of copper's high conductivity (low conductor loss) and low raw material cost, while achieving a high bending strength comparable to that of high-temperature co-fired ceramics (HTCC). This paper first introduces the material properties of the copper-system LTCC, and then show the results of the experimental substrate fabrication and micro-assembly verification. The results demonstrate that it can provide a viable solution for future low-cost, high bending strength, high frequency aerospace applications.

articleTitle: Improving the interface bonding strength of epoxy adhesives for electronic packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In flip-chip packaging, the delamination between the chip and the underfill (UF) adhesive is the main problem of yield loss and reliability. The delamination at the interface of UF/chip or UF/package substrate will lead to interconnect cracking and chip package failure. In this study, the electron-withdrawing groups and electron-donating groups (fluorenyl and cyclohexane) were introduced into the epoxy backbone through molecular design to enhance the bonding strength of the epoxy adhesive to the encapsulation interfaces. The results indicate that the introduction of electron-withdrawing groups in epoxy adhesive can effectively improve the bonding strength between Si and PI interface and between Si and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface.

articleTitle: Study on cracking behavior of sintering silver joints based on cohesive zone model
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, Based on the experimental results of shear fracture tests of sintered silver joints, the finite element analysis of cracking and crack. propagation of sintered silver joints was carried out by using the cohesive zone model (CZM) and numerical calculation method. Through reverse analysis and experiments, bilinear cohesive zone model is adopted to simulate sintered silver joint failure, which could provide a theoretical guidance for reliability design of SiC power module.

articleTitle: Power noise coupling simulation of DDR4 for FCBGA Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of advanced packaging, the bump pitch on FCBGA packaging is also getting smaller and smaller. At present, the typical value of the packaging process is 130um, and the minimum can reach 90um pitch, and will be 60um in the future. Although the crosstalk between sensitive signals or power rails will be considered when arranging the bump, the ground bump will be used to isolate, but sometimes when the pins are dense, there is not enough space to arrange the ground bumps. This also makes the noise coupling problem between different power rails increasingly prominent. Therefore, it is necessary to correctly evaluate the noise coupling problem caused by the packaging design itself. This paper introduces the correct simulation flow of noise coupling between different power rails of DDR4 IP, and studies the influence of different termination. At the same time, we also explained why the traditional singal integrity(SI) method can not be used to evaluate the coupling noise for power integrity(PI). Alterlatively, an improved method is proposed, which can be used in the pre-PI simulation flow in the early stage of chip design. By comparing the post simulation results with real models, we found that the error between the two methods for coupling noise of VDDQCK is within 1. 5%. Using the same method, we also obtained the coupling noise of VDDPLL with high accuracy which is still within 1. 5%, that means the improved method is feasible. It can be used in the pre-PI simulation process to speed up the chip development cycle. It is very important for the early design stage of chips without CPM model.

articleTitle: Microstructure evolution and fracture mechanism of sintered nano-Ag joints on bare copper during high temperature aging
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Low-temperature sintering of nanoscale silver paste in die-attached interconnection has been widely applied in the packaging of high-power devices due to its excellent electrical properties, thermal properties, and high melting temperature. Herein, we investigated the reliability of pressure-assisted sintered silver joints on bare copper during high temperature storage (HTS) tests in air at 300 °C. It was found that after aging for a period of time, the copper oxide phase appeared in the sintered silver layer as a semi-closed loop. We found the existence of oxygen under high temperature aging could expand the pore size and rise the porosity of the sintered Ag film, which might introduce the nucleation site of the Cu oxide. Based on this, the growth mechanism of copper oxides was discussed and the growth model of the semi-closed loop structure was proposed. We also found the semi-closed loop structure had a certain hindering effect on the intrusion of oxygen into the interior of the sintered silver, which slowed down the degradation of the strength of the sintered silver joint. The fracture mechanism of sintered nano-Ag joints during high temperature aging process was also studied.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-thin vapor chamber based on graphite copper-clad film for thermal management in electronic devices
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As highly integrated and miniaturized power components rapidly develop, the extreme heat accumulation of electronic devices easily occurs, leading to an urgent demand for better thermal performance of heat dissipation devices. Besides, an efficient heat dissipation method was still essential for the development of flexible power components. Herein, a novel ultra-thin vapor chamber (UTVC) based on graphite copperclad film with a thickness of only 0.68 mm was fabricated by a simple hot pressing process, and the composite wick structure was used as a capillarity-enhanced structure and a supporting structure for vapor flowing. The different filling liquid mass and test orientations of UTVC were both discussed. The surface temperature, temperature difference, thermal resistance, and thermal conductivity of UTVC were experimentally investigated, respectively. The UTVC could achieve a uniform surface temperature distribution (below 7.5 W), a low temperature difference (less than 2℃ at 6.5 W), a low thermal resistance (0.33℃/W at 6.5 W), and a high thermal conductivity (beyond 10000 W/(m·K)) under different orientations. Moreover, UTVC also showed wonderful flexibility, providing a potential application in the field of flexible folding. Further research will be carried out based on its flexibility.

articleTitle: Synthesis and characterization of highly-dispersed copper submicron particles for low temperature sintering joints
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The wide band-gap semiconductors are increasingly used in high-power devices. Due to the increasing operating temperature of high-power devices, stringent matertial properties are required. Nano-Ag paste has been widely utilized in the interface connection of high-power devices. However, sintered Ag has migration and cost concern. Compared with Ag, copper is cheaper and has comparable electrical and thermal properties. Cu nanoparticles(CuNPs) are likely to aggregate and oxidizd, which prevents its application. It is indicated that the particle size of copper should be controlled carefully, by which high sintering performance and aggregation and oxidation resistance can be achieved. In this paper, antioxidant and highly-dispersed Cu submicron-particles(CuSPs) with an average particles size of 500 nm were synthesized. Polyvinyl pyrrolidone and ascorbic acid were used as mixed capping agents to enhance antioxidant properties and dispersibility. According to the result of XRD, peaks of oxidized copper were not detected. The Cu-Cu joints were prepared with pressure sintering in vacuum environment. The shear strengths of the joints were 80.89 MPa at 270°C for 10 minutes under 20 MPa, showing high reliability of the joints.

articleTitle: Study on Low-Temperature Bonding and Reliability of Nano-Twin Copper Micro-Cone Array
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: nano-twin copper (nt-Cu) has been a promising bonding material for its capability to control the unidirectional growth of intermetallic compounds (IMCs) and suppress the formation of Kirkendall voids at bonding interface. Furthermore, copper nano/micro cones have been applied in the field of low-temperature solid-state bonding, where mechanical interlocking effects improve bonding strength. In this paper, nano-twin copper micro-cone array (MCA) with twin boundaries (111-orientation) nearly perpendicular to the substrate prepared by pulse deposition was used to bond with SAC305 solder ball. Shearing test results show that the bonding strength between nt-Cu MCA substrate and solder ball is about 50% higher than that of twin-free Cu MCA and ten times of flat Cu. Reliability tests results show that nt-Cu MCA will generate thicker IMCs with electroplated Sn than other two substrates after reflow, which promotes bonding. In addition, nt-Cu MCA can promote the unidirectional diffusion of Cu atoms along the twinning plane, facilitating unidirectional growth of IMCs, which improves bonding reliability.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of board-level drop reliability of WLCSP solder joints with eutectic Sn-Bi, hybrid Sn-Bi/Sn-Ag-Cu and Sn-Ag-Cu solders
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The board-level drop test has emerged as an important indicator for assessing the impact reliability of electronic components. In the present work, finite element analysis (FEA) was used to simulate the strains of the eutectic Sn-Bi, hybrid Sn-Bi/Sn-Ag-Cu and Sn-Ag-Cu solder joints during board-level drop test, where Input-G method was used. The FEA showed that the maximum strain occurred at the corner solder joints of a component. The model was feasible, since the strain errors between the experimental and FEA results were lower than 5 %. Moreover, the maximum strains of WLCSP solder joints with the three kinds of solders were different, and the rank was as follows, eutectic Sn-58Bi solder joints > hybrid solder joints > SAC405 solder joints. Accordingly, SAC405 solder joints had the best board-level drop reliability. The solder joints with NSMD pads had a better board-level drop reliability than those with SMD pads, as the maximum strain shifted from the solder/Cu interface to the resin of PCB side with an angle of 45°.

articleTitle: The investigation of threshold voltage instability of p-GaN AlGaN/GaN HEMT caused by the measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this paper, the mechanism and law of threshold voltage instability in p-GaN AlGaN/GaN HEMT caused by the tested were investigated. A preprocess and rescan method was used to test the transfer characteristics, and the threshold voltage variation of p-gate schottky contact GaN HEMT was studied under different preprocessing duration, floating time and scanning time of gate pulse voltage. The results show that the threshold voltage instability of p-gate schottky contact GaN HEMT devices is complex and variable under positive voltage preprocessing, and also depends on the downward/upward direction of gate voltage during the scanning of the transfer characteristics. Among them, the charge properties, distribution and flow direction of p-GaN layer are the main reasons for the complexity of threshold voltage variation of p-gate GaN devices.

articleTitle: The low Dk, Df surface modification of silica filler in the high speed and high frequency applications
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the continuous development of electronic communication technology, the 5G communication involving GHz signal (millimeter wavelength) transmission has met the challenge in signal delay and loss due to the large Dk and Df of the dielectric materials in the communication devices. In order to meet the less signal delay and low loss requirements in 5G technologies, the copper clad laminate (CCL) for high frequency and high speed applications has attracted intense interests. As a critical components in the CCL, silica fillers could reach the filling ratio ~ 60% in mass, and it is an effective approach to improve the high speed/frequency performance of CCL via reducing the Dk and Df of the silica fillers with surface modification. Through the surface modification via grafting the low or none-polar surface coupling agents (SCAs), apart from the reduced Dk and Df, the silica fillers could also be benefitted with better dispersibility, larger adhesion energy with the resin matrix as well as the lower water absorption ratio, which could give rise to a better high speed/high frequency performance of the CCL.In this paper, three SCAs with specific molecular structure were used to perform the surface modification of silica fillers. By optimizing the content and type of SCA, silica filler with low dielectric constant and dielectric loss could be reached. The vector network analyzer was used to test the Dk and Df of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Epoxy composites (pseudo CCL), and the Dage4000 was used to test the adhesion strength of the composites on the copper film. The coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and modulus of the composites were measured by thermomechanical and dynamic thermomechanical analyzer, respectively. Moreover, the interface adhesion between the silica filler and the epoxy matrix was characterized by the cross-section view in a scanning electron microscopy. The water absorption test of the composites was measured with a high-pressure cooking method. The results showed that the molecular structure and the adding mass ratio of SCAs played the vital role in tailoring the dielectric performance of the surface modified silica fillers, and the best high speed/high frequency performance with low Dk, Df, low water absorption ratio as well as the high copper adhesion strength could be attained after the optimization of SCA molecular structure and the surface modification process.

articleTitle: In-plane Heat Transfer Enhancement of Phosphor Layer in Transmissive Laser-excited White Lighting
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The phosphors in transmissive laser-excited white lighting play the core role of wavelength conversion, but they also act as the micro heat sources in the devices. Since the phosphors are normally wrapped by polymer packaging materials with extremely low thermal conductivity, the generated heat is hard to be dissipated in time, thus resulting in a sharp temperature rise of the phosphor layer during the working process, and even lead to thermal quenching and carbonization under high power scenarios. To tackle the above problem, an in-plane heat transfer enhancement strategy by forming hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) alignment in the phosphor layer using hot-pressing method is proposed in this paper. When the filling mass fraction of hBN reaches 7.5 wt%, the in-plane thermal conductivity of the phosphor layer increases by 89% compared with that of the traditional phosphor layer without hBN, and the corresponding maximum surface temperature decreases by 68.3 °C under the driving current of 800 mA. The in-plane heat transfer enhancement strategy proposed in this paper provides a powerful means to solve the local high temperature issue in the phosphor layer of transmissive laser-excited white lighting, and may hold great promise for the further application of white lighting devices.

articleTitle: Study on the Correlation between the Ball Collapse Height and the Coplanarity Control Requirements for PBGA Reflow Soldering
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of components in the direction of fine pitch, ultra thin and ultra large dimensions, board level assembly has increasingly high requirements for the control of the coplanarity of surface mounted component pins, resulting in an increase in assembly production control difficulty. To some extent, solder paste can alleviate the soldering defects directly caused by the slight deviation in the coplanarity of component pins. Therefore, clarifying the correlation between the coplanarity differences of surface mount pins and solder joint states, and refining the technical requirements for coplanarity control in combination with the application of solder paste, are of technical reference value for coplanarity control in assembly production practices. Based on experimental research on the shape and size of PBGA bumps before and after soldering, this paper explores the correlation between bump heights and solders joint heights, providing a technical reference for the control of PBGA coplanarity.

articleTitle: Electrical Performance Enhancement Solution with FO-EB in HPC Application
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Since the Video Media has changed the way to provide the service, the cloud service become the most popular mode to provide video streaming and the high performance computing (HPC) become the most important for this kind of service. It is not only the high band width has been required, but also the high electrical performance. In terms of providing the better electrical performance for HPC, we need to consider about the packaging design. There are several ways can enhance electrical performance, and the first one would be the System on Chip (SoC) size increasing which contains more transistors providing better electrical performance, and it is the simple design solution for a SoC chip size with a package size increasing. Refer to Figure 1. Chip Size Increasing with Better Performance.Today, the package of high speed design has included the capacitor to prevent the AC noise, and the signal protection and stable the voltage is the must request for the package design. By using the Integrated Passive Device (IPD) capacitor can reduce the AC noise, and it is the best design way to enhance the AC noise for the better electrical performance. The major purpose to use FO-EB package is cost saving because the advanced node with low yield of larger silicon chip size is really expensive. So using the chiplet to connect with embedded bridge die, and the bridge die can do the communications with high electrical performance. Accompany by bridge die and HBM Integration, the FO-EB package of the high bandwidth memory also has good electrical performance as well as 2.5D package. The FO-EB package has integrated silicon bridge die which means to use the silicon bridge die to connect with spilt dies. It is not only can provide the short distance, but also become more flexable for the package design. The FO-EB can contribute the good electrical performance in HPC application and this package can also provide the good warpgae.In this paper, we like to discover the FO-EB design and evaluate the FO-EB perofrmance including the package warpage of shadow Moire, the HBM electrical preformance and also do the IPD design for the AC noisy. And, the chiplets Integration of FO-EB Package solution would be the best choice in HPC Application. Refer to Figure 2. High Performance Computing.

articleTitle: Improving Optical and Electronic Performance of Monolayer Silicon Carbide via Metal Doping
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Two-dimensional SiC materials possess exceptional chemical reactivity and thermal stability, similar to graphene and silicone. Using first-principles computations, this work examines the electrical and optical characteristics of monolayer SiC and doped monolayer SiC with Ag, Co, Fe, and Pt. In monolayer SiC, the Si and C sites have distinctive electronic and optical characteristics, and their interactions with metal dopants result in a variety of electronic structural modifications. The performance of SiC-based electronic devices in semiconductor, optoelectronic, and photovoltaic applications must be optimized in light of these discoveries. SiC monolayer band gap and work function are impacted by doping, with Agdoped SiC showing the greatest reduction in band gap and work function. Doping, especially Ag doping at the C site, which exhibits the greatest absorption coefficient in the visible light spectrum, changes the absorption and reflectance characteristics of monolayer SiC. The loss function is also changed by doping, adding further information about its optical characteristics. This study emphasizes how electrical and optical properties may be modified by doping, providing opportunities for its use in a variety of optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Effects of TiO2 Nanoparticles on Growth Behavior of IMCs between Sn/Cu joint during isothermal stage of soldering
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Although Composite solder can improve the reliability of solder joint, there has been much investigations about the influence of NPs on the interfacial reaction of solder joint, underlying mechanism is still far from being understood. Therefore, it is an interesting and valuable work to investigate the growth mechanism of intermetallic compounds (IMC) under the interaction of different NPs. In this study, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NPs was introduced at the interface of Sn/Cu solder joint. Combined with high-pressure air purging liquid solder experiment, the effect of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NPs on the growth behaviour of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> at the interface of Sn/Cu solder joint during the heat preservation stage of soldering has been studied. Form this study, it is observed that the Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grain growth can be significantly hindered with the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NPs. At the initial stage of soldering, the number of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> nucleation increases with the addition of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NPs, because it can provide heterogeneous nucleation cites for Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grains. With the ongoing heat preservation stage, the adsorption of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NPs on the surface and grain boundaries of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grains decrease the Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> crystal grain surface energy and hinder the diffusion of Cu atoms from Cu substrate to the liquid solder, which will significantly suppress the Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> crystal grain growth.

articleTitle: An Exploratory Study to Achieve Cu Bump Bonding Structures with Assistance of Bimodal-sized Cu Nanoparticles by Low-Temperature Thermocompression Bonding in Air
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Multiple chip stacking technology has provided a cost-effective solution to achieve three-dimensional (3D) heterogeneous integration, which can realize vertical high-density interconnections of chips by means of Cu-filled through silicon vias (TSVs) and Cu–Cu direct bonding. Despite some attempt to use Cu nanoparticle (NP) capped Cu pillar to facilitate Cu–Cu direct bonding without special treatment of Cu surface, there are still challenging issues to be solved. In this work, the surface of single Cu pillar arrays is coated with a patented Cu paste consisting of bimodal Cu nanoparticles (NPs), then the Cu NP paste capped Cu pillars are assembled on Cu substrate, and Cu–Cu direct bonding process is performed by low-temperature and low-pressure sintering in air without special surface treatment of the Cu pillars. The effects of different Cu pillar diameters (200, 500 and 800 μm) and varying sintering pressure (0.1, 0.5 and 1.0 MPa) on the sintering behavior of Cu–Cu direct bonding structures (joints) are studied. The results show that the Cu–Cu direct bonding joints with small diameter Cu pillar sintered under high sintering pressure show denser microstructure of the sintered Cu paste matrix and have high shear mechanical strength. After shear tests of Cu–Cu direct bonding joints, fractographic morphologies exhibit obvious plastic deformation features, indicating an excellent bonding quality of the joints, and both the proportion of plastic fracture regions on the fracture surface and the degree of plastic deformation increase with the decrease of Cu pillar diameter.

articleTitle: A resonance suppression strategy of LCL-type grid-connected inverter based on compound voltage feedforward
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-current closed-loop resonance suppression strategy based on compound feedforward to address the inherent resonance peaks and grid voltage distortions of LCL-type grid-connected inverters, which affect the grid-connected power quality. Firstly, a grid-configured PV grid-connected power generation system model is constructed based on Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) technology. Then, a dual closed-loop control architecture of grid current and capacitor current is proposed to suppress the inherent resonance spikes of LCL filter circuit. Secondly, the combined feedforward control of capacitor voltage and grid voltage is developed to mitigate the effect of grid voltage background harmonics on the grid-connected current. Finally, the performance analysis of the control strategy is performed by MATLAB platform. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method can effectively eliminate the harmonics generated by the LCL-type grid-connected inverter and ensure the stable operation of the inverter with high fundamental amplitude and low harmonic distortion rate of the grid-connected current when the grid voltage is distorted.

articleTitle: Investigation on Silver Nanowire/Resin-Induced Liquid Crystal Polymer Metallization
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the rapid advance of the fifth-generation (5G) communication technology, millimeter-wave, and terahertz frequencies have attracted great attention in advanced wireless communication. However, the traditional printed circuit board materials with the disadvantages of high dielectric constant and loss, and high absorbency have struggled to meet the demands of high-frequency communication. Liquid crystal polymer (LCP) is used as a printed circuit board material widely applied in electronic products and communication equipment due to its low dielectric constant and loss, as well as low water absorption. In this paper, silver nanowire (AgNW) /resin material was employed to induce the metalization of LCP. Initially, plasma treatment was utilized to improve the surface energy of LCP with micro-blind holes. Subsequently, a resin containing fillers was pre-coated on the LCP substrate as a primer, where the fillers could form surface void structures. Then, AgNWs were spin-coated on the primer as a conductive seed layer and embedded within the surface voids of the primer. Finally, copper was electrodeposited onto the surface of the AgNW seed layer, and the deposited copper atoms were filled into the voids of the primer under the induction of AgNWs, forming an "interlocking" structure between the copper layer and the primer, which significantly enhanced the adhesion of the metal layer. Furthermore, the microstructure and mechanical properties of copper metalized LCP were characterized. The microstructure of copper-plated micro blind holes in LCP was observed by the metallographic microscope, and the micro blind holes were filled. The surface morphology of the copper layer was assessed by scanning electron microscopy, and its surface was flat and dense. The adhesion of the copper layer was tested by the hundred-grid method and reached 4B. In comparison with traditional fabricating methods of LCP copper-clad laminations, this method with the advantages of ease of process, high efficiency, high performance, and universality for different substrates and metal layers, broadens the avenue to metalize insulating substrates.

articleTitle: Carbazole-grafted Polyimide with Enhanced Adhesion to Smooth Copper
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Polyimide (PI) has become a crucial material for interlayer dielectrics in advanced packaging thanks to its admirable comprehensive properties. PI and copper wires collaborate to construct the redistribution layer (RDL), the key part of fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP), allowing for higher I/O density. However, the weak adhesion and the mismatch of coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) between PI and copper lead to reliability issues. Herein, a novel polyimide (named GPI) containing benzimidazole ring in backbone and carbazole ring in side chain was designed and synthesized. Since the nitrogen-containing heterocycles can form coordination with copper, the prepared polyimide was supposed to have stronger interactions with copper. Besides, the grafted side groups tuned the flexibility of chains, and further improved the bond between polyimide and copper. With the grafting of carbazole ring into polyimide, the peel strength of GPI-3 increased to 0.9424N/3mm in 90° peel test, showing satisfactory adhesion. Furthermore, the fracture mode was proved to be cohesive failure by analyzing the peeled surface, indicating a strong interfacial bonding between GPI-3 and copper. Meanwhile, this new polyimide possesses outstanding mechanical (the tensile strength of GPI-3 is 176.6 MPa and the Young’s modulus is 3.97 GPa), thermal properties (T5% of GPI-3 is 464.83 °C, CTE is 22.43 ppm/K, close to the CTE of copper). Therefore, the prepared GPI has application prospects in FOWLP and provides a reference for the design of PI materials with enhanced adhesion to smooth copper.

articleTitle: A crosstalk mitigation method of DDR5 in large size LGA package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: DDR5 interface has become a standard configuration for high-performance CPUs, and its data transfer rate can reach up to 8800MT/s. But it will raise many SI issues, particularly crosstalk. For LGA package CPU products connected with a socket, it is more challenging, because the socket pin will introduce inductive crosstalk, resulting in a speed bottleneck. This paper proposes a novel solution, by designing a coplanar rake structure in the package substrate and artificially introducing mutual capacitive coupling to compensate for the influence of inductive crosstalk. Simulation results show that it can achieve ~24dB far-end crosstalk improvement while ensuring good impedance matching. This paper also provides detailed modeling and design flow regarding rake structure design. A comparative analysis with another method that uses interlayer coupling was also studied, confirming that this method achieves better results. Finally, we conducted a full-link DDR SI simulation analysis and observed a significant improvement in the eye diagram compared to the original structure. Additionally, the sample has passed the DDR5 test, which confirms the effectiveness of the crosstalk mitigation method.

articleTitle: Wafer bumping of Sn-Ag micro-bumps with high coplanarity
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The concentrations of solution components were optimized to prepare Sn-Ag micro-bumps with high coplanarity. The increasing concentration of methyl sulfonic acid (MSA) accelerated the transport rate of ions in the electroplating bath, resulting in the rapid deposition in the area of dense power lines and aggravated the tilt of micro-bumps and the edge effect. The high concentration of tin methyl sulfonic acid leaded to an accelerated deposition rate and a coarse morphology of micro-bumps. When the concentrations of the two complexing agents were high, the coplanarity of micro-bumps was poor and voids were observed. The optimized concentrations of methyl sulfonic acid, tin methyl sulfonic acid, complexing agent A and complexing agent B were 1.500, 0.500, 0.002 and 0.015 mol/L, respectively. Sn-(1.0~2.0) wt.% Ag micro-bumps of 80 μm in diameter with fine grains and high coplanarity were successfully prepared with the current densities of 4 and 8 ASD and the coplanarity of Sn-Ag micro-bumps after 1 reflow soldering was 4.16 %.

articleTitle: A Review of Program disturb of 3D NAND Flash Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As a non-volatile memory, NAND flash exists widely in mobile devices, USB, SD cards, consumer electronics, computer systems and other applications. With the development of electronic information technology, the demand for high-density memory for massive storage data is increasing. NAND flash memory is an indispensable member of the flash family because of its excellent characteristics such as large capacity, fast write and erase speed, high durability and low cost per bit. The development of NAND flash memory technology is inseparable to the advanced manufacturing technology. In the past decade, 2D NAND flash has gradually entered the physical bottleneck. In order to further reduce the unit bit storage cost without increasing the original lithography technology requirements, NAND flash memory has transitioned from planar to three-dimensional stacked structures, which further improves the storage density per unit area. However, the 3D NAND architecture has brought about an increase in programming disturb patterns compared to 2D, resulting in a wider threshold distribution and greater bit error probability. This paper demonstrates the development history, technical principles, and storage architecture of NAND flash, then the origin of program disturbs and the current mainstream solutions were highlighted.

articleTitle: FDTD Simulation of anti-reflective performance for the SiO2/PDMS transparent packaging materials
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the development of optoelectronic devices, anti-reflective coating is receiving intense attention as an important optical component, which is widely used in various optical and optoelectronic devices, e.g., LCDs, solar cells, automotive dashboards and laser devices. When light travels from one medium to another, part of the light get reflected and the residue gets transmitted and/or absorbed. Reflection occurs when there is a difference between the refractive index for the adjacent medium, where the light is reflected based on the Fresnel law. The bigger the difference between the refractive indexes, the larger the reflection. In this study, a hollow SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/PDMS composite anti-reflective structure is designed based on effective medium theory and gradient refractive index model. The antireflective properties of the composite coating on the glass substrate are investigated by the finite time domain difference (FDTD) method, where PDMS is submerged at half the height of silica to provide mechanical support and bonding, and the low refractive index hollow silica is used as the main function filler to provide the anti-reflection function. Different hollow silica samples with various particle size (50nm/100nm/ 200nm/300nm), and different wall thickness, were investigate in the FDTD simulation. The simulation results show that the hollow silica with 200nm particle size and 20nm wall thickness shows the best anti-reflective effect in this coating, and prove that the silica with a certain wall thickness can effectively enhance the transparent performance of the composite film, and the addition of PDMS can help to build a gradient refractive index and surface microroughness to form a kind of light trap, which obviously enhances the anti-reflective performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Mechanism Study of a Novel Green Chemical Mechanical Polishing Slurry for Cobalt Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Cobalt (Co) was recently proposed as the new generation of interconnection material in feature size below 10 nm and also new kind of bonding material in 3D packaging. However, the introduction of Co as interconnects also poses new challenges to chemical mechanical polishing (CMP), the most widely used planarization technology to planarize the uneven interconnect surface after electroplating because current CMP slurries are only applicable to copper. In this paper, a novel high-performance slurry for Co CMP was developed. And unlike traditional toxic slurries, the newly developed slurry contained full green ingredients including H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and a new biodegradable complexing agent methylglycinediacetic acid (MGDA). The effects of the slurry components and their concentrations on Co removal rate (RR) were clarified through polishing experiment. It is found that the introduction of MGDA could significantly increase Co RR. An optimal slurry with 5% colloidal SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, 0.2% H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and 1% MGDA at pH 8 was determined which could achieve a high RR of 322.3 nm/min. In addition, the synergistic mechanism of the slurry components on Co CMP was elucidated by virtue of electrochemical tests, UV-vis, XPS characterizations.

articleTitle: A New High-efficient Burn-in Screening Methodology Applied in Automotive Integrated Circuits Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In order to ensure the extremely high reliability of automotive products, Burn-In (BI), as a kind of essential technical means for screening early failures caused by potential defects, is usually applied in the electronic components of the automobile system before putting into use. However, the general BI screening only uses Final Test specification for failure judgment and does not establish a systematic screening standard. This paper proposes a new BI screening methodology, which considers the different degradation behaviors of Vmin/∆Vmin in high-temperature working life (HTOL) and BI test through a series of multilevel BI experiments with different stress voltages and screening times. The quantitative relationship between BI screening and Vmin/∆Vmin degradation is established, and reasonable auxiliary screening specification are determined. This strategy can effectively reduce the early failure rate (ELFR) of automotive devices and achieve mass production in the future.

articleTitle: Influence of Bonding Conditions on Low-temperature Solid-state Bonding of Cobalt Based Nanocones
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: With the miniaturization of integrated circuits, high processing temperature in mass reflow leads to more interface failure, high thermal stress and other reliability problems. Low-temperature solid-state bonding technology is potential in future 3D packaging due to its low processing temperature, high packaging density and simple post-processing. Cobalt is a promising barrier material with high hardness and electromigration resistance. Therefore, Co based nanocones prepared by electrodeposition for low-temperature solid-state bonding have a promising application. It is vital to explore the effect of bonding conditions on its bonding effect. In this paper, Co based nanocones were fabricated by electrodeposition, which were then applied in low-temperature solid-state bonding. The obtained solder joint cross-section morphology and the surface of the solder joint after shearing were characterized by SEM. The shear strength of solder joints was tested under different bonding temperatures and pressures. On the basis of above work, 190℃, 1000 gf and 150 s were determined as the appropriate low temperature bonding conditions in this experiment, and the corresponding shear strength of solder joint reached 48.99 MPa, which provides reference for the practical industrial application of low-temperature solid-state bonding of cobalt based nanocones in the future.

articleTitle: Investigation on the effect of the packaging-induced stress on the reliability of a MEMS sensor package
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Currently, with the increasing trend towards miniaturization and thinning of semiconductor devices, ensuring product reliability has become a crucial aspect in electronic packaging. This paper specifically focuses on MEMS temperature and humidity sensors and utilizes Moldex3D software for three-dimensional mold flow simulation analysis. The purpose of the analysis is to predict the distribution of potential air traps and identify the locations of weld lines. The influence of gate location and gate quantity on process defects and reliability issues is investigated using a single-factor method. The results clearly indicate that the design of the gate system has a significant impact on the reliability of sensor packaging. The simulation results for different gate locations demonstrate that placing the gate in the middle achieves a more balanced flow of epoxy resin. However, insufficient filling pressure in this configuration may result in an increase in the occurrence of air traps and weld lines. When multiple gates are used in the simulation, it is observed that the number of air traps does not decrease with an increase in the quantity of gates. Nonetheless, multiple gates promote a more balanced resin flow, although some convergence occurs, leading to the generation of numerous air traps at the convergence points. Additionally, excessive injection pressure can cause overflow and wire shifting at the window opening of the temperature and humidity sensor. In conclusion, the design of the gate system should carefully consider the structural characteristics of the product and the transfer molding process. It is evident that the gate system design plays a crucial role in the formation of air traps and weld lines. Therefore, a rational gate system design is vital to ensure both the yield and reliability of sensor products.

articleTitle: Direct soldering of 5A06 Al alloy using a Ti alloy mesh reinforced SAC305 composite solder
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 5A06 aluminum alloy exhibits excellent properties such as low density, high strength, and high electrical conductivity, which has been widely used in microwave communication components. However, the dense oxide film on the Al alloy surface hinders its direct soldering with electronic components. In this study, Ti alloy mesh reinforced SAC305 active composite solder was employed to solder 5A06 Al alloy. The effects of soldering time on the microstructure and mechanical properties of joints were investigated. Results showed that the reaction products in the solder seam changed from Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Ni, Cu)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu, and (Cu, Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> multiphase to the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Ni, Cu)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> single phase with the extension of soldering time. The diffusion of Al from the substrate into the solder seam controlled the phase transformation process of the microstructure. The increase of reaction products and the reinforcement of the Ti alloy skeletons in the solder seam improved the shear strength of joints, and the maximum strength value of 73.67 MPa was obtained for the joint soldered at 425 °C for 30 min with a pressure of 0.5 MPa.

articleTitle: Preparation and sintering performance of micro-nano hybrid copper particles for third-generation semiconductor package interconnects
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: This article presents a novel fabrication process for producing copper particles with varying ratios of micrometer and nanometer sizes, and compares them with copper particles prepared using conventional methods. The results demonstrate that the particles synthesized using the new process exhibit excellent dispersion, with minimal aggregation observed in the mixed system as the nanoscale particles increase. Furthermore, when the micro-nano hybrid ratio is 9:1, the shear strength of the hybrid copper particles prepared using the new process is 27.9 MPa, while the shear strength of the hybrid copper particles prepared using the traditional process is 15.2 MPa.

articleTitle: Study on Reflow Warpage Deformation of High Pin Density BGA Devices Affected by Moisture
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Based on the Joint Electron Device Engineering Council (JEDEC) standard, this study chooses Intel i7-7600u SR33Z CPU as experimental object, with the packaging form of Flip Chip Ball Grid Array (FCBGA), and explores the reflow warpage deformation behavior of CPU after drying (group A) and moisture absorption (group B) treatment. Finite element method is used by ANSYS Workbench to obtain the CPU warpage deformation under different conditions. During the temperature rise and fall process, the warpage value first decreases, and then increases from the highest temperature. Moisture absorption does not affect the warpage deformation trend of the chip, but affects the warpage value. The error between experiment and simulation in the warpage value of group A at the highest temperature is 10.99%, while the error of group B is 6.19%.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance of 2.5D Packaging with the Through Glass Via (TGV) Interposer
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: 2.5D interposer technology has gotten a lot of attention as a viable solution to high IO density, cost, and performance challenges. The thermal management of through glass vias (TGVs) is not currently being studied as much as through glass vias (TSV) heat dissipation and microfluidic design. In this paper, a creative work for the thermal performance of the memory chips based on 2.5D packaging is comprehensively studied to investigate the heat dissipation of the package. On the one hand, the idea of integrating TGV copper pillar arrays into the glass substrate is studied and refined. In order to explore the effect of TGV copper pillars for evaluating the ability of dissipating heat, a finite element model (FEM) based on CFD theory is built. According to the results, when there are more TGV copper arrays, the maximum junction temperature steadily decreases. On the other hand, the use of steady-state heat transfer methods for detecting the package's junction temperature and the execution of corresponding control tests. The experiments indicated that the maximum junction temperature of the package can be respectively decreased by 12% and 51% when silicon-based and diamond-based heat sink materials are selected.

articleTitle: Characterization and modeling of interface delamination in 3D stacked package with combination of experimental and CZM analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The focus of this paper is to investigate the interface delamination between the chip and substrate in 3D stacked packaging, where the interface is bonded together by a Die Adhesive Film (DAF) layer. Firstly, we conducted an analysis of the interface based on fracture mechanics theory. Considering that Mode I and Mode II are typically the primary failure modes in engineering applications, this paper primarily discusses these two fracture modes. We designed single cantilever beam (SCB) and four-point bending (4PB) tests based on the two failure modes and calculated the critical energy release rates, GIC and GIIC, through computation of the test results. Additionally, utilizing the fracture analysis module in Ansys finite element analysis software, we obtained the parameters required to establish the cohesive zone model (CZM) through simulation, which characterizes the initiation and propagation of cracks. We also discussed the influence of the critical shear strength on the critical load in the simulation analysis. Finally, we found that the obtained CZM not only characterizes the occurrence and propagation of cracks at the interface between the chip and substrate in 3D stacked packaging but can also be applied to study similar interfaces in other types of packaging. Overall, the research findings of this paper have significant reference value for analyzing interface delamination between chips and substrates.

articleTitle: Study on the failure mechanism and characteristics of electrochemical migration of electronic package structures in humid environment
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: As the trend of miniaturization in the microelectronics industry continues, the adverse effects of electrochemical migration on devices are becoming increasingly significant, particularly in humid environments. These issues, manifested as short-circuits caused by dendritic growth, have a profound impact on device performance, efficiency, and lifespan. Hence, the necessity to study the dynamic characteristics of ion electrochemical migration and dendrite formation in electronic devices is paramount to enhance device reliability and longevity. To this end, this study introduces an innovative approach that considers the role of electrolyte melting in dendritic growth under low-temperature environments, a factor overlooked in previous models. This study employs a two-dimensional multiphysical finite element method model, grounded in Fick's mass diffusion theory, Nernst-Planck theory, Nernst-Einstein equation, and the electric-heat-concentration effect, to investigate the failure mechanism and dynamic characteristics of ion electrochemical migration in electronic packaging devices. Furthermore, the level set mathematical method is utilized to track changes in dendrite morphology, establishing an equation for the interface motion between the electrolyte and dendrite. This innovative approach accounts for the boundary movement of the model, induced by dendrite formation via ion diffusion electrodeposition at the cathode side. Our results reveal that upon application of bias voltage, an electrochemical reaction triggers ion diffusion from the anode to the cathode, creating a notable ion concentration gradient. This leads to the gradual formation and extension of dendrites towards the anode. When dendrites reach the anode, the device risks short-circuit failure. Our model predicts a device failure time of approximately 1769s, offering a valuable tool for enhancing the reliability and lifespan of microelectronic devices under various environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Investigation of Moisture Influence on Structure and Thermal Conductivity of Epoxy Resin by Molecular Dynamics Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Epoxy resin is commonly used in electronic package. However, it has a very low thermal conductivity of 0.1-0.5 W/m/K and absorbs moisture, which usually causes several defects such as cracks, delamination and warpage. In this paper, the effect of moisture on the structure and thermal conductivity of epoxy resins was investigated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative elementary volume (RVE) of polymer was constructed, with diglycidyl ether of bisphenol A (DGEBA) and polyetheramine (D230 or D400) as epoxy resin and curing agent, respectively. Then the moisture invasion model was constructed by adding water molecules to the RVE. The crosslinking degree from 0% to 98% and moisture concentration from 0wt.% to 10wt.% were studied. The hydrogen bonds length of about 2.75 Å was obtained by calculating the radial distribution function (RDF). Both increased crosslinking degree and moisture concentration could increase the hydrogen bonds between water molecules and polymer networks. Next, the volume was analyzed. The total volume shrank by 4.4vol.% when the crosslinking degree was changed from 0% to 98.96%. The water molecules in free volume would squeeze the polymer networks, and the mechanism varies with the moisture concentration. The thermal conductivity of D230 cured DGEBA increased from 0.11 to 0.17 W/m/K as the crosslinking degree increased from 0% to 98.96%. Based on the model with crosslinking degree of 75%, the thermal conductivity of D230 cured DGEBA increased from 0.16 to 0.19 W/m/K as the moisture concentration increased from 0.1wt.% to 10wt.%. The thermal conductivity of long chains is higher than that of short chains. Through the above analysis, a theoretical basis was provided for the hygrothermal reliability study of electronic packaging.

articleTitle: Study on grinding of Cu-Ta interface based on molecular dynamic
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, the molecular dynamics method is used to simulate the process of particle scratching, so as to reveal the microscopic mechanism of scratch formation, and characterize the stress distribution and microscopic interface changes of the Cu/Ta interface during the particle grinding process. Due to different etching processes, different types of distributions will be formed at the Cu/Ta interface between the interconnection metal and the barrier layer. Further, the stress-strain distribution of different types of Cu/Ta interfaces in the mechanical grinding process is studied to reveal the possible failure modes of Cu/Ta interfaces with different distributions. The results of this simulation will be beneficial to reduce the interface damage of the multilayer copper interconnection structure caused by particle scratches during the CMP process, reduce the defects caused by the CMP process, and improve the reliability of the multilayer copper interconnection structure.

articleTitle: Study on the Curing Kinetics and Curing Behavior of Epoxy Conductive Adhesive Materials for Electronic Packaging and Their Impact on Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Epoxy resin-based conductive adhesive materials (ECAs) are widely used in electronic packaging due to their good electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and curing adhesion properties. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) is a common method for studying the curing behavior of epoxy resin materials, but there are few reports on its application to the study of the curing behavior of high filled ECAs. Considering that the curing behavior of ECAs will significantly affect their electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and adhesion behavior, this study selected a domestically produced ECAs product, and used the equivalent transformation method to solve the kinetic parameters of the ECAs obtained through the Kissinger-Akahira-Sunose non-model method. Then a kinetic model was established. The study found that the curing behavior of the ECAs has low temperature dependence, and the curing reaction of the epoxy based conductive adhesive was greatly affected by the curing time. That is, even though the curing temperature is relatively low (still above the reaction temperature of the curing agent), a high curing degree can be obtained through the prolongation of the isothermal curing duration. Meanwhile, the kinetic model of J427 has stage differences at high temperatures. Sample J427 exhibits a typical latent curing agent curing process. It has the characteristics of autocatalytic curing in the early stage of the reaction. In the late stage of the reaction, it turns to n-level model control. Moreover, the increase in curing temperature will accelerate the autocatalytic process, and the curing reaction quickly turns to n-level model control. After raising its curing temperature, its resistivity increased from 75.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> cm·Ω drops to 37.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> cm·Ω. The dynamic dielectric analysis curing (DEA) was used to characterize the change in ion concentration during the curing process of the composite material. It was found that the variation of ion concentration is consistent with the change of thermal enthalpy. The DEA data verify that the fluidity of the composite solution decreased after increasing the curing temperature, and the uniform distribution of silver powder can be quickly fixed. It also indicates that when curing at higher temperatures, the cross-linking network formed by the resin may be more uniform and complete, which is contributed to the overlapping of conductive fillers that cause enhanced electrical conductivity. Based on these results, the curing process of the ECAs can be easily improved to enhance its conductivity. This study provides some reference for improving the performance of ECAs used in electronic packaging.

articleTitle: Effect of additives on uniformity of copper coatings at electroless plating interconnection
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In packaging interconnection technology, the high process temperature poses a challenge due to the resulting thermal mismatch at the interconnect interface, leading to deformations and cracks. Therefore, there is a need to address the issue of reducing the process temperature in interconnection technology. Therefore, a low temperature electroless interconnection method has been proposed. Electroless interconnection involves depositing a layer on the activated metal surface through a REDOX reaction. This technique has the advantages of high bonding strength, high alignment and coplanar tolerance. Common interconnecting metals include Ni, Cu, etc. However, during the interconnection process, the limited supply of copper ions and the delayed discharge of hydrogen in the reaction can result in voids at the interconnect interface. In this study, the effects of PEG and 2,2’-bipyridine content on the coating uniformity of copper bumps in the sodium hypophosphite system were investigated, along with the synergistic effect of these two additives. A microfluidic channel device was used for the electroless copper interconnection, and then the cross section of the copper interconnection was observed. The results showed that PEG can increase the coatings deposition rate. Although the simultaneous use of both additives led to a decreased growth rate of the coatings, it resulted in coatings with a bright and uniform surface. While improvements in plating solution flow mode could eliminate the voids caused by the reduction of the interconnect gap, but the porosity resulting from hydrogen could not be reduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of Metallization Effects of Pressure-Assisted Cu Nanoparticle Sintering on DBC by Experiment and Nanoscale Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Substrate metallization is a crucial factor affecting the mechanical properties of sintered nanoparticles in microelectronics applications, as it is essential for ensuring good adhesion between the substrate and the sintered material. In this study, we investigated the influence of metallization on pressure-assisted nanocopper sintering and analyzed the related mechanism of interaction using experiments and molecular dynamics simulation. In the first session, we bonded dummy dies on various substrates, including bare Cu, and substrates with Ag or Au metallization by nanocopper pressure-assisted sintering. The mechanical properties of the bonding layers were estimated using shear strength and SEM image analysis of fracture and cross-section morphologies under different sintering conditions. We found that the group of Cu-bare Cu have better bonding strength as the sintering temperature or assisted pressure is not high enough. However, as more energy input to the bonding layer, such as higher temperature or larger sintering pressure, the mechanical performance showed a significant increase. In the second session, a sintering model, which contained a single nanoparticle and substrate, was built to illustrate the effects of metallization from the perspective of solid-state wetting. The contact angle was estimated using a creative method, and the crystallization structure evolutions under different sintering conditions were analyzed. We found that the lattice boundary generated as the Cu nanoparticle coalescence with Ag or Au substrate, which may decrease the bonding strength. However, for Ag and Au metallization, limited interface diffusion can be observed at the neck region, where a few numbers of substrate atoms transmitted toward Cu nanoparticle, and the contact area was larger than that of bare Cu substrate. Finally, a simple uniaxial stretching simulation was conducted to prove the results of sintering simulation. This study provides valuable insights into the effects of metallization on pressure-assisted nanocopper sintering, which can contribute to the optimization of mechanical properties of sintered nanoparticles in microelectronics applications.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of different microfluidic cooling technologies for high performance chips
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thermal management has emerged as a crucial factor restricting device functionality and lifetime. The enhancement of IC fabrication technology has led to a dramatical increase in chip performance and power density. The heat flux of hotspots in the future will approach 1000W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This article provides a theoretical analysis that compares the distribution of thermal resistance among three cooling schemes: remote cooling, near-die cooling, and die-embedded cooling. The results indicate that selecting TIM1 with high thermal conductivity can significantly diminish the thermal resistance of remote cooling and near-die cooling in the case of uniform heating and single hotspot heating. This study provides a valuable reference for engineers in selecting microfluidic cooling schemes for high performance chips.

articleTitle: A Novel IGZO-TFT Device With High Dielectric Constant Sandwich Structure Gate Dielectric Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: Thin film transistors (TFTs), as an important component of flat panel display technology, will also become the top priority at this stage. The emergence of amorphous indium gallium zinc oxide thin-film transistors (IGZO-TFTs) quickly became the new favorite of the display technology market. This article mainly reports the sandwich structure of high dielectric constant (High-K) materials wrapped by low dielectric constant (Low-K) materials according to the combination of High-K materials and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Low-K materials are used to reduce interlayer capacitance, thereby reducing RC signal delay and increasing device operating frequency. High-K is used to increase the thickness of the gate layer and suppress tunneling leakage current, and this sandwich structure can better balance TFT performance.The SILVACO simulation software was used to simulate the structure and device output characteristics and transfer characteristics, and the IGZO thin-film transistors at this stage were improved by combining the relevant process flow of IGZO, and the photoelectric characteristics of IGZO thin-film transistors based on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/hfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate layer were understood. In order to ensure that the interlayer capacitance of the gate dielectric layer is stable and unchanged, but also to ensure sufficient physical thickness, the selection of a gate dielectric material with a High-K can effectively suppress the device tunneling effect caused by too small a physical thickness.hfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has good thermal stability on Si substrate, high dielectric constant, large band gap, and large band compensation with Si. The technical introduction of High-K materials is mainly aimed at solving the technical problem of greatly reducing the efficiency of electronic dielectric migration caused by the thinning of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film dielectric gate layer materials. The High-k medium can also be reduced to the threshold voltage of the devices. Based on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/hfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate dielectric layer, IGZO-TFT is expected to improve device stability while improving device performance.

articleTitle: Implantable flexible temperature sensor for in-operando sensing of Lithium-ion batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: The safety concerns play a key role in promoting the application of lithium-ion battery (LIB) in electric vehicles, renewable energy storage and consumer electronics. Thermal runaway is one of the primary risks of LIB. Operando monitoring LIB’s temperature is expected to provide essential signal for the early warning of thermal runaway. In this study, a flexible temperature sensor with robustness to the internal environment of LIB cell is presented. By using ultra-violent laser micromachining and transfer-printing technique, the corrosion-resistant Molybdenum thin film is patterned and integrated with polyimide (PI) film to serve as the temperature sensitive layer. The encapsulation of Molybdenum layer enabled by the hot-pressing process further improves the reliability of the sensor in LIB cell. The stability of the sensor in the LIB cell is experimentally verified with the neglectable change of resistance when the sensor is immersed in the electrolyte for 48 hours. The ability of the proposed sensor to monitor the internal temperature of LIB is also demonstrated by implanting the sensor in a pouch cell and measuring the temperature in the charge-discharge cycles.

articleTitle: Hansen solubility parameter optimization of surface modified silica filler in electronic packaging materials
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In the advanced electronic packaging, underfill is used to release the thermal mechanical stress on solder joints caused by the different coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) between the chips and organic substrates. The underfill is usually a composite composed of epoxy resin matrix and the silica filler. Epoxy resin has excellent characteristics such as high toughness, corrosion resistance, and high insulation. With the addition of silica filler, the underfill materials are expected to have low CTE, high modulus, low humidity absorption and the high strength. The surface modification is to improve the adhesion strength of silica filler in the epoxy matrix, which is critical for attaining the high-performance underfill. However, the quantitatively analysis of the surface modification via the Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) theory was rarely reported.The Hansen solubility parameter is composed of the dispersive solubility parameter δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>, the polar solubility parameter δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, and the hydrogen bond solubility parameter δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>. In this paper, the inverse gas chromatography (iGC) instrument was used to test the dispersion, polar, and the hydrogen bond HSP components of the surface modified silica fillers and the epoxy resin. The HSP difference was calculated via the parameter δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> through the formula ${\delta _t} = {}{({\delta _d}^2 + {\delta _p}^2 + {\delta _h}^2)^{1/2}}$. The bad or good dispersibility of the filler in the resin matrix is based on whether the δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> value of the filler is matchable to the epoxy resin’s. The HSP was tested at three different temperatures (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>< Tg, T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>= Tg, T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>> Tg). The Tg(glass transition temperature) of epoxy resin was tested using a dynamic thermal mechanical analyzer (DMA). Through HSP analysis, the surface modification of silica was optimized, and the silica filled underfill showed the optimum performance with low viscosity, high fluidity as well as the improved thermal mechanical properties due to the better adhesion between the filler and the epoxy resin.

articleTitle: A case study of intermetallic evolutions in a solder joint under electromigration using a novel experiment-simulation combined approach
publicationTitle: 2023 24th International Conference on Electronic Packaging Technology (ICEPT)
abstract: In this work, by using high-resolution X-ray computed tomography (μ-XCT), we revealed the 3D Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> evolutions in a typical single-crystal solder joint during electromigration (EM), and the finite element modeling (FEM) based on a reconstructed real solder joint model was performed to understand the microstructure evolution mechanism. Simulation results show that the migration direction of Cu atoms is nearly parallel with the c-axis of βSn. Primary Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> rods within the region of higher Cu diffusion flux exhibit more obvious growth with higher volume change.
